congo/lakes-rivers.description: The second largest river on earth by volume, and the whole eastern border of the country.
congo/lakes-rivers.alt: the vast brown Congo river with forest on the far bank

congo/local-life.caption: The Bars of Poto-Poto
congo/local-life.description: Rumba, grilled fish and beer, from the afternoon until it is not the afternoon.
congo/local-life.alt: an open-air bar with music in the Poto-Poto quarter, Congo

congo/luxury.caption: Small and Excellent
congo/luxury.description: Odzala's camps are among the best-run in Central Africa, and there are three of them.
congo/luxury.alt: a raised forest camp deck overlooking a bai in Odzala, Congo

congo/mountains.caption: Mount Berongou
congo/mountains.description: 903 metres in the Mayombe, and the highest ground in a country of forest and plateau.
congo/mountains.alt: the forested Mayombe hills under low cloud, Congo

congo/nature.caption: The Congo Basin
congo/nature.description: Two thirds of the country is rainforest, and much of it has never had a road in it.
congo/nature.alt: unbroken Congo Basin rainforest canopy from the air

congo/outdoor.caption: Tracking and Pirogue
congo/outdoor.description: Long days on foot through swamp forest, and quiet mornings on the Lekoli.
congo/outdoor.alt: trackers wading a shallow forest stream, Congo

congo/photography.caption: Green and Steam
congo/photography.description: A bai at first light, when the mist is still on it and the elephants are already there.
congo/photography.alt: mist over a forest bai at dawn with elephants in it, Congo

congo/safari.caption: Bai Watching
congo/safari.description: Forest buffalo, bongo, sitatunga and elephant come to the clearings, and you sit and wait.
congo/safari.alt: forest buffalo and elephants at a bai in Odzala, Congo

congo/traditional-people.caption: Kongo, Teke, Mbochi and the Aka
congo/traditional-people.description: Bantu peoples along the river, and Aka forest hunter-gatherers in the north.
congo/traditional-people.alt: an Aka forest camp with leaf shelters in the north, Congo

congo/waterfalls.caption: The Loufoulakari
congo/waterfalls.description: Falls on the Congo above Brazzaville, where the river drops through rock.
congo/waterfalls.alt: the Loufoulakari falls dropping through rock into the Congo

congo/why-visit.caption: Why Congo
congo/why-visit.description: The best western lowland gorilla tracking anywhere, in forest that has never been cut.
congo/why-visit.alt: a gorilla family moving through dense green forest, Congo

congo/wildlife.caption: Western Lowland Gorillas
congo/wildlife.description: Smaller, redder and harder to see than mountain gorillas, and tracked through swamp forest.
congo/wildlife.alt: a silverback western lowland gorilla in dense green forest, Congo

cote-divoire/adventure.caption: Surf, Hike, Paddle
cote-divoire/adventure.description: Surf at Assinie, hiking the western hills, and pirogues through the lagoon.
cote-divoire/adventure.alt: surfers in the water off Assinie, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/architecture.caption: Lagoon Colonial
cote-divoire/architecture.description: The wooden trading houses of Grand-Bassam, and Abidjan's tropical modernism.
cote-divoire/architecture.alt: a colonial trading house on the Grand-Bassam waterfront, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/beaches.caption: Assinie and Grand-Béréby
cote-divoire/beaches.description: Assinie's sandbar east of Abidjan, and the quieter Atlantic beaches to the west.
cote-divoire/beaches.alt: palms and surf on the beach at Assinie, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/cities.caption: Abidjan
cote-divoire/cities.description: The Plateau's towers, the Ébrié lagoon, and a nightlife the region measures itself against.
cote-divoire/cities.alt: the towers of the Plateau district in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/crafts.caption: Weaving and Carving
cote-divoire/crafts.description: Baoulé strip cloth, Korhogo painted cloth, and Dan masks carved for use rather than sale.
cote-divoire/crafts.alt: Korhogo cloth painted with mud pigment, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/culture.caption: Sixty Peoples
cote-divoire/culture.description: Akan, Krou, Mandé and Gur — around sixty peoples inside one border.
cote-divoire/culture.alt: a Baoulé mask dance in central Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/eco-tourism.caption: Taï and the Chimpanzees
cote-divoire/eco-tourism.description: Forty years of chimpanzee research at Taï, run with the villages around the park.
cote-divoire/eco-tourism.alt: a researcher on a forest trail at Taï, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/family-community.caption: Beach and Lagoon
cote-divoire/family-community.description: Assinie's sandbar has ocean on one side and calm lagoon on the other, which suits children.
cote-divoire/family-community.alt: children swimming on the lagoon side at Assinie, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/festivals.caption: Abissa and the Masks
cote-divoire/festivals.description: Abissa at Grand-Bassam in November, and the mask festivals of the western hills.
cote-divoire/festivals.alt: masked dancers at the Abissa festival in Grand-Bassam, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/food.caption: Attiéké and Kedjenou
cote-divoire/food.description: Attiéké with grilled fish, and kedjenou slow-cooked in a sealed pot.
cote-divoire/food.alt: attiéké and grilled fish served at a maquis, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/forests.caption: Taï Rainforest
cote-divoire/forests.description: One of the last blocks of primary rainforest in West Africa, and chimpanzees that use tools.
cote-divoire/forests.alt: primary rainforest interior at Taï, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/heritage.caption: Yamoussoukro
cote-divoire/heritage.description: A basilica larger than Saint Peter's, built in the founder's home village.
cote-divoire/heritage.alt: the basilica of Our Lady of Peace at Yamoussoukro, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/hero.caption: Lagoons, Forest and the Atlantic
cote-divoire/hero.description: A lagoon city, one of West Africa's last rainforests, and five hundred kilometres of Atlantic.
cote-divoire/hero.alt: the Abidjan skyline across the Ébrié lagoon, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/hidden-gems.caption: Man
cote-divoire/hidden-gems.description: The western hills, with waterfalls, mask villages and a mountain nobody climbs.
cote-divoire/hidden-gems.alt: the hills and forest around the town of Man, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/historic-sites.caption: Grand-Bassam
cote-divoire/historic-sites.description: The first colonial capital, on a sandbar between lagoon and ocean, and now a world site.
cote-divoire/historic-sites.alt: the colonial quarter of Grand-Bassam, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/lakes-rivers.caption: The Ébrié and the Bandama
cote-divoire/lakes-rivers.description: The lagoon system behind the coast, and the Bandama running the length of the country.
cote-divoire/lakes-rivers.alt: pirogues on the Ébrié lagoon at dusk, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/local-life.caption: Maquis at Night
cote-divoire/local-life.description: The open-air maquis — grill, music and a plastic chair — is the country's real institution.
cote-divoire/local-life.alt: a busy open-air maquis at night in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/luxury.caption: Assinie and Abidjan
cote-divoire/luxury.description: Lagoon villas at Assinie, and Abidjan hotels that serve the whole region's business.
cote-divoire/luxury.alt: a lagoon-side villa terrace at Assinie, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/mountains.caption: Mount Nimba
cote-divoire/mountains.description: The Nimba range on the Guinea and Liberia border, at 1,752 metres, with its own species.
cote-divoire/mountains.alt: the grassy summit ridge of Mount Nimba, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/nature.caption: Forest to Savanna
cote-divoire/nature.description: Rainforest in the south-west, a lagoon coast, and savanna running north to Mali.
cote-divoire/nature.alt: the Ébrié lagoon fringed with palms, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/outdoor.caption: Surf and Hike
cote-divoire/outdoor.description: Assinie's breaks, and the liana bridges and falls in the hills around Man.
cote-divoire/outdoor.alt: a liana bridge strung across a river near Man, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/photography.caption: Lagoon Light
cote-divoire/photography.description: Pirogues on flat water at either end of the day, and a skyline behind them.
cote-divoire/photography.alt: pirogues silhouetted on the lagoon at sunset, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/safari.caption: Comoé
cote-divoire/safari.description: One of the largest protected areas in West Africa, with elephant, buffalo and hippo.
cote-divoire/safari.alt: open savanna and gallery forest at Comoé, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/traditional-people.caption: Baoulé, Senufo and Dan
cote-divoire/traditional-people.description: Baoulé weaving, Senufo sculpture, and Dan masks from the western hills.
cote-divoire/traditional-people.alt: Senufo carved figures on a workshop bench, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/waterfalls.caption: Man and the Waterfalls
cote-divoire/waterfalls.description: The falls around Man in the western hills, and the liana bridges strung above them.
cote-divoire/waterfalls.alt: a waterfall in the hills around Man, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/why-visit.caption: The Engine of the Region
cote-divoire/why-visit.description: The largest economy in francophone West Africa, and the easiest of them to travel.
cote-divoire/why-visit.alt: a coastal highway running west out of Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/wildlife.caption: Taï and Comoé
cote-divoire/wildlife.description: Pygmy hippo and chimpanzees at Taï, and Comoé's savanna in the north-east.
cote-divoire/wildlife.alt: dense rainforest canopy at Taï national park, Côte d'Ivoire

djibouti/adventure.caption: Snorkelling and Rift Walking
djibouti/adventure.description: Swimming with whale sharks in the morning, walking a spreading rift in the afternoon.
djibouti/adventure.alt: snorkellers entering the water beside a boat in the Gulf of Tadjoura, Djibouti

djibouti/architecture.caption: Arcades and Coral
djibouti/architecture.description: Colonial arcades in the European quarter, and coral-block houses in the old town.
djibouti/architecture.alt: colonnaded arcades in the European quarter of Djibouti City

djibouti/beaches.caption: The Gulf of Tadjoura
djibouti/beaches.description: Beaches at Sable Blanc and the Sept Freres islands, and reef straight off the sand.
djibouti/beaches.alt: the white sand and clear water of Sable Blanc beach, Djibouti

djibouti/cities.caption: Djibouti City
djibouti/cities.description: A French-Arab port city with a covered market, and the Horn's busiest container terminal.
djibouti/cities.alt: the covered central market of Djibouti City

djibouti/crafts.caption: Weaving and Woodwork
djibouti/crafts.description: Afar mats and milk vessels, and carved wooden headrests that double as stools.
djibouti/crafts.alt: a carved wooden Afar headrest and woven milk vessel, Djibouti

djibouti/culture.caption: Afar and Somali
djibouti/culture.description: Two peoples, French and Arabic official, and a port that half the Horn depends on.
djibouti/culture.alt: a busy street market in Djibouti City

djibouti/eco-tourism.caption: Salt, Cut by Hand
djibouti/eco-tourism.description: Slabs still cut from Assal and loaded onto camels, on a route a thousand years old.
djibouti/eco-tourism.alt: salt slabs being cut by hand from the crust at Lake Assal, Djibouti

djibouti/family-community.caption: Sable Blanc
djibouti/family-community.description: Shallow, warm, empty white sand an hour and a half from the capital.
djibouti/family-community.alt: a family on the empty white sand of Sable Blanc beach, Djibouti

djibouti/festivals.caption: Independence Day
djibouti/festivals.description: 27 June, and the Afar and Somali dance traditions that come out for it.
djibouti/festivals.alt: dancers in traditional dress at a Djibouti independence celebration

djibouti/food.caption: Skoudehkaris and Yemeni Fish
djibouti/food.description: Spiced rice with lamb, and whole fish baked in a Yemeni clay oven on the coast.
djibouti/food.alt: a whole fish baked Yemeni-style served on flatbread, Djibouti

djibouti/forests.caption: The Last Juniper
djibouti/forests.description: The Day forest is a relic of a wetter Horn, and it is shrinking.
djibouti/forests.alt: old juniper trees in the mist of the Day forest, Djibouti

djibouti/heritage.caption: The Lake Abbe Landscape
djibouti/heritage.description: Not listed, but the chimneys are on every list of the strangest places on earth.
djibouti/heritage.alt: steaming limestone chimneys at dawn on Lake Abbe, Djibouti

djibouti/hero.caption: Lake Assal
djibouti/hero.description: A salt lake 155 metres below sea level, ringed white, the lowest point in Africa.
djibouti/hero.alt: the white salt shore and turquoise water of Lake Assal, Djibouti

djibouti/hidden-gems.caption: The Sept Freres
djibouti/hidden-gems.description: Seven islands at the mouth of the gulf, with the best reef in the country round them.
djibouti/hidden-gems.alt: a small boat off the Sept Freres islands with reef below, Djibouti

djibouti/historic-sites.caption: Ottoman Tadjoura
djibouti/historic-sites.description: One of the oldest towns on this coast, with seven mosques and a sultan's history.
djibouti/historic-sites.alt: the white mosques and low houses of Tadjoura on the gulf, Djibouti

djibouti/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Abbe
djibouti/lakes-rivers.description: Limestone chimneys steaming on a dry lake bed, on the Ethiopian border.
djibouti/lakes-rivers.alt: limestone chimneys venting steam on the flats of Lake Abbe, Djibouti

djibouti/local-life.caption: Khat at Four
djibouti/local-life.description: The flight lands from Ethiopia and the city stops for it. Every afternoon.
djibouti/local-life.alt: men sorting bundles of khat at a street stall in the afternoon, Djibouti

djibouti/luxury.caption: Small and Getting Better
djibouti/luxury.description: A few good hotels in the capital and a diving lodge on the gulf.
djibouti/luxury.alt: a terrace overlooking the Gulf of Tadjoura at sunset, Djibouti

djibouti/mountains.caption: The Goda and Mabla
djibouti/mountains.description: Mousa Ali at 2,028 metres, and juniper forest above the coastal plain at Day.
djibouti/mountains.alt: the Goda mountains rising above the arid coastal plain, Djibouti

djibouti/nature.caption: The Afar Triangle
djibouti/nature.description: Three tectonic plates pulling apart, and you can stand in the crack.
djibouti/nature.alt: the black basalt fissures of the Ardoukoba rift, Djibouti

djibouti/outdoor.caption: The Ardoukoba
djibouti/outdoor.description: A volcano that erupted in 1978 as the rift opened. The lava field is still bare.
djibouti/outdoor.alt: the bare black lava field of the Ardoukoba volcano, Djibouti

djibouti/photography.caption: White on Turquoise
djibouti/photography.description: Lake Assal at midday, when the salt is blinding and the water is the wrong blue.
djibouti/photography.alt: the salt crust and impossibly blue water of Lake Assal at midday, Djibouti

djibouti/safari.caption: Day Forest
djibouti/safari.description: Beira antelope and the last Djibouti francolin in the juniper of the Goda mountains.
djibouti/safari.alt: juniper forest on the slopes of the Goda mountains at Day, Djibouti

djibouti/traditional-people.caption: The Afar
djibouti/traditional-people.description: Salt caravans still come up from Assal, and the Afar have worked that trade for centuries.
djibouti/traditional-people.alt: an Afar man leading camels loaded with salt slabs from Lake Assal, Djibouti

djibouti/waterfalls.caption: Nothing Permanent
djibouti/waterfalls.description: There are no rivers here. The water is in wadis, springs and the sea.
djibouti/waterfalls.alt: a palm-shaded spring pool in a Djiboutian wadi

djibouti/why-visit.caption: Why Djibouti
djibouti/why-visit.description: Whale sharks, the lowest point in Africa and a rift valley opening, in a country you cross in a day.
djibouti/why-visit.alt: a swimmer in clear water beside a whale shark, Djibouti

djibouti/wildlife.caption: Whale Sharks
djibouti/wildlife.description: They come into the Gulf of Tadjoura from November, in numbers, close to shore.
djibouti/wildlife.alt: a whale shark swimming near the surface in the Gulf of Tadjoura, Djibouti

dr-congo/adventure.caption: Nyiragongo Overnight
dr-congo/adventure.description: Six hours up, a night in a hut on the rim, and the lava lake below you all of it.
dr-congo/adventure.alt: climbers on the crater rim of Nyiragongo above the lava lake, DR Congo

dr-congo/architecture.caption: Belgian Colonial and Cite
dr-congo/architecture.description: Art deco Kinshasa from the 1930s, and the cite quarters that grew around it.
dr-congo/architecture.alt: a 1930s art deco building in central Kinshasa, DR Congo

dr-congo/beaches.caption: Muanda, and the Lakes
dr-congo/beaches.description: Forty kilometres of Atlantic at the river mouth, and beaches on Kivu and Tanganyika.
dr-congo/beaches.alt: the shore and clear water of Lake Kivu at Goma, DR Congo

dr-congo/cities.caption: Kinshasa and Lubumbashi
dr-congo/cities.description: One of the largest cities in Africa, facing Brazzaville, and the mining capital in the south.
dr-congo/cities.alt: the skyline and traffic of Kinshasa on the Congo river, DR Congo

dr-congo/crafts.caption: Masks, Raffia and Copper
dr-congo/crafts.description: Kuba raffia cloth, Pende and Songye masks, and Katangese copper crosses.
dr-congo/crafts.alt: a length of Kuba raffia cloth with geometric appliqué, DR Congo

dr-congo/culture.caption: Two Hundred and Fifty Peoples
dr-congo/culture.description: Four national languages, and a music that has set the terms for the whole continent.
dr-congo/culture.alt: a street market crowd in Kinshasa, DR Congo

dr-congo/eco-tourism.caption: Virunga's Rangers
dr-congo/eco-tourism.description: Over two hundred rangers have died protecting this park. It is the oldest in Africa.
dr-congo/eco-tourism.alt: Virunga rangers on patrol at the forest edge, DR Congo

dr-congo/family-community.caption: Not for Families
dr-congo/family-community.description: The east requires current advice and the distances are enormous. This is careful travel.
dr-congo/family-community.alt: a school class in a village in eastern DR Congo

dr-congo/festivals.caption: Rumba and Ndombolo
dr-congo/festivals.description: Franco, Papa Wemba, Koffi Olomide — Kinshasa has exported dance music for seventy years.
dr-congo/festivals.alt: a rumba band on stage in a Kinshasa nightclub, DR Congo

dr-congo/food.caption: Fufu, Pondu and Liboke
dr-congo/food.description: Cassava fufu, pondu cassava leaf, and fish steamed in leaves over a fire.
dr-congo/food.alt: fish steamed in banana leaf served with fufu, DR Congo

dr-congo/forests.caption: The Ituri and the Salonga
dr-congo/forests.description: Salonga is the largest tropical rainforest reserve in Africa, and mostly unentered.
dr-congo/forests.alt: the closed canopy of the Salonga rainforest, DR Congo

dr-congo/heritage.caption: Five World Heritage Sites
dr-congo/heritage.description: Virunga, Garamba, Kahuzi-Biega, Salonga and the Okapi Reserve — all five on the danger list.

dr-congo/hero.caption: Nyiragongo
dr-congo/hero.description: The world's largest lava lake, in a crater you climb to in a day and sleep beside.
dr-congo/hero.alt: the glowing lava lake in the crater of Nyiragongo at night, DR Congo

dr-congo/hidden-gems.caption: Lake Kivu
dr-congo/hidden-gems.description: Volcanic islands, terraced hills and calm water, between Goma and Bukavu.
dr-congo/hidden-gems.alt: Idjwi island and calm water on Lake Kivu, DR Congo

dr-congo/historic-sites.caption: Kisangani and the River Stations
dr-congo/historic-sites.description: Stanley's route up the river, and the Wagenia fishing structures that predate all of it.
dr-congo/historic-sites.alt: the wooden Wagenia fishing tripods over rapids at Kisangani, DR Congo

dr-congo/lakes-rivers.caption: The Congo River
dr-congo/lakes-rivers.description: Four and a half thousand kilometres, and the deepest river in the world at 220 metres.
dr-congo/lakes-rivers.alt: the immense width of the Congo river seen from the bank, DR Congo

dr-congo/local-life.caption: SAPE
dr-congo/local-life.description: The Society of Ambianceurs and Elegant People — dressing as a discipline and an argument.
dr-congo/local-life.alt: a sapeur in a bright tailored suit on a Kinshasa street, DR Congo

dr-congo/luxury.caption: Virunga's Lodges
dr-congo/luxury.description: Mikeno and Tchegera, run by the park itself, and the money goes back into it.
dr-congo/luxury.alt: a lodge terrace looking towards the Virunga volcanoes, DR Congo

dr-congo/mountains.caption: The Rwenzori
dr-congo/mountains.description: 5,109 metres at Margherita, glaciated, on the equator, and the Mountains of the Moon.
dr-congo/mountains.alt: glaciers and rock on the summit ridge of the Rwenzori, DR Congo

dr-congo/nature.caption: The Albertine Rift
dr-congo/nature.description: Glaciers on the Rwenzori, volcanoes in the Virungas, and the deepest forest in Africa between them.
dr-congo/nature.alt: the glaciated peaks of the Rwenzori above forest, DR Congo

dr-congo/outdoor.caption: Volcano and Gorilla
dr-congo/outdoor.description: Nyiragongo, then gorillas in Virunga's lowlands, from the same base at Goma.
dr-congo/outdoor.alt: trekkers on a forested slope in Virunga National Park, DR Congo

dr-congo/photography.caption: Lava at Night
dr-congo/photography.description: The Nyiragongo crater after dark, when the lake is the only light there is.
dr-congo/photography.alt: the orange glow of Nyiragongo's lava lake at night, DR Congo

dr-congo/safari.caption: Garamba and Upemba
dr-congo/safari.description: Northern savanna with elephant and Kordofan giraffe, being brought back after decades of loss.
dr-congo/safari.alt: elephants on open savanna in Garamba National Park, DR Congo

dr-congo/traditional-people.caption: The Mbuti
dr-congo/traditional-people.description: Forest hunter-gatherers of the Ituri, with a relationship to that forest going back millennia.
dr-congo/traditional-people.alt: Mbuti hunters with nets in the Ituri forest, DR Congo

dr-congo/waterfalls.caption: Boyoma and Lofoi
dr-congo/waterfalls.description: The seven cataracts at Kisangani, and Lofoi with a single drop of 340 metres.
dr-congo/waterfalls.alt: the Wagenia fishing structures at the Boyoma falls, Kisangani, DR Congo

dr-congo/why-visit.caption: Why DR Congo
dr-congo/why-visit.description: A lava lake, mountain gorillas, glaciers on the equator, and the okapi.
dr-congo/why-visit.alt: a climber silhouetted on the rim above Nyiragongo's lava lake, DR Congo

dr-congo/wildlife.caption: Mountain Gorillas and Okapi
dr-congo/wildlife.description: Virunga's gorillas in the east, and the okapi in the Ituri forest, which lives nowhere else.
dr-congo/wildlife.alt: an okapi in dense Ituri forest undergrowth, DR Congo

egypt/adventure.caption: Desert Crossings
egypt/adventure.description: Diving the Red Sea, walking the Sinai with Bedouin guides, and crossing the sand sea by vehicle.
egypt/adventure.alt: a vehicle crossing dunes in the Great Sand Sea, Egypt

egypt/architecture.caption: Mamluk Cairo
egypt/architecture.description: The mosques, sabils and madrasas of the medieval city, largely still standing.
egypt/architecture.alt: the carved stone facade of a Mamluk mosque in Cairo, Egypt

egypt/beaches.caption: The Red Sea
egypt/beaches.description: Some of the clearest reef diving on earth, an hour's flight from the pyramids.
egypt/beaches.alt: coral reef and clear water on the Red Sea coast, Egypt

egypt/cities.caption: Cairo and Alexandria
egypt/cities.description: Twenty million people on the Nile, and a Mediterranean city that remembers being Greek.
egypt/cities.alt: the Alexandria corniche curving along the Mediterranean, Egypt

egypt/crafts.caption: Papyrus, Glass and Cotton
egypt/crafts.description: Hand-blown glass in Cairo, Egyptian cotton, and papyrus made the way it always was.
egypt/crafts.alt: a glassblower working in a Cairo workshop, Egypt

egypt/culture.caption: Coptic, Islamic, Pharaonic
egypt/culture.description: Three layers still in daily use, sometimes in the same street in old Cairo.
egypt/culture.alt: the minarets and rooftops of Islamic Cairo, Egypt

egypt/eco-tourism.caption: Reef and Oasis
egypt/eco-tourism.description: Reef protection on the Red Sea, and oasis agriculture that has managed water for millennia.
egypt/eco-tourism.alt: a marine reserve buoy over Red Sea reef, Egypt

egypt/family-community.caption: Straightforward with Children
egypt/family-community.description: Short internal flights, boats instead of buses, and a story at every stop.
egypt/family-community.alt: a family boarding a Nile cruise boat at Luxor, Egypt

egypt/festivals.caption: Moulids and Ramadan
egypt/festivals.description: The moulid processions, and Cairo at iftar when the whole city eats at once.
egypt/festivals.alt: lanterns strung across a Cairo street for Ramadan, Egypt

egypt/food.caption: Ful, Koshary and Bread
egypt/food.description: Breakfast is ful and bread; lunch is koshary; both are older than most cuisines.
egypt/food.alt: koshary being served at a Cairo street kitchen, Egypt

egypt/forests.caption: The Fayoum
egypt/forests.description: Not forest — the Fayoum's palm and olive, and the acacia of Wadi el-Rayan.
egypt/forests.alt: palm groves in the Fayoum oasis, Egypt

egypt/heritage.caption: Karnak, Luxor, Abu Simbel
egypt/heritage.description: Karnak took two thousand years to build; Abu Simbel was moved sixty metres to save it.
egypt/heritage.alt: the hypostyle hall columns at Karnak, Egypt

egypt/hero.caption: Five Thousand Years
egypt/hero.description: The Nile made the country and the country has been recording it ever since.
egypt/hero.alt: the Giza pyramids at first light across the desert, Egypt

egypt/hidden-gems.caption: Siwa
egypt/hidden-gems.description: Eight hundred kilometres west, a Berber-speaking oasis with its own language and salt lakes.
egypt/hidden-gems.alt: salt pools and palms at the Siwa oasis, Egypt

egypt/historic-sites.caption: The Valley of the Kings
egypt/historic-sites.description: Sixty-odd tombs cut into a single dry valley, most of them painted floor to ceiling.
egypt/historic-sites.alt: painted tomb walls in the Valley of the Kings, Egypt

egypt/lakes-rivers.caption: The Nile Itself
egypt/lakes-rivers.description: Feluccas under sail at Aswan, and a river that has been the country's main road for millennia.
egypt/lakes-rivers.alt: a felucca under sail on the Nile at Aswan, Egypt

egypt/local-life.caption: The Corniche at Dusk
egypt/local-life.description: Families out along the river, tea on the pavement, and the traffic finally slowing.
egypt/local-life.alt: families walking the Nile corniche in Cairo at dusk, Egypt

egypt/luxury.caption: Dahabiyas and Desert Camps
egypt/luxury.description: Small sailing dahabiyas instead of the big cruisers, and camps in the White Desert.
egypt/luxury.alt: a dahabiya sailing boat moored on the Nile at sunset, Egypt

reasons: looks like 71% of a slot already filled here

egypt/mountains.caption: Sinai
egypt/mountains.description: Mount Sinai and Saint Catherine's, and granite peaks over two thousand metres above the Red Sea.
egypt/mountains.alt: the granite peaks of the Sinai above Saint Catherine's, Egypt

egypt/nature.caption: The Nile and the Desert
egypt/nature.description: A green ribbon a few kilometres wide, and sand for a thousand kilometres either side of it.
egypt/nature.alt: the green Nile valley meeting desert on both banks, Egypt

egypt/outdoor.caption: Dive, Sail, Ride
egypt/outdoor.description: Reef diving at Marsa Alam, feluccas at Aswan, and camels in the Western Desert.
egypt/outdoor.alt: divers entering the water on the Red Sea coast, Egypt

egypt/photography.caption: The Light at Six
egypt/photography.description: Desert light at either end of the day is the whole reason to be up early here.
egypt/photography.alt: dawn light on the temple columns at Luxor, Egypt

egypt/safari.caption: The Western Desert
egypt/safari.description: Not big game — desert fox, gazelle and the silence of the Great Sand Sea.
egypt/safari.alt: the White Desert chalk formations at dusk, Egypt

egypt/traditional-people.caption: Nubians and Bedouin
egypt/traditional-people.description: Nubian villages above Aswan and Bedouin communities in the Sinai and the Western Desert.
egypt/traditional-people.alt: a brightly painted Nubian village on the Nile at Aswan, Egypt

egypt/waterfalls.caption: The First Cataract
egypt/waterfalls.description: The Nile's cataracts at Aswan — rapids rather than falls, and the reason the boats stopped here.
egypt/waterfalls.alt: the Nile running over granite at the Aswan cataract, Egypt

egypt/why-visit.caption: The Oldest Journey
egypt/why-visit.description: People have been travelling to see this country for two and a half thousand years.
egypt/why-visit.alt: the Sphinx and the Great Pyramid at sunrise, Egypt

egypt/wildlife.caption: Birds of the Delta
egypt/wildlife.description: Two million migrating birds use the Delta and the Red Sea coast as a flyway each year.
egypt/wildlife.alt: flamingos and waders on a Nile delta wetland, Egypt

equatorial-guinea/adventure.caption: Trekking the Caldera
equatorial-guinea/adventure.description: Three days on foot from Ureca to the Gran Caldera, through forest, with no road at all.
equatorial-guinea/adventure.alt: walkers on a forest trail towards the Gran Caldera, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/architecture.caption: Spanish Colonial
equatorial-guinea/architecture.description: Malabo's cathedral, customs house and shuttered merchant houses, in a Gulf of Guinea version of Spain.
equatorial-guinea/architecture.alt: shuttered Spanish colonial houses on a Malabo street, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/beaches.caption: Black Sand and Turtles
equatorial-guinea/beaches.description: Four species nest on Bioko's southern beaches — leatherback, green, olive ridley and hawksbill.
equatorial-guinea/beaches.alt: a leatherback turtle on black sand at Bioko's southern beach, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/cities.caption: Malabo and Bata
equatorial-guinea/cities.description: The island capital in a drowned crater, and the mainland's largest city on the coast.
equatorial-guinea/cities.alt: the harbour and colonial waterfront of Malabo, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/crafts.caption: Carving and Basketry
equatorial-guinea/crafts.description: Fang carving on the mainland, and Bubi basketry and wooden bells on Bioko.
equatorial-guinea/crafts.alt: a carved wooden Fang figure and woven basket, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/culture.caption: Spanish, Fang and Bubi
equatorial-guinea/culture.description: The only Spanish-speaking country in Africa, with Fang on the mainland and Bubi on Bioko.
equatorial-guinea/culture.alt: a street of Spanish colonial buildings in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/eco-tourism.caption: The Bioko Biodiversity Programme
equatorial-guinea/eco-tourism.description: University-run monitoring of the turtle beaches and primates since 1998.
equatorial-guinea/eco-tourism.alt: researchers recording a turtle nest on Bioko's black sand, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/family-community.caption: Beach and Forest
equatorial-guinea/family-community.description: Arena Blanca on Bioko is calm and shaded, and Pico Basile is drivable.
equatorial-guinea/family-community.alt: a family on the sheltered sand at Arena Blanca on Bioko, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/festivals.caption: The Abira
equatorial-guinea/festivals.description: A Bubi purification ceremony, danced with drums and rattles.
equatorial-guinea/festivals.alt: Bubi dancers with rattles at a village ceremony on Bioko, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/food.caption: Pepe Soup and Malamba
equatorial-guinea/food.description: Pepper soup with fish, and malamba — palm wine sweetened with cane.
equatorial-guinea/food.alt: a bowl of fish pepper soup with plantain, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/forests.caption: Cloud Forest and Lowland
equatorial-guinea/forests.description: Cloud forest above a thousand metres on Bioko, and Congo Basin forest on the mainland.
equatorial-guinea/forests.alt: moss-covered cloud forest on the slopes of Pico Basile, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/heritage.caption: Nothing Listed Yet
equatorial-guinea/heritage.description: No World Heritage sites, and a colonial architecture that has been very little studied.
equatorial-guinea/heritage.alt: a decaying Spanish colonial verandah building in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/hero.caption: Bioko
equatorial-guinea/hero.description: A volcanic island in the Gulf of Guinea, forested to the summit and ringed by black sand.
equatorial-guinea/hero.alt: the forested volcanic cone of Bioko rising above the sea, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/hidden-gems.caption: Annobon
equatorial-guinea/hidden-gems.description: A volcanic island six hundred kilometres out, with a crater lake and four flights a month.
equatorial-guinea/hidden-gems.alt: the crater lake and volcanic slopes of Annobon island, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/historic-sites.caption: Colonial Malabo
equatorial-guinea/historic-sites.description: Santa Isabel was a Spanish port town, and the cathedral and customs house still stand.
equatorial-guinea/historic-sites.alt: the twin-spired Spanish colonial cathedral in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/lakes-rivers.caption: The Wele and the Muni
equatorial-guinea/lakes-rivers.description: The Wele runs across the mainland; the Muni estuary marks the Gabonese border.
equatorial-guinea/lakes-rivers.alt: the Muni estuary with mangrove at low tide, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/local-life.caption: Sunday After Mass
equatorial-guinea/local-life.description: Malabo empties into the streets after the cathedral, and stays there.
equatorial-guinea/local-life.alt: people gathered outside the cathedral in Malabo after mass, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/luxury.caption: Business Hotels, Mostly
equatorial-guinea/luxury.description: Malabo and Bata have good hotels built for the oil industry, and Bioko's south has none.
equatorial-guinea/luxury.alt: a hotel terrace overlooking the sea at Malabo, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/mountains.caption: Pico Basile
equatorial-guinea/mountains.description: 3,011 metres, the island's volcano, with a road most of the way up it.
equatorial-guinea/mountains.alt: the summit and cloud forest of Pico Basile on Bioko, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/nature.caption: The Gran Caldera
equatorial-guinea/nature.description: A collapsed volcanic crater in the south of Bioko, forested, and reached only on foot.
equatorial-guinea/nature.alt: the forested rim of the Gran Caldera de Luba on Bioko, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/outdoor.caption: Walking Bioko
equatorial-guinea/outdoor.description: The south of the island has no roads. Everything there is done on foot.
equatorial-guinea/outdoor.alt: a forest path descending towards the sea on southern Bioko, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/photography.caption: Black Sand and Green
equatorial-guinea/photography.description: Ureca in the rain, which is most of the time — the wettest place in Africa.
equatorial-guinea/photography.alt: rain over black sand and rainforest at Ureca on Bioko, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/safari.caption: Monte Alen
equatorial-guinea/safari.description: Mainland forest with gorilla, chimpanzee and forest elephant, walked rather than driven.
equatorial-guinea/safari.alt: rainforest and a river valley in Monte Alen National Park, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/traditional-people.caption: The Bubi
equatorial-guinea/traditional-people.description: Bioko's first people, with their own language, and a history separate from the mainland.
equatorial-guinea/traditional-people.alt: a Bubi village on a forested slope on Bioko, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/waterfalls.caption: Iladyi
equatorial-guinea/waterfalls.description: A 250-metre cascade off the caldera rim in the south of Bioko.
equatorial-guinea/waterfalls.alt: the Iladyi cascade falling from the caldera rim on Bioko, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/why-visit.caption: Why Equatorial Guinea
equatorial-guinea/why-visit.description: Four turtle species on one black beach, under a forest with drills in it.
equatorial-guinea/why-visit.alt: turtle tracks on black sand below rainforest at dawn, Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea/wildlife.caption: Seven Primates on One Island
equatorial-guinea/wildlife.description: Bioko has seven species, several of them found on that island and nowhere else.
equatorial-guinea/wildlife.alt: a Bioko drill monkey in the island's cloud forest, Equatorial Guinea

eritrea/adventure.caption: The Massawa Road
eritrea/adventure.description: Down the escarpment by road or by the restored steam railway, two thousand metres in a morning.
eritrea/adventure.alt: a steam locomotive on the mountain railway above Asmara, Eritrea

eritrea/architecture.caption: Futurist and Coral
eritrea/architecture.description: Fiat Tagliero's concrete wings in Asmara, and Massawa's buildings cut from the reef itself.
eritrea/architecture.alt: the arched coral-stone facade of an old Massawa merchant house, Eritrea

eritrea/beaches.caption: The Dahlak Archipelago
eritrea/beaches.description: Three hundred and fifty islands, four of them inhabited, and reefs almost nobody has dived.
eritrea/beaches.alt: an empty white beach and turquoise water on a Dahlak island, Eritrea

eritrea/cities.caption: Asmara and Massawa
eritrea/cities.description: One a cool art-deco plateau town, the other a coral-block Ottoman port on the sea.
eritrea/cities.alt: coral-block Ottoman buildings on the waterfront at Massawa, Eritrea

eritrea/crafts.caption: Filigree and Basketry
eritrea/crafts.description: Silver filigree from Asmara's goldsmiths, and coiled straw baskets from the highlands.
eritrea/crafts.alt: silver filigree jewellery on a workbench in Asmara, Eritrea

eritrea/culture.caption: Nine Groups, Two Faiths
eritrea/culture.description: Tigrinya, Tigre, Afar, Bilen and five more, roughly half Christian and half Muslim.
eritrea/culture.alt: people at an outdoor cafe on Harnet Avenue in Asmara, Eritrea

eritrea/eco-tourism.caption: Terraces That Hold the Soil
eritrea/eco-tourism.description: Highland terracing built by hand over centuries, and still the reason the topsoil is there.
eritrea/eco-tourism.alt: hand-built stone terraces on a steep Eritrean hillside

eritrea/family-community.caption: The Safest Capital Around
eritrea/family-community.description: Asmara is small, walkable and calm, and children are everywhere in it after dark.
eritrea/family-community.alt: children playing in a public square in Asmara at dusk, Eritrea

eritrea/festivals.caption: Meskel and Eid
eritrea/festivals.description: Meskel bonfires in September, and Eid in Massawa, in the same country and often the same street.
eritrea/festivals.alt: a Meskel bonfire and crowd in an Eritrean town square

eritrea/food.caption: Injera, Zigni and Macchiato
eritrea/food.description: Eritrean stews on injera, and an Italian coffee culture that never left.
eritrea/food.alt: a macchiato in a glass on a marble cafe table in Asmara, Eritrea

eritrea/forests.caption: The Green Belt
eritrea/forests.description: Semenawi Bahri, a strip of cloud forest on the escarpment an hour from the capital.
eritrea/forests.alt: mist in the cloud forest of Semenawi Bahri on the escarpment, Eritrea

eritrea/heritage.caption: Asmara, Listed Whole
eritrea/heritage.description: The first modernist city anywhere to be inscribed as a World Heritage site, in 2017.
eritrea/heritage.alt: the modernist facade of the Cinema Impero on Harnet Avenue, Eritrea

eritrea/hero.caption: Asmara on the Plateau
eritrea/hero.description: A whole modernist city at 2,300 metres, built in the 1930s and barely altered since.
eritrea/hero.alt: the Fiat Tagliero building in Asmara with its concrete wings, Eritrea

eritrea/hidden-gems.caption: The Tank Graveyard
eritrea/hidden-gems.description: A hillside outside Asmara stacked with the wreckage of thirty years of war.
eritrea/hidden-gems.alt: rusting tanks and vehicles stacked at the Asmara tank graveyard, Eritrea

eritrea/historic-sites.caption: Adulis and Qohaito
eritrea/historic-sites.description: A Red Sea port that traded with Rome, and a highland city on the escarpment above it.
eritrea/historic-sites.alt: stone columns standing at the ruins of Qohaito on the escarpment, Eritrea

eritrea/lakes-rivers.caption: The Red Sea Coast
eritrea/lakes-rivers.description: No permanent rivers to speak of — the water here is the sea, and it is very warm.
eritrea/lakes-rivers.alt: clear shallow water over coral off the Eritrean Red Sea coast

eritrea/local-life.caption: The Passeggiata
eritrea/local-life.description: Asmara walks Harnet Avenue in the evening. Everybody does, and nobody hurries.
eritrea/local-life.alt: people walking Harnet Avenue in Asmara in the evening, Eritrea

eritrea/luxury.caption: Modest, and Improving
eritrea/luxury.description: A handful of restored Italian-era hotels in Asmara. Nothing on the coast yet.
eritrea/luxury.alt: a restored Italian-era hotel interior in Asmara, Eritrea

eritrea/mountains.caption: Emba Soira
eritrea/mountains.description: 3,018 metres in the southern highlands, with terraced farming right up the sides.
eritrea/mountains.alt: terraced fields climbing the slopes of the Eritrean highlands

eritrea/nature.caption: The Escarpment
eritrea/nature.description: The plateau drops two thousand metres to the Red Sea in about ninety kilometres.
eritrea/nature.alt: the Eritrean highland escarpment dropping away in terraces

eritrea/outdoor.caption: Cycling
eritrea/outdoor.description: Eritrea is a cycling country — the Tour of Eritrea climbs the escarpment.
eritrea/outdoor.alt: a peloton of cyclists climbing a mountain road in Eritrea

eritrea/photography.caption: Deco in Low Light
eritrea/photography.description: Asmara's facades in the late afternoon, when the plaster goes warm and the streets empty.
eritrea/photography.alt: late sun on a curved art deco facade in Asmara, Eritrea

eritrea/safari.caption: Not the Business Here
eritrea/safari.description: There is no safari circuit. The wildlife is coastal and marine, and it is worth the swap.
eritrea/safari.alt: a green turtle over seagrass in the Dahlak archipelago, Eritrea

eritrea/traditional-people.caption: The Afar and the Rashaida
eritrea/traditional-people.description: The Afar on the southern coast, and the Rashaida who came across from Arabia in the 1840s.
eritrea/traditional-people.alt: a Rashaida woman in an embroidered veil near the Red Sea coast, Eritrea

eritrea/waterfalls.caption: Seasonal Only
eritrea/waterfalls.description: The highland streams run in the summer rains and are dry the rest of the year.
eritrea/waterfalls.alt: a dry rocky streambed in the Eritrean highlands

eritrea/why-visit.caption: Why Eritrea
eritrea/why-visit.description: Nowhere else has a whole intact modernist city, a steam railway and an unfished reef.
eritrea/why-visit.alt: a vintage Fiat parked outside an art deco cinema in Asmara, Eritrea

eritrea/wildlife.caption: Danakil and Dahlak
eritrea/wildlife.description: Wild ass in the Danakil, dugong and turtle in the Dahlak archipelago.
eritrea/wildlife.alt: an African wild ass on stony ground in the Danakil, Eritrea

eswatini/adventure.caption: Canopy Tours and Whitewater
eswatini/adventure.description: The Malolotja canopy tour, and rafting the Great Usutu when it is up.
eswatini/adventure.alt: a canopy tour zipline crossing a forested gorge at Malolotja, Eswatini

eswatini/architecture.caption: Beehive and Colonial
eswatini/architecture.description: Woven beehive huts in the homesteads, and small colonial towns in stone.
eswatini/architecture.alt: a woven grass beehive hut at a Swazi homestead, Eswatini

eswatini/beaches.caption: Landlocked, and Close
eswatini/beaches.description: No coast — but the Mozambican beaches at Ponta do Ouro are two hours from Manzini.
eswatini/beaches.alt: a river pool with rocks and trees in the Malolotja valley, Eswatini

eswatini/cities.caption: Mbabane and Manzini
eswatini/cities.description: A small capital in the hills, and the commercial town and market in the middle.
eswatini/cities.alt: the market and streets of Manzini, Eswatini

eswatini/crafts.caption: Candles, Glass and Weaving
eswatini/crafts.description: Swazi Candles, Ngwenya Glass from recycled bottles, and Gone Rural's grass weaving.
eswatini/crafts.alt: hand-made Swazi candles in bright patterns on a bench, Eswatini

eswatini/culture.caption: A Living Monarchy
eswatini/culture.description: Umhlanga and Incwala are not performances — they are the constitutional year.
eswatini/culture.alt: young women in ceremonial dress at the Umhlanga reed dance, Eswatini

eswatini/eco-tourism.caption: Big Game Parks
eswatini/eco-tourism.description: One family has run Hlane, Mkhaya and Mlilwane since 1960, and brought the rhino back.
eswatini/eco-tourism.alt: a ranger tracking rhino on foot at Mkhaya, Eswatini

eswatini/family-community.caption: Easy and Safe
eswatini/family-community.description: Short distances, malaria-light, rhino you can walk to, and a very gentle pace.
eswatini/family-community.alt: a family on a guided walk towards rhino at Mkhaya, Eswatini

eswatini/festivals.caption: Umhlanga and Incwala
eswatini/festivals.description: The reed dance in late August, and Incwala, the kingship ceremony, in December and January.
eswatini/festivals.alt: the reed dance procession at Umhlanga, Eswatini

eswatini/food.caption: Sidvudvu and Emasi
eswatini/food.description: Pumpkin with maize, emasi soured milk, and braai everywhere.
eswatini/food.alt: a bowl of sidvudvu pumpkin porridge, Eswatini

eswatini/forests.caption: Malolotja and Ngwempisi
eswatini/forests.description: Montane grassland and Afromontane forest in the northwest, with proper wilderness walking.
eswatini/forests.alt: montane grassland and forest patches at Malolotja, Eswatini

eswatini/heritage.caption: Nothing Listed, Everything Living
eswatini/heritage.description: No World Heritage sites, and a ceremonial calendar that has never been interrupted.
eswatini/heritage.alt: a Swazi homestead of beehive huts within a reed fence, Eswatini

eswatini/hero.caption: Small, and Full
eswatini/hero.description: Two hours across, and it holds rhino, rainforest gorges, granite domes and a living monarchy.
eswatini/hero.alt: the Ezulwini valley with granite hills on both sides, Eswatini

eswatini/hidden-gems.caption: Ngwempisi Gorge
eswatini/hidden-gems.description: A wilderness gorge in the west with hanging bridges and no vehicles.
eswatini/hidden-gems.alt: a suspension bridge over the forested Ngwempisi gorge, Eswatini

eswatini/historic-sites.caption: Ngwenya Mine
eswatini/historic-sites.description: Iron ore mined here forty-three thousand years ago — among the oldest mines on earth.
eswatini/historic-sites.alt: the red iron ore workings of the ancient Ngwenya mine, Eswatini

eswatini/lakes-rivers.caption: The Great Usutu
eswatini/lakes-rivers.description: The country's main river, running east through a gorge to the Mozambican border.
eswatini/lakes-rivers.alt: the Great Usutu river running through a rocky gorge, Eswatini

eswatini/local-life.caption: The Manzini Market
eswatini/local-life.description: Produce downstairs, handicraft upstairs, and the whole country passing through on a Thursday.
eswatini/local-life.alt: the handicraft section of Manzini market, Eswatini

eswatini/luxury.caption: Small and Good
eswatini/luxury.description: Mkhaya's Stone Camp, and lodges through the Ezulwini valley.
eswatini/luxury.alt: an open-sided stone and thatch camp in the bush at Mkhaya, Eswatini

eswatini/mountains.caption: Sibebe
eswatini/mountains.description: The largest exposed granite dome in the world after Uluru, and you walk up it.
eswatini/mountains.alt: the bare granite dome of Sibebe rock above the valley, Eswatini

eswatini/outdoor.caption: Walking Malolotja
eswatini/outdoor.description: Multi-day wilderness trails across grassland and gorge, with huts and no roads.
eswatini/outdoor.alt: a walking trail crossing open grassland at Malolotja, Eswatini

eswatini/photography.caption: Granite and Grass
eswatini/photography.description: Sibebe in the late afternoon, when the whole dome goes orange.
eswatini/photography.alt: late sun on the granite dome of Sibebe, Eswatini

eswatini/safari.caption: Hlane and Mkhaya
eswatini/safari.description: Lion and elephant at Hlane, rhino and sable at Mkhaya, both small and both excellent.
eswatini/safari.alt: lions resting under a tree in Hlane Royal National Park, Eswatini

eswatini/traditional-people.caption: The Swazi
eswatini/traditional-people.description: One nation, one language, and a set of ceremonies that everyone in the country takes part in.
eswatini/traditional-people.alt: Swazi men in traditional dress at a royal ceremony, Eswatini

eswatini/waterfalls.caption: Mantenga
eswatini/waterfalls.description: A wide falls beside the cultural village in the Ezulwini valley.
eswatini/waterfalls.alt: the Mantenga falls spreading over rock in the Ezulwini valley, Eswatini

eswatini/why-visit.caption: Why Eswatini
eswatini/why-visit.description: Rhino on foot, a monarchy in ceremony, and a country you can cross before lunch.
eswatini/why-visit.alt: a rhino at close range from a walking trail at Mkhaya, Eswatini

eswatini/wildlife.caption: Rhino at Mkhaya
eswatini/wildlife.description: Black and white rhino, tracked on foot, in a private reserve that has never lost one to poaching.
eswatini/wildlife.alt: a black rhino among thorn scrub at Mkhaya, Eswatini

ethiopia/adventure.caption: Trekking Country
ethiopia/adventure.description: Multi-day treks in the Simiens and Bale, and the Danakil at a hundred metres below sea level.
ethiopia/adventure.alt: the sulphur springs of the Danakil depression, Ethiopia

ethiopia/architecture.caption: Round Houses and Rock Churches
ethiopia/architecture.description: The tukul, and the rock architecture of Tigray cut into cliff faces you have to climb.
ethiopia/architecture.alt: a Tigray rock church high in a cliff face, Ethiopia

ethiopia/beaches.caption: No Coast, and No Loss
ethiopia/beaches.description: Landlocked since 1993 — the water here is the Rift lakes and the crater lakes of Bishoftu.
ethiopia/beaches.alt: a crater lake at Bishoftu in the early morning, Ethiopia

ethiopia/cities.caption: Addis Ababa
ethiopia/cities.description: Founded 1886, at 2,355 metres, and the diplomatic capital of the continent.
ethiopia/cities.alt: the Merkato district of Addis Ababa from above, Ethiopia

ethiopia/crafts.caption: Weaving and Silver
ethiopia/crafts.description: Handwoven shemma cotton, and Coptic crosses in silver, each region with its own shape.
ethiopia/crafts.alt: a silversmith working an Ethiopian cross

ethiopia/culture.caption: Its Own Everything
ethiopia/culture.description: Its own alphabet, its own calendar with thirteen months, and its own church since the fourth century.
ethiopia/culture.alt: priests in white robes outside a rock-hewn church, Ethiopia

ethiopia/eco-tourism.caption: Community Conservation
ethiopia/eco-tourism.description: Guides and scouts drawn from the villages inside the parks, which is why the wolves are still there.
ethiopia/eco-tourism.alt: a park scout looking out over the Bale plateau, Ethiopia

ethiopia/family-community.caption: Highland Travel
ethiopia/family-community.description: Cool highland air, short flights between the historic sites, and no malaria at altitude.
ethiopia/family-community.alt: a family walking a highland track in northern Ethiopia

ethiopia/festivals.caption: Timkat and Meskel
ethiopia/festivals.description: Timkat in January at Gondar, and Meskel bonfires across the country in September.
ethiopia/festivals.alt: the Timkat procession with white-robed crowds at Gondar, Ethiopia

ethiopia/food.caption: Injera and Doro Wat
ethiopia/food.description: Sourdough injera under everything, and fasting food that has made vegans of visitors.
ethiopia/food.alt: injera with several wats served on a shared platter, Ethiopia

ethiopia/forests.caption: Harenna and the Church Forests
ethiopia/forests.description: Harenna's cloud forest in Bale, and the church forests that are the last woodland of the north.
ethiopia/forests.alt: a round church surrounded by its own remnant forest, Ethiopia

ethiopia/heritage.caption: Aksum and Gondar
ethiopia/heritage.description: The Aksumite stelae, and the seventeenth-century castles of Gondar built by Fasilides.
ethiopia/heritage.alt: the stone castles of Fasil Ghebbi at Gondar, Ethiopia

ethiopia/hero.caption: The Roof of Africa
ethiopia/hero.description: Eighty per cent of Africa's land above three thousand metres is in this one country.
ethiopia/hero.alt: the Simien mountains escarpment dropping away into cloud, Ethiopia

ethiopia/hidden-gems.caption: Tigray
ethiopia/hidden-gems.description: Rock churches in cliff faces reached by hand and foot, with almost nobody else there.
ethiopia/hidden-gems.alt: the climb to a rock church in the Gheralta mountains, Ethiopia

ethiopia/historic-sites.caption: Lalibela
ethiopia/historic-sites.description: Eleven churches cut down into solid rock in the twelfth century, still in use every day.
ethiopia/historic-sites.alt: the rock-hewn church of Bete Giyorgis at Lalibela, Ethiopia

ethiopia/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Tana
ethiopia/lakes-rivers.description: The source of the Blue Nile, with monasteries on its islands still in use.
ethiopia/lakes-rivers.alt: an island monastery on Lake Tana seen from the water, Ethiopia

ethiopia/local-life.caption: Coffee, Properly
ethiopia/local-life.description: Coffee was found here, and it is still roasted, ground and poured in front of you.
ethiopia/local-life.alt: a coffee ceremony with roasting pan and jebena, Ethiopia

ethiopia/luxury.caption: Lodges on the Escarpment
ethiopia/luxury.description: Limalimo and Bale Mountain Lodge — small, sited well, and built by people who stayed.
ethiopia/luxury.alt: a lodge terrace on the edge of the Simien escarpment, Ethiopia

ethiopia/mountains.caption: The Simiens
ethiopia/mountains.description: Ras Dashen is 4,550 metres; the trek to it runs along the escarpment for days.
ethiopia/mountains.alt: trekkers on the ridge trail in the Simien mountains, Ethiopia

ethiopia/nature.caption: Escarpment and Rift
ethiopia/nature.description: The Rift Valley cuts the whole country in half, with highlands either side of it.
ethiopia/nature.alt: the Ethiopian Rift valley lakes seen from the escarpment

ethiopia/outdoor.caption: Trek and Climb
ethiopia/outdoor.description: The Simien traverse, Bale's plateau, and the Tigray churches that need a rope.
ethiopia/outdoor.alt: a climber on the approach to a Tigray cliff church, Ethiopia

ethiopia/photography.caption: Faces and Escarpments
ethiopia/photography.description: The light at four thousand metres, and portraiture that has to be asked for properly.
ethiopia/photography.alt: cloud below the escarpment edge in the Simien mountains, Ethiopia

ethiopia/safari.caption: Bale and the Ethiopian Wolf
ethiopia/safari.description: The Bale mountains hold the last five hundred Ethiopian wolves, on the Sanetti plateau.
ethiopia/safari.alt: an Ethiopian wolf on the Sanetti plateau in Bale

ethiopia/traditional-people.caption: Omo Valley
ethiopia/traditional-people.description: The lower Omo holds sixteen peoples in one valley, and the visits should be arranged carefully.
ethiopia/traditional-people.alt: a village of the lower Omo valley at the end of the day, Ethiopia

ethiopia/waterfalls.caption: The Blue Nile Falls
ethiopia/waterfalls.description: Tis Issat — the water that smokes — where the Blue Nile leaves Lake Tana.
ethiopia/waterfalls.alt: the Blue Nile falls in full flow at Tis Issat, Ethiopia

ethiopia/why-visit.caption: Nothing Else Like It
ethiopia/why-visit.description: No colonial period, its own script, its own calendar, and its own year that starts in September.
ethiopia/why-visit.alt: a priest holding a processional cross at a rock church, Ethiopia

ethiopia/wildlife.caption: Gelada and Walia Ibex
ethiopia/wildlife.description: The gelada lives nowhere else on earth, and grazes the Simien escarpment in troops of hundreds.
ethiopia/wildlife.alt: a troop of gelada baboons grazing on the Simien escarpment, Ethiopia

gabon/adventure.caption: Whales, Turtles and Surf
gabon/adventure.description: Humpbacks from July, leatherbacks from November, and a beach nobody else is on.
gabon/adventure.alt: a humpback whale breaching off the Gabonese coast

gabon/architecture.caption: Colonial and Contemporary
gabon/architecture.description: French colonial along the coast, and Libreville's newer buildings behind it.
gabon/architecture.alt: a colonial-era building beside modern blocks in Libreville, Gabon

gabon/beaches.caption: Eight Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
gabon/beaches.description: Empty beaches with forest behind them, humpbacks offshore, and leatherbacks nesting.
gabon/beaches.alt: an empty Atlantic beach backed by rainforest in Gabon

gabon/cities.caption: Libreville and Port-Gentil
gabon/cities.description: An Atlantic capital, and an oil town on an island at the Ogooue delta.
gabon/cities.alt: the seafront boulevard and buildings of Libreville, Gabon

gabon/crafts.caption: Masks and Ngombi Harps
gabon/crafts.description: Punu white-faced masks, Fang reliquary figures, and the carved harps of Bwiti.
gabon/crafts.alt: a carved Fang reliquary guardian figure, Gabon

gabon/culture.caption: Bwiti
gabon/culture.description: An initiatory religion built around iboga, and the ceremonies run all night to harp and drum.
gabon/culture.alt: a Bwiti ceremony at night with harp and torches, Gabon

gabon/eco-tourism.caption: Thirteen Parks in One Decision
gabon/eco-tourism.description: Gabon created all thirteen national parks in 2002, on one day, covering eleven per cent of the country.
gabon/eco-tourism.alt: a park boundary sign at the edge of Gabonese rainforest

gabon/family-community.caption: Elephants From a Boat
gabon/family-community.description: Loango's lagoon puts you at eye level with elephant and buffalo, safely, from the water.
gabon/family-community.alt: a boat on Loango lagoon with elephants on the far bank, Gabon

gabon/festivals.caption: The Bwiti Night
gabon/festivals.description: Ngombi harp, mouth bow and dancing until dawn, and it is a religion rather than a show.
gabon/festivals.alt: musicians playing the ngombi harp at a night ceremony, Gabon

gabon/food.caption: Nyembwe and Smoked Fish
gabon/food.description: Chicken in palm nut nyembwe sauce, and river fish smoked over a slow fire.
gabon/food.alt: a dish of poulet nyembwe with cassava, Gabon

gabon/forests.caption: Congo Basin Forest
gabon/forests.description: Lope has one of the longest continuous records of forest-savanna change anywhere.
gabon/forests.alt: buttressed rainforest trees and understorey at Lope, Gabon

gabon/heritage.caption: Lope-Okanda, and Ivindo
gabon/heritage.description: Two World Heritage sites: the forest-savanna mosaic, and the falls on the Ivindo.
gabon/heritage.alt: the forest-savanna boundary landscape at Lope-Okanda, Gabon

gabon/hero.caption: Loango
gabon/hero.description: Forest elephant and buffalo walking out of the trees onto the Atlantic sand.
gabon/hero.alt: forest elephants on the beach at Loango National Park, Gabon

gabon/hidden-gems.caption: The Trans-Gabonais
gabon/hidden-gems.description: The railway from Libreville to Franceville, straight through Lope, overnight.
gabon/hidden-gems.alt: the Trans-Gabonais railway running through rainforest

gabon/historic-sites.caption: Lope's Rock Art
gabon/historic-sites.description: Engravings on the Ogooue at Lope, and Iron Age sites going back two and a half thousand years.
gabon/historic-sites.alt: rock engravings on granite beside the Ogooue at Lope, Gabon

gabon/lakes-rivers.caption: The Ogooue and the Ivindo
gabon/lakes-rivers.description: The Ogooue drains almost the whole country; the Ivindo runs through Ivindo National Park.
gabon/lakes-rivers.alt: the Ogooue river running broad between forested banks, Gabon

gabon/local-life.caption: Grilled Fish on the Sand
gabon/local-life.description: The Libreville beach restaurants at the weekend, and the fish landed that morning.
gabon/local-life.alt: grilled fish being served at a beach restaurant in Libreville, Gabon

gabon/luxury.caption: A Handful, and Good
gabon/luxury.description: Loango and Lope have real lodges, and the rest of the parks are camping.
gabon/luxury.alt: a lodge deck overlooking the lagoon at Loango, Gabon

gabon/mountains.caption: The Chaillu Massif
gabon/mountains.description: 1,575 metres at Mont Iboundji, forested to the top, in the middle of the country.
gabon/mountains.alt: the forested Chaillu massif under cloud, Gabon

gabon/nature.caption: Eighty-Eight Per Cent Forest
gabon/nature.description: One of the most forested countries on earth, and eleven per cent of it in national parks.
gabon/nature.alt: unbroken rainforest running down to a lagoon in Gabon

gabon/outdoor.caption: Kayak, Trek and Boat
gabon/outdoor.description: Lagoon kayaking at Loango, forest trekking at Ivindo, and the train through Lope.
gabon/outdoor.alt: kayakers on the Loango lagoon at first light, Gabon

gabon/photography.caption: Forest Meeting Ocean
gabon/photography.description: Loango at low sun, when the elephants come out and the beach is empty in both directions.
gabon/photography.alt: elephants crossing an empty beach with forest behind at sunset, Gabon

gabon/safari.caption: Forest and Savanna at Lope
gabon/safari.description: Where the forest meets the last of the Ogooue savanna, with elephant and buffalo in both.
gabon/safari.alt: the forest edge meeting open savanna at Lope, Gabon

gabon/traditional-people.caption: Fang, Punu, Myene and the Baka
gabon/traditional-people.description: Fang across the north, Punu in the south, and Baka forest people in the interior.
gabon/traditional-people.alt: a Punu white-faced mask with carved coiffure, Gabon

gabon/waterfalls.caption: Kongou and Mingouli
gabon/waterfalls.description: Kongou on the Ivindo — three kilometres wide in flood, in the middle of rainforest.
gabon/waterfalls.alt: the wide Kongou falls spread across rainforest on the Ivindo, Gabon

gabon/why-visit.caption: Why Gabon
gabon/why-visit.description: The only place in the world where forest elephants walk out onto an ocean beach.
gabon/why-visit.alt: a forest elephant standing on Atlantic sand at Loango, Gabon

gabon/wildlife.caption: Lowland Gorillas and Mandrills
gabon/wildlife.description: Habituated gorillas at Loango, and mandrill hordes at Lope that run to hundreds.
gabon/wildlife.alt: a mandrill with a bright face in Lope forest, Gabon

gambia/adventure.caption: Upriver by Boat
gambia/adventure.description: Four days up the river from Banjul to Janjanbureh, watching the country change.
gambia/adventure.alt: a small river boat moving upstream past mangrove, The Gambia

gambia/architecture.caption: Colonial and Compound
gambia/architecture.description: Colonial Banjul, and the walled family compounds that are the real unit of Gambian building.
gambia/architecture.alt: a walled family compound with a swept yard and mango tree, The Gambia

gambia/beaches.caption: Eighty Kilometres of Atlantic
gambia/beaches.description: Kotu, Kololi and Cape Point, and the quieter sand south towards Kartong.
gambia/beaches.alt: a wide Atlantic beach with fishing boats at Tanji, The Gambia

gambia/cities.caption: Banjul and Serekunda
gambia/cities.description: A small capital on an island, and the much larger market town that outgrew it.
gambia/cities.alt: the Albert Market and crowds in Banjul, The Gambia

gambia/crafts.caption: Batik, Carving and Baskets
gambia/crafts.description: Tie-dye and batik along the coast, and coiled baskets from the upper river.
gambia/crafts.alt: batik cloth and coiled baskets at a craft market stall, The Gambia

gambia/culture.caption: Mandinka, Fula, Wolof, Jola
gambia/culture.description: Four main peoples in a country of three million, and a griot tradition across all of them.
gambia/culture.alt: a kora player performing at a Gambian village gathering, The Gambia

gambia/eco-tourism.caption: Community Birding
gambia/eco-tourism.description: Village guide associations have run the birding here for decades, and the money stays.
gambia/eco-tourism.alt: a local guide pointing out a bird to visitors on a creek, The Gambia

gambia/family-community.caption: Easy for Everybody
gambia/family-community.description: Short flights, short distances, warm shallow sea and a country used to visitors.
gambia/family-community.alt: children playing in shallow water on a Gambian beach, The Gambia

gambia/festivals.caption: Kankurang
gambia/festivals.description: A masked figure of the Mandinka initiation, and a UNESCO-listed tradition.
gambia/festivals.alt: the Kankurang masked figure in red bark and leaves, The Gambia

gambia/food.caption: Benachin and Domoda
gambia/food.description: Benachin — one-pot rice — and domoda, groundnut stew with lamb.
gambia/food.alt: a shared bowl of benachin rice with fish and vegetables, The Gambia

gambia/forests.caption: Bijilo and Abuko
gambia/forests.description: Small forest reserves close to the coast, with colobus, vervets and a great deal of birdlife.
gambia/forests.alt: red colobus monkeys in the canopy at Bijilo forest, The Gambia

gambia/heritage.caption: Stone Circles and the Slave Route
gambia/heritage.description: The Wassu stone circles are a thousand years old; the river route is four hundred.
gambia/heritage.alt: the standing laterite stone circles at Wassu, The Gambia

gambia/hero.caption: The River
gambia/hero.description: The country is the river — three hundred kilometres of it, and a strip either bank.
gambia/hero.alt: the wide Gambia river with mangrove banks at sunset, The Gambia

gambia/hidden-gems.caption: Kartong
gambia/hidden-gems.description: The far south, a river mouth, a crocodile pool and almost nobody.
gambia/hidden-gems.alt: the quiet river mouth and empty beach at Kartong, The Gambia

gambia/historic-sites.caption: Kunta Kinteh Island
gambia/historic-sites.description: A slaving island in the river, eroding, and the reason a great many people come.
gambia/historic-sites.alt: the ruined fort on Kunta Kinteh Island in the Gambia river

gambia/lakes-rivers.caption: The Gambia Itself
gambia/lakes-rivers.description: Tidal for half its length, and every town on it is a landing.
gambia/lakes-rivers.alt: a ferry crossing the Gambia river at Farafenni

gambia/local-life.caption: The Fish Landing at Tanji
gambia/local-life.description: The boats come in mid-afternoon and the beach becomes a market in twenty minutes.
gambia/local-life.alt: painted fishing pirogues and crowds at Tanji fish landing, The Gambia

gambia/luxury.caption: Long Established
gambia/luxury.description: Everything from big beach hotels to small river lodges, and forty years of practice.
gambia/luxury.alt: a river lodge terrace looking out over the Gambia river

gambia/mountains.caption: Flat
gambia/mountains.description: The highest point is fifty-three metres. This is river country, not hill country.
gambia/mountains.alt: flat savanna and a lone baobab in the upper river region, The Gambia

gambia/nature.caption: Mangrove, Savanna and Gallery Forest
gambia/nature.description: Salt mangrove at the mouth, freshwater swamp in the middle, dry savanna at the top.
gambia/nature.alt: mangrove creeks and channels off the Gambia river

gambia/outdoor.caption: Birding on Foot
gambia/outdoor.description: Abuko, Tanji and the Kotu creek — three of the best birding walks in Africa, all near the beach.
gambia/outdoor.alt: birdwatchers with binoculars on a creek path at Kotu, The Gambia

gambia/photography.caption: River Light
gambia/photography.description: The upper river at dawn, when the mist sits on the water and the fish eagles call.
gambia/photography.alt: mist on the Gambia river at dawn with a fish eagle

gambia/safari.caption: Chimps at Baboon Islands
gambia/safari.description: A rehabilitated chimpanzee population on river islands, watched from boats only.
gambia/safari.alt: chimpanzees on the bank of a Gambia river island, The Gambia

gambia/traditional-people.caption: The Griots
gambia/traditional-people.description: The Jali families hold the histories, and the kora is how they are told.
gambia/traditional-people.alt: a Jali griot playing the kora outside a compound, The Gambia

gambia/waterfalls.caption: None
gambia/waterfalls.description: No falls. The river drops so little across the country that the tide runs a hundred kilometres up it.
gambia/waterfalls.alt: still water and reflected trees on the upper Gambia river, The Gambia

gambia/why-visit.caption: Why The Gambia
gambia/why-visit.description: Six hundred bird species and four hundred years of river history, in a country you cross in a day.
gambia/why-visit.alt: a small boat on the Gambia river with mangrove either side

gambia/wildlife.caption: Six Hundred Bird Species
gambia/wildlife.description: In a country you can drive across in twenty minutes. It is one of the great birding places.
gambia/wildlife.alt: an Abyssinian roller on a branch in Gambian savanna, The Gambia

ghana/adventure.caption: Canopy, Surf and Lake
ghana/adventure.description: The Kakum walkway, Busua's beach breaks, and hiking the Volta hills to the Togo border.
ghana/adventure.alt: a hiking trail through the hills of the Volta region, Ghana

ghana/architecture.caption: Posuban and Colonial Coast
ghana/architecture.description: The Fante posuban shrines, and the trading architecture strung along the coast road.
ghana/architecture.alt: a painted Fante posuban shrine in a coastal town, Ghana

ghana/beaches.caption: Busua and Cape Three Points
ghana/beaches.description: Surf at Busua, and the point where the country runs out into the Gulf of Guinea.
ghana/beaches.alt: palms above the beach at Busua on the Ghanaian coast

ghana/cities.caption: Accra and Kumasi
ghana/cities.description: Accra on the Atlantic, and Kumasi's Kejetia — one of the largest markets in West Africa.
ghana/cities.alt: the vast Kejetia market spread out at Kumasi, Ghana

ghana/crafts.caption: Kente and Adinkra
ghana/crafts.description: Kente woven in strips at Bonwire, and adinkra symbols stamped by hand at Ntonso.
ghana/crafts.alt: adinkra symbols being stamped onto cloth by hand, Ghana

ghana/culture.caption: Ashanti
ghana/culture.description: A kingdom that fought the British to a standstill, and still keeps its own court at Kumasi.
ghana/culture.alt: the Manhyia palace grounds at Kumasi, Ghana

ghana/eco-tourism.caption: Community Forest
ghana/eco-tourism.description: The Wechiau hippo sanctuary and the Boabeng-Fiema monkey sanctuary, both village-run.
ghana/eco-tourism.alt: hippos in the Black Volta at the Wechiau sanctuary, Ghana

ghana/family-community.caption: Easy First Africa
ghana/family-community.description: English-speaking, short distances, and about as gentle an introduction as the continent offers.
ghana/family-community.alt: children playing on a beach on the Ghanaian coast

ghana/festivals.caption: Homowo and Chale Wote
ghana/festivals.description: Homowo in Accra in August, and the Chale Wote street art festival in Jamestown.
ghana/festivals.alt: a street art festival crowd in Jamestown, Accra, Ghana

ghana/food.caption: Jollof, Banku and Grilled Tilapia
ghana/food.description: The jollof argument is unwinnable; the tilapia off the grill with banku settles it.
ghana/food.alt: grilled tilapia and banku served at a roadside chop bar, Ghana

ghana/forests.caption: Kakum
ghana/forests.description: Rainforest with a canopy walkway thirty metres up, strung between seven emergent trees.
ghana/forests.alt: the canopy walkway suspended above Kakum rainforest, Ghana

ghana/heritage.caption: The Year of Return
ghana/heritage.description: Ghana asked the diaspora to come back, and a great many people did.
ghana/heritage.alt: a memorial gathering at Cape Coast castle, Ghana

ghana/hero.caption: The Forts, the Forest and the Highlife
ghana/hero.description: Coastal forts, Ashanti gold, elephants in the north, and a band playing somewhere every night.
ghana/hero.alt: the white walls of Cape Coast castle above the Atlantic, Ghana

ghana/hidden-gems.caption: Nzulezo
ghana/hidden-gems.description: A village built entirely on stilts over Lake Tandane, reached only by canoe.
ghana/hidden-gems.alt: the stilt village of Nzulezo over the water, Ghana

ghana/historic-sites.caption: The Slave Forts
ghana/historic-sites.description: Cape Coast and Elmina — the doors of no return, kept as they were and not softened.
ghana/historic-sites.alt: the door of no return at Elmina castle, Ghana

ghana/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Volta
ghana/lakes-rivers.description: The largest reservoir on earth by surface area, with ferries that take a full day to cross it.
ghana/lakes-rivers.alt: fishing boats on Lake Volta at first light, Ghana

ghana/local-life.caption: Chop Bars and Trotros
ghana/local-life.description: The country runs on shared minibuses and roadside kitchens, and both are worth using.
ghana/local-life.alt: a busy trotro station in Accra, Ghana

ghana/luxury.caption: Lodges on the Water
ghana/luxury.description: Small lodges above the beach at Busua and Axim, and the Mole escarpment rooms over the waterhole.
ghana/luxury.alt: a lodge terrace overlooking the waterhole at Mole, Ghana

ghana/mountains.caption: The Akwapim and Afadja
ghana/mountains.description: Afadjato is 885 metres and the highest point, walkable in a morning from Liati Wote.
ghana/mountains.alt: the green hills of the Volta region from Afadjato, Ghana

ghana/nature.caption: Coast to Savanna
ghana/nature.description: Rainforest and lagoon in the south, transitional woodland through the middle, savanna at Mole.
ghana/nature.alt: rainforest canopy in Kakum national park, Ghana

ghana/outdoor.caption: Surf, Hike, Paddle
ghana/outdoor.description: Busua's breaks, the Volta hills, and canoes on the lake at Dodi.
ghana/outdoor.alt: a surfer walking out at Busua beach, Ghana

ghana/photography.caption: Colour Everywhere
ghana/photography.description: Kente, market cloth and painted trotros — nothing here is any colour by accident.
ghana/photography.alt: stacked bolts of printed cloth in a Ghanaian market

ghana/safari.caption: Walking Safari at Mole
ghana/safari.description: One of the few parks in West Africa where the game drive is done on foot, with an armed ranger.
ghana/safari.alt: a ranger leading walkers through savanna at Mole, Ghana

ghana/traditional-people.caption: The Ewe and the Dagomba
ghana/traditional-people.description: Kente weaving in Volta and Ashanti, and the Dagbon drumming traditions of the north.
ghana/traditional-people.alt: a weaver working a kente loom in Bonwire, Ghana

ghana/waterfalls.caption: Wli
ghana/waterfalls.description: The highest falls in West Africa, dropping out of forest on the Togo border, with bats overhead.
ghana/waterfalls.alt: the Wli waterfall dropping through forest in the Volta region, Ghana

ghana/why-visit.caption: The Gentle Introduction
ghana/why-visit.description: English, good roads, a short flight from Europe, and everything within a day's drive.
ghana/why-visit.alt: a coastal road running along the Gulf of Guinea, Ghana

ghana/wildlife.caption: Mole and Ankasa
ghana/wildlife.description: Elephants that walk into the camp waterhole at Mole, and forest elephants at Ankasa.
ghana/wildlife.alt: elephants at the waterhole below Mole motel, Ghana

guinea-bissau/adventure.caption: Island Hopping by Pirogue
guinea-bissau/adventure.description: There are no bridges. Everything is boats, tides and waiting, and that is the pleasure of it.
guinea-bissau/adventure.alt: a motorised pirogue crossing between Bijagos islands, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/architecture.caption: Portuguese Colonial and Palm Thatch
guinea-bissau/architecture.description: Tiled colonial fronts in Bissau, and rectangular palm-thatch houses through the islands.
guinea-bissau/architecture.alt: a palm-thatched island house with a swept sand yard, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/beaches.caption: Island Sand
guinea-bissau/beaches.description: Bubaque, Rubane and Orango have empty palm-backed beaches and warm water.
guinea-bissau/beaches.alt: an empty palm-backed beach on Rubane island, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/cities.caption: Bissau
guinea-bissau/cities.description: A small Portuguese-built capital with a decaying Bissau Velho quarter and very good music.
guinea-bissau/cities.alt: the faded Portuguese colonial buildings of Bissau Velho, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/crafts.caption: Carving and Cloth
guinea-bissau/crafts.description: Bijago bull and shark masks, and the woven pano de pente cloth used as currency.
guinea-bissau/crafts.alt: a carved Bijago shark mask and woven pano cloth, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/culture.caption: Matrilineal, and Still So
guinea-bissau/culture.description: Bijago women choose husbands, own the houses, and hold the religious authority.
guinea-bissau/culture.alt: Bijago women in ceremonial dress on an island beach, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/eco-tourism.caption: Community Conservation
guinea-bissau/eco-tourism.description: The island communities police the turtle beaches themselves, and it works.
guinea-bissau/eco-tourism.alt: villagers recording a turtle nest on a Bijagos beach, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/family-community.caption: Boats and Beaches
guinea-bissau/family-community.description: Not for very small children — the boats are open and the tides are serious.
guinea-bissau/family-community.alt: a family on the sand beside a beached pirogue, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/festivals.caption: Carnival in Bissau
guinea-bissau/festivals.description: Masks, drums and neighbourhood competition, Portuguese in form and entirely local in content.
guinea-bissau/festivals.alt: masked dancers at the Bissau carnival, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/food.caption: Rice, Cashew and Bica
guinea-bissau/food.description: Rice from the paddies, cashew as the whole export economy, and Portuguese coffee.
guinea-bissau/food.alt: a plate of rice with fish and palm oil sauce, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/forests.caption: Palm and Sacred Grove
guinea-bissau/forests.description: Oil palm through the islands, and groves that are ceremonial ground and off limits.
guinea-bissau/forests.alt: oil palms and dense forest on a Bijagos island, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/heritage.caption: The Bijagos Biosphere
guinea-bissau/heritage.description: The whole archipelago is a UNESCO biosphere reserve, run with the island communities.
guinea-bissau/heritage.alt: a community ranger boat among the Bijagos islands, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/hero.caption: The Bijagos
guinea-bissau/hero.description: Eighty-eight islands, twenty of them inhabited, and a UNESCO biosphere reserve over all of it.
guinea-bissau/hero.alt: palm-fringed islands and tidal channels in the Bijagos archipelago, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/hidden-gems.caption: Orango
guinea-bissau/hidden-gems.description: Hippos, an island king, and a lodge with no road on the island at all.
guinea-bissau/hidden-gems.alt: a savanna clearing with hippo tracks on Orango island, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/historic-sites.caption: Cacheu
guinea-bissau/historic-sites.description: A slaving fort of 1588 on the river, and one of the oldest European buildings in West Africa.
