guinea-bissau/historic-sites.alt: the old Portuguese fort and cannon at Cacheu, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/lakes-rivers.caption: The Geba and the Corubal
guinea-bissau/lakes-rivers.description: Two rivers cutting deep estuaries into the mainland, navigable a long way up.
guinea-bissau/lakes-rivers.alt: the wide brown estuary of the Geba river, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/local-life.caption: Sunday at the Beach
guinea-bissau/local-life.description: Bissau goes to Bubaque and the near islands at weekends, by ferry, with a stereo.
guinea-bissau/local-life.alt: a crowded island ferry leaving Bissau on a Sunday, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/luxury.caption: Two or Three Lodges
guinea-bissau/luxury.description: Small fishing and eco-lodges on Rubane and Orango, and not much else anywhere.
guinea-bissau/luxury.alt: a small thatched eco-lodge among palms on a Bijagos island, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/mountains.caption: Flat Country
guinea-bissau/mountains.description: The highest point is three hundred metres. This is a country of water, not relief.
guinea-bissau/mountains.alt: flat green rice paddy stretching to a treeline, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/nature.caption: Mangrove and Tide
guinea-bissau/nature.description: The tidal range here is five metres, and the channels between the islands change with it.
guinea-bissau/nature.alt: mangrove channels at low tide in the Bijagos, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/outdoor.caption: Fishing the Channels
guinea-bissau/outdoor.description: Barracuda and tarpon in the passes between islands, on light tackle.
guinea-bissau/outdoor.alt: an angler casting from a boat in a Bijagos channel, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/photography.caption: Tide and Palm
guinea-bissau/photography.description: The channels at low water, when the mangrove roots come out and the light goes flat.
guinea-bissau/photography.alt: exposed mangrove roots and channels at low tide, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/safari.caption: Turtles at Poilao
guinea-bissau/safari.description: One of the largest green turtle nesting sites in the Atlantic, on an uninhabited island.
guinea-bissau/safari.alt: a green turtle returning to the sea at dawn on Poilao, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/traditional-people.caption: The Bijagos
guinea-bissau/traditional-people.description: Age grades govern life, and the vaca-bruto initiation is danced in a bull mask.
guinea-bissau/traditional-people.alt: a Bijago dancer in a carved bull mask at a village ceremony, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/waterfalls.caption: None to Speak Of
guinea-bissau/waterfalls.description: No falls — the land has nowhere to fall from. The water here moves sideways with the tide.
guinea-bissau/waterfalls.alt: a tidal creek running through mangrove at Cacheu, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/why-visit.caption: Why Guinea-Bissau
guinea-bissau/why-visit.description: Saltwater hippos, nesting turtles, and a society run by its women.
guinea-bissau/why-visit.alt: a pirogue crossing still water between two Bijagos islands, Guinea-Bissau

guinea-bissau/wildlife.caption: Saltwater Hippos
guinea-bissau/wildlife.description: The hippos of Orango swim in the sea between islands, which almost no others do.
guinea-bissau/wildlife.alt: a hippo in shallow salt water off Orango island, Guinea-Bissau

guinea/adventure.caption: Hiking the Fouta
guinea/adventure.description: Village to village between waterfalls and cliffs, with the best walking network in the region.
guinea/adventure.alt: walkers on a path between villages in the Fouta Djallon, Guinea

guinea/architecture.caption: Colonial and Fouta Vernacular
guinea/architecture.description: French colonial in Conakry, and round thatched houses with painted walls in the highlands.
guinea/architecture.alt: a round thatched Fouta house with a painted wall, Guinea

guinea/beaches.caption: Three Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
guinea/beaches.description: Mangrove coast with the Iles de Los off Conakry, and beaches on Roume and Kassa.
guinea/beaches.alt: a beach and palms on Roume island off Conakry, Guinea

guinea/cities.caption: Conakry
guinea/cities.description: A capital on a peninsula, with the Grande Mosquee and the sea on both sides.
guinea/cities.alt: the Grande Mosquee and low buildings of Conakry, Guinea

guinea/crafts.caption: Weaving and Indigo
guinea/crafts.description: Fouta indigo cloth, Malinke weaving, and the leatherwork of the highland towns.
guinea/crafts.alt: indigo-dyed cloth drying at a Fouta Djallon workshop, Guinea

guinea/culture.caption: Where the Music Came From
guinea/culture.description: Bembeya Jazz, the Ballets Africains, and a state that funded orchestras for two decades.
guinea/culture.alt: a djembe and balafon group performing in Conakry, Guinea

guinea/eco-tourism.caption: Nimba's Endemics
guinea/eco-tourism.description: The mountain has species found on it and nowhere else, and an iron deposit under them.
guinea/eco-tourism.alt: a botanist recording plants on the Nimba grassland, Guinea

guinea/family-community.caption: Waterfalls You Can Swim In
guinea/family-community.description: Most of the Fouta's falls have a pool at the bottom and a path down to it.
guinea/family-community.alt: children swimming in a pool below a Fouta Djallon waterfall, Guinea

guinea/festivals.caption: Masked Dance in the Forest Region
guinea/festivals.description: The forest peoples of the southeast keep mask societies that are not for visitors, and some that are.
guinea/festivals.alt: a stilt dancer performing at a village festival in Guinea

guinea/food.caption: Riz Gras and Fouti
guinea/food.description: Rice with palm oil and fish, and the sour milk and maize of the Fouta.
guinea/food.alt: a shared plate of Guinean rice with fish and sauce

guinea/forests.caption: The Guinean Forest
guinea/forests.description: Ziama and Diecke in the southeast — some of the last high forest in West Africa.
guinea/forests.alt: buttressed rainforest trees in the Ziama massif, Guinea

guinea/heritage.caption: Nimba, Listed
guinea/heritage.description: Mount Nimba is a World Heritage site for its endemic toad, viviparous, that lives on the ridge.
guinea/heritage.alt: montane grassland and cloud on the Nimba ridge, Guinea

guinea/hero.caption: The Fouta Djallon
guinea/hero.description: A sandstone highland at a thousand metres, cut by gorges, and the source of three great rivers.
guinea/hero.alt: green plateau and sandstone cliffs in the Fouta Djallon, Guinea

guinea/hidden-gems.caption: The Dame de Mali
guinea/hidden-gems.description: A rock face near Mali-ville shaped like a woman's profile, at the top of the Fouta.
guinea/hidden-gems.alt: the Dame de Mali rock profile above the Fouta escarpment, Guinea

guinea/historic-sites.caption: The Almamy's Fouta
guinea/historic-sites.description: The Fouta Djallon was a theocratic Fulani state for a century and a half before the French came.
guinea/historic-sites.alt: an old mosque and stone walls in a Fouta Djallon town, Guinea

guinea/lakes-rivers.caption: The Upper Niger
guinea/lakes-rivers.description: It rises near the Sierra Leone border and is already wide by the time it leaves the country.
guinea/lakes-rivers.alt: the upper Niger river running broad through green country, Guinea

guinea/local-life.caption: Market Day in Labe
guinea/local-life.description: The highland market fills with Fulani from every village within a day's walk.
guinea/local-life.alt: the crowded weekly market at Labe in the Fouta Djallon, Guinea

guinea/luxury.caption: Modest
guinea/luxury.description: Hotels in Conakry and a few in Labe and Dalaba. The Fouta runs on homestays.
guinea/luxury.alt: a colonial-era hill station guesthouse at Dalaba, Guinea

guinea/mountains.caption: Mount Nimba
guinea/mountains.description: 1,752 metres on the Liberian border, with species that live on that mountain and nowhere else.
guinea/mountains.alt: the grassy ridge of Mount Nimba above forest, Guinea

guinea/nature.caption: Where the Rivers Rise
guinea/nature.description: The Niger, the Senegal and the Gambia all begin within a hundred kilometres of each other.
guinea/nature.alt: a clear stream running over rock at the source of the Niger, Guinea

guinea/outdoor.caption: Trekking the Highlands
guinea/outdoor.description: The Fouta has marked routes, village guides and huts, which is rare in the region.
guinea/outdoor.alt: a marked walking trail across the Fouta Djallon plateau, Guinea

guinea/photography.caption: Cliffs and Water
guinea/photography.description: The Fouta escarpments in the hour after the rain stops, when everything is running.
guinea/photography.alt: cliffs and multiple waterfalls after rain in the Fouta Djallon, Guinea

guinea/safari.caption: The Forest, Not the Plain
guinea/safari.description: There is no savanna circuit. What Guinea has is forest primates and the Nimba massif.
guinea/safari.alt: dense forest canopy on the slopes of Mount Nimba, Guinea

guinea/traditional-people.caption: Fulani, Malinke, Susu
guinea/traditional-people.description: Fulani in the Fouta, Malinke in the upper Niger country, Susu on the coast.
guinea/traditional-people.alt: a Fulani herder with cattle on the Fouta Djallon plateau, Guinea

guinea/waterfalls.caption: Ditinn and Kinkon
guinea/waterfalls.description: Ditinn drops a hundred metres off a sheer cliff; Kinkon runs through a gorge below Pita.
guinea/waterfalls.alt: the Ditinn waterfall falling from a sheer cliff in the Fouta, Guinea

guinea/why-visit.caption: Why Guinea
guinea/why-visit.description: The best walking in West Africa, and the rivers that made the whole region.
guinea/why-visit.alt: a walker looking out over layered Fouta Djallon ridges, Guinea

guinea/wildlife.caption: Chimpanzees at Bossou
guinea/wildlife.description: One of the best-studied wild chimpanzee groups anywhere, and one that uses stone tools.
guinea/wildlife.alt: a wild chimpanzee cracking nuts with a stone at Bossou, Guinea

kenya/adventure.caption: Balloon Over the Mara
kenya/adventure.description: Up before dawn, an hour over the plains at treetop height, and breakfast on the grass where you land.
kenya/adventure.alt: a hot-air balloon over the Maasai Mara plains at sunrise, Kenya

reasons: looks like 56% of a slot already filled here

kenya/architecture.caption: Coral Stone and Carved Doors
kenya/architecture.description: Swahili coral-rag houses with inner courtyards, and doors carved in Lamu and shipped up the coast.
kenya/architecture.alt: an ornately carved Swahili door in a coral stone wall in Lamu, Kenya

kenya/beaches.caption: The Swahili Coast
kenya/beaches.description: Diani, Watamu and Lamu: white sand, warm Indian Ocean, and a coastline that traded with Arabia for a thousand years.
kenya/beaches.alt: white sand and dhows on Diani Beach on the Indian Ocean, Kenya

kenya/cities.caption: Nairobi, Green City in the Sun
kenya/cities.description: The only capital on earth with a national park inside the city limits, and lions in sight of the skyline.
kenya/cities.alt: the Nairobi skyline seen across Nairobi National Park, Kenya

kenya/crafts.caption: Beadwork and Kisii Stone
kenya/crafts.description: Maasai beadwork, Kisii soapstone carving, and kiondo sisal baskets made the way they always were.
kenya/crafts.alt: Maasai women stringing beadwork ornaments, Kenya

kenya/culture.caption: Maasai and Swahili
kenya/culture.description: Two Kenyas: the cattle-keeping highlands and the coral-stone, Arabic-inflected coast.
kenya/culture.alt: Maasai elders in red shuka cloth on the open plains, Kenya

kenya/eco-tourism.caption: Rhino, Counted Daily
kenya/eco-tourism.description: Ol Pejeta and Lewa run some of Africa's most closely monitored rhino populations, funded by the beds on the property.
kenya/eco-tourism.alt: black rhino grazing on the Ol Pejeta conservancy at dawn, Kenya

kenya/family-community.caption: The Conservancies
kenya/family-community.description: Community conservancies lease grazing land back for wildlife, and the lease pays the schools around the Mara.
kenya/family-community.alt: a community conservancy ranger team on patrol near the Maasai Mara, Kenya

kenya/festivals.caption: Lamu Cultural Festival
kenya/festivals.description: Dhow races, donkey races, henna and taarab music in the alleys of a town with almost no cars.
kenya/festivals.alt: dhow racing during the Lamu cultural festival, Kenya

kenya/food.caption: Nyama Choma and Ugali
kenya/food.description: Goat roasted over charcoal, maize meal, sukuma wiki, and coastal biryani that came in by dhow.
kenya/food.alt: nyama choma roasting over charcoal at a Nairobi grill, Kenya

kenya/forests.caption: Kakamega, the Last of It
kenya/forests.description: The only Kenyan remnant of the Guineo-Congolian rainforest that once ran clear across the continent.
kenya/forests.alt: dense canopy and hanging vines inside Kakamega Forest, Kenya

kenya/heritage.caption: Lamu Old Town
kenya/heritage.description: The oldest continuously inhabited Swahili settlement, carved doors, coral rag walls and no room for a car.
kenya/heritage.alt: carved wooden doors and coral stone alleys in Lamu Old Town, Kenya

kenya/hero.caption: Where the Safari Was Invented
kenya/hero.description: The Maasai Mara at first light, and everything the word safari has meant for a century.
kenya/hero.alt: acacia and open grassland in the Maasai Mara at sunrise, Kenya

kenya/hidden-gems.caption: Chalbi and Marsabit
kenya/hidden-gems.description: The desert north: Chalbi's salt pan, Marsabit's forested crater and the road down to Lake Turkana.
kenya/hidden-gems.alt: the salt pan and dunes of the Chalbi desert in northern Kenya

kenya/historic-sites.caption: Fort Jesus, Mombasa
kenya/historic-sites.description: Portuguese, built 1593, taken and retaken nine times — now UNESCO World Heritage above the old harbour.
kenya/historic-sites.alt: the coral ramparts of Fort Jesus above Mombasa old harbour, Kenya

kenya/lakes-rivers.caption: Flamingo Country
kenya/lakes-rivers.description: Nakuru, Bogoria and Elementaita hold soda water, hot springs and flamingo in numbers that change by the season.
kenya/lakes-rivers.alt: flamingos massed on the shallows of Lake Nakuru, Kenya

kenya/local-life.caption: Matatus and Markets
kenya/local-life.description: Painted, over-amplified matatus, Maasai Market on rotation through the week, and tea at every stop.
kenya/local-life.alt: brightly painted matatu minibuses in a Nairobi street, Kenya

kenya/luxury.caption: Camps on the Mara
kenya/luxury.description: Small tented camps on private conservancies, night drives and off-road access the main reserve does not allow.
kenya/luxury.alt: a luxury tented safari camp overlooking the Maasai Mara plains, Kenya

kenya/mountains.caption: Mount Kenya, 5,199 m
kenya/mountains.description: Equatorial glaciers, giant lobelia, and a trekking route to Point Lenana that needs no technical climbing.
kenya/mountains.alt: the jagged glaciated peaks of Mount Kenya above the moorland

kenya/nature.caption: The Great Rift Valley
kenya/nature.description: The escarpment drops away below the Naivasha road, holding a chain of soda lakes and dormant volcanoes.
kenya/nature.alt: the Great Rift Valley escarpment and floor seen from the Naivasha road, Kenya

kenya/outdoor.caption: Walking Hell's Gate
kenya/outdoor.description: The one Kenyan park you can walk and cycle through, with gorge scrambling and geothermal steam.
kenya/outdoor.alt: cyclists on the track between the cliffs of Hell's Gate National Park, Kenya

kenya/photography.caption: Kilimanjaro from Amboseli
kenya/photography.description: The mountain is in Tanzania; the view of it is in Kenya, and it is only clear for an hour at each end of the day.
kenya/photography.alt: elephants beneath Mount Kilimanjaro seen from Amboseli at sunrise, Kenya

kenya/safari.caption: The Great Migration
kenya/safari.description: Between July and October a million wildebeest cross the Mara river, and the crocodiles are already waiting.
kenya/safari.alt: wildebeest crossing the Mara river during the great migration, Kenya

kenya/traditional-people.caption: Samburu and Maasai
kenya/traditional-people.description: Samburu in the northern drylands, Maasai in the south, both still moving cattle between seasonal grazing.
kenya/traditional-people.alt: a Samburu warrior with beaded ornaments in the northern drylands, Kenya

kenya/waterfalls.caption: Thomson's Falls
kenya/waterfalls.description: The Ewaso Ng'iro drops seventy-four metres into a fern gorge at Nyahururu, on the way north to Samburu.
kenya/waterfalls.alt: Thomson's Falls dropping into the fern gorge at Nyahururu, Kenya

kenya/why-visit.caption: Magical Kenya
kenya/why-visit.description: Migration, glacier, reef and desert inside one border, with the infrastructure to see all four in a fortnight.
kenya/why-visit.alt: acacia silhouetted against a red sunset on the Kenyan savannah

kenya/wildlife.caption: Wildlife on the Savannah
kenya/wildlife.description: The Big Five, plus the reticulated giraffe and Grevy's zebra that live nowhere south of here.
kenya/wildlife.alt: elephants crossing the plain at Amboseli beneath Kilimanjaro, Kenya

lesotho/adventure.caption: Pony Trekking
lesotho/adventure.description: The Basotho pony is the way to cross this country, and has been for a hundred and fifty years.
lesotho/adventure.alt: riders on Basotho ponies crossing a high mountain pass, Lesotho

lesotho/architecture.caption: Sandstone and Rondavel
lesotho/architecture.description: Colonial sandstone in Maseru, and painted rondavels with stone walls in the mountains.
lesotho/architecture.alt: a stone rondavel with a thatched roof in the Maloti, Lesotho

lesotho/beaches.caption: High Reservoirs
lesotho/beaches.description: Landlocked and mountainous: the water here is Katse and Mohale, and it is sold to South Africa.
lesotho/beaches.alt: the Katse dam wall and reservoir between mountains, Lesotho

lesotho/cities.caption: Maseru
lesotho/cities.description: A small capital on the Caledon, with the border post at the end of the main street.
lesotho/cities.alt: the main street and sandstone buildings of Maseru, Lesotho

lesotho/crafts.caption: Blankets, Hats and Tapestry
lesotho/crafts.description: Woven mohair tapestry, the conical mokorotlo hat, and the blankets themselves.
lesotho/crafts.alt: a woven mohair tapestry on a loom in Lesotho

lesotho/culture.caption: The Blanket and the Hat
lesotho/culture.description: The Basotho blanket is worn seriously and read closely, and the mokorotlo is on the flag.
lesotho/culture.alt: a man in a patterned Basotho blanket on a mountain road, Lesotho

lesotho/eco-tourism.caption: Water as the Economy
lesotho/eco-tourism.description: The Highlands Water Project sells water to South Africa, and the dams are the landscape now.
lesotho/eco-tourism.alt: the Katse reservoir winding between steep mountainsides, Lesotho

lesotho/family-community.caption: Ponies and Snow
lesotho/family-community.description: Short pony treks, dinosaur footprints and, in winter, actual snow.
lesotho/family-community.alt: children on Basotho ponies with a guide, Lesotho

lesotho/festivals.caption: Morija Arts and Cultural Festival
lesotho/festivals.description: Music, poetry and horse racing at Morija every year, and the country turns up.
lesotho/festivals.alt: horse racing at the Morija cultural festival, Lesotho

lesotho/food.caption: Papa, Moroho and Motoho
lesotho/food.description: Maize papa with wild greens, and motoho — fermented sorghum drink.
lesotho/food.alt: a bowl of papa with moroho greens, Lesotho

lesotho/forests.caption: Almost None
lesotho/forests.description: Above the treeline for most of the country, and the small patches left are protected.
lesotho/forests.alt: a patch of indigenous forest in a sheltered Lesotho gorge

lesotho/heritage.caption: Maloti-Drakensberg
lesotho/heritage.description: A World Heritage site shared with South Africa, for its landscape and its San rock art.
lesotho/heritage.alt: San rock paintings on a sandstone overhang in Lesotho

lesotho/hero.caption: The Kingdom in the Sky
lesotho/hero.description: Nowhere in Lesotho is below 1,400 metres, which is true of no other country.
lesotho/hero.alt: the high Maloti mountains with a shepherd's hut on a ridge, Lesotho

lesotho/hidden-gems.caption: Dinosaur Footprints
lesotho/hidden-gems.description: Trackways in the sandstone at Moyeni and Morija, in the open and unfenced.
lesotho/hidden-gems.alt: fossil dinosaur footprints in exposed sandstone rock, Lesotho

lesotho/historic-sites.caption: Thaba Bosiu
lesotho/historic-sites.description: The flat-topped mountain Moshoeshoe I defended, and where the nation was made.
lesotho/historic-sites.alt: the flat-topped plateau of Thaba Bosiu above the plain, Lesotho

lesotho/lakes-rivers.caption: The Senqu
lesotho/lakes-rivers.description: The Orange river rises here and runs the whole width of South Africa afterwards.
lesotho/lakes-rivers.alt: the young Senqu river running through a high mountain valley, Lesotho

lesotho/local-life.caption: Sunday on Horseback
lesotho/local-life.description: The horse is transport, not recreation, and every village has them saddled.
lesotho/local-life.alt: villagers on horseback on a mountain track, Lesotho

lesotho/luxury.caption: Lodges and Trading Posts
lesotho/luxury.description: Malealea and Semonkong grew out of trading posts, and they are the best of it.
lesotho/luxury.alt: a mountain lodge with stone buildings at Semonkong, Lesotho

lesotho/mountains.caption: Thabana Ntlenyana
lesotho/mountains.description: 3,482 metres, the highest point in Africa south of Kilimanjaro.
lesotho/mountains.alt: the summit plateau of Thabana Ntlenyana under snow, Lesotho

lesotho/nature.caption: The Maloti
lesotho/nature.description: Basalt highlands cut by river gorges, and the roof of southern Africa.
lesotho/nature.alt: the Maloti mountains with deep valleys and no trees, Lesotho

lesotho/outdoor.caption: Sani and Sehlabathebe
lesotho/outdoor.description: The Sani Pass in four-wheel-drive, and the rock formations and rivers of Sehlabathebe.
lesotho/outdoor.alt: the hairpins of the Sani Pass climbing the escarpment, Lesotho

lesotho/photography.caption: High and Clear
lesotho/photography.description: The Maloti in autumn, when the grass turns and the air will not hold any haze.
lesotho/photography.alt: clear autumn light on golden grassland and basalt ridges, Lesotho

lesotho/safari.caption: Not the Business Here
lesotho/safari.description: This is a mountain country, not a savanna one. What you go for is the ground and the horses.
lesotho/safari.alt: eland grazing in high grassland at Sehlabathebe, Lesotho

lesotho/traditional-people.caption: The Basotho
lesotho/traditional-people.description: One people, one language, and a kingdom that kept its independence by going uphill.
lesotho/traditional-people.alt: Basotho herders in blankets with sheep on a high pasture, Lesotho

lesotho/waterfalls.caption: Maletsunyane
lesotho/waterfalls.description: 192 metres in a single drop, and a commercial abseil down beside it.
lesotho/waterfalls.alt: the single 192-metre drop of the Maletsunyane falls, Lesotho

lesotho/why-visit.caption: Why Lesotho
lesotho/why-visit.description: A whole country above a thousand metres, crossed on a pony, with snow in July.
lesotho/why-visit.alt: a rider on a Basotho pony against a wide mountain horizon, Lesotho

lesotho/wildlife.caption: Bearded Vulture and Eland
lesotho/wildlife.description: The lammergeier breeds on the Drakensberg escarpment, and eland are back in the reserves.
lesotho/wildlife.alt: a bearded vulture in flight along a mountain escarpment, Lesotho

liberia/adventure.caption: Surfing Robertsport
liberia/adventure.description: Cassava Point and Fisherman's Point — long left-hand point breaks, and a village surf club.
liberia/adventure.alt: a surfer on a long left-hand wave at Robertsport, Liberia

liberia/architecture.caption: Verandah and Zinc
liberia/architecture.description: Americo-Liberian timber houses with deep verandahs, and zinc-roofed cityscape behind them.
liberia/architecture.alt: a timber verandah house with a zinc roof in Monrovia, Liberia

liberia/beaches.caption: Five Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
liberia/beaches.description: Long empty beaches, and a serious swell from November on.
liberia/beaches.alt: an empty palm-backed beach on the Liberian Atlantic coast

liberia/cities.caption: Monrovia
liberia/cities.description: A capital on a peninsula between the Atlantic and the Mesurado, rebuilt and rebuilding.
liberia/cities.alt: the waterfront and low skyline of Monrovia, Liberia

liberia/crafts.caption: Masks and Country Cloth
liberia/crafts.description: Poro and Sande society masks in the interior, and woven country cloth everywhere.
liberia/crafts.alt: a carved wooden Dan mask with a smooth blackened surface, Liberia

liberia/culture.caption: Americo-Liberian and Sixteen Others
liberia/culture.description: A settler republic founded in 1822 over sixteen indigenous peoples, and the tension of that.
liberia/culture.alt: a nineteenth-century settler house with a verandah in Monrovia, Liberia

liberia/eco-tourism.caption: Forty Per Cent of What Is Left
liberia/eco-tourism.description: Liberia's forest is the largest surviving piece of the Upper Guinean block.
liberia/eco-tourism.alt: an aerial view of unbroken rainforest canopy in Liberia

liberia/family-community.caption: Kpatawee and the Coast
liberia/family-community.description: A waterfall pool inland and calm bays on the coast, both easy days out.
liberia/family-community.alt: children swimming in the pool below Kpatawee falls, Liberia

liberia/festivals.caption: Independence Day
liberia/festivals.description: 26 July, and the parades, the food and the noise that come with it.
liberia/festivals.alt: an Independence Day parade in the streets of Monrovia, Liberia

liberia/food.caption: Jollof, Palm Butter and Fufu
liberia/food.description: Palm butter soup, cassava fufu, and a jollof Liberians will argue about at length.
liberia/food.alt: a bowl of palm butter soup with rice and fish, Liberia

liberia/forests.caption: Sapo and Gola
liberia/forests.description: Two blocks of high forest, both transboundary, and the best-protected in the region.
liberia/forests.alt: mist rising off rainforest canopy at dawn in Sapo, Liberia

liberia/heritage.caption: A Republic Built by the Freed
liberia/heritage.description: Monrovia's nineteenth-century houses are the architecture of a return that did not go simply.
liberia/heritage.alt: a decaying nineteenth-century settler mansion in Monrovia, Liberia

liberia/hero.caption: Sapo
liberia/hero.description: Rainforest with pygmy hippo, forest elephant and chimpanzee, and no road into most of it.
liberia/hero.alt: closed rainforest canopy and a river in Sapo National Park, Liberia

liberia/hidden-gems.caption: Lake Piso
liberia/hidden-gems.description: A lagoon behind Robertsport with mangrove, fishing villages and no visitors.
liberia/hidden-gems.alt: fishing canoes on the still water of Lake Piso, Liberia

liberia/historic-sites.caption: Providence Island
liberia/historic-sites.description: Where the first settlers landed in 1822, in the middle of Monrovia's harbour.
liberia/historic-sites.alt: the old cotton tree and monument on Providence Island, Liberia

liberia/lakes-rivers.caption: The Saint Paul and the Cavalla
liberia/lakes-rivers.description: The Saint Paul runs past Monrovia; the Cavalla marks the whole Ivorian border.
liberia/lakes-rivers.alt: the Saint Paul river running wide through forest, Liberia

liberia/local-life.caption: The Beach at Sinkor
liberia/local-life.description: Monrovia goes to the beach bars along Sinkor at the weekend, and stays.
liberia/local-life.alt: beach bars and crowds along the shore at Sinkor, Monrovia, Liberia

liberia/luxury.caption: Beginning
liberia/luxury.description: Beach lodges at Robertsport and a few good hotels in Monrovia.
liberia/luxury.alt: a simple beach lodge under palms at Robertsport, Liberia

liberia/mountains.caption: Mount Nimba and Wologizi
liberia/mountains.description: Nimba on the Guinean border, and the Wologizi range with the highest ground in the country.
liberia/mountains.alt: the forested Wologizi range under cloud, Liberia

liberia/nature.caption: The Upper Guinean Forest
liberia/nature.description: Liberia holds about forty per cent of what is left of it.
liberia/nature.alt: buttressed rainforest trees and lianas in Liberian forest

liberia/outdoor.caption: Sapo on Foot
liberia/outdoor.description: Multi-day forest walking with rangers, sleeping in camps, and no vehicles at all.
liberia/outdoor.alt: a ranger camp under tarpaulins in Sapo rainforest, Liberia

liberia/photography.caption: Green and Water
liberia/photography.description: Sapo after rain, when the canopy drips and the light comes through in shafts.
liberia/photography.alt: shafts of light through wet rainforest canopy in Sapo, Liberia

liberia/safari.caption: Forest Tracking
liberia/safari.description: There is no game drive here. Sapo is walked, with trackers, over days.
liberia/safari.alt: a tracker on a forest path in Sapo National Park, Liberia

liberia/traditional-people.caption: Kpelle, Bassa, Grebo, Vai
liberia/traditional-people.description: The Vai invented their own script in the 1830s, one of very few in Africa.
liberia/traditional-people.alt: carved Vai script characters on a wooden board, Liberia

liberia/waterfalls.caption: Kpatawee
liberia/waterfalls.description: Falls over granite ledges into a swimmable pool in Bong county.
liberia/waterfalls.alt: the Kpatawee waterfall falling over granite into a pool, Liberia

liberia/why-visit.caption: Why Liberia
liberia/why-visit.description: The best surf in West Africa, and the forest the pygmy hippo has left.
liberia/why-visit.alt: a lone surfer walking a long empty beach at Robertsport, Liberia

liberia/wildlife.caption: The Pygmy Hippo
liberia/wildlife.description: Nocturnal, solitary, forest-dwelling, and one of the rarest large mammals in Africa.
liberia/wildlife.alt: a pygmy hippo at the edge of a forest stream at night, Liberia

libya/adventure.caption: Into the Acacus
libya/adventure.description: Four-wheel-drive expeditions of a week, camping under the arches with Tuareg guides.
libya/adventure.alt: a desert camp under a rock arch in the Acacus at night, Libya

libya/architecture.caption: Ghadames
libya/architecture.description: A covered mud-brick town where the streets are tunnels and the roofs are the women's road.
libya/architecture.alt: the whitewashed roof terraces and covered alleys of Ghadames, Libya

libya/beaches.caption: Two Thousand Kilometres of Coast
libya/beaches.description: The longest Mediterranean coastline of any African country, and almost none of it built on.
libya/beaches.alt: an empty white sand beach on the Libyan Mediterranean coast

libya/cities.caption: Tripoli and Benghazi
libya/cities.description: An Ottoman medina inside Italian arcades in Tripoli, and Benghazi rebuilding.
libya/cities.alt: the Ottoman medina and clock tower of Tripoli, Libya

libya/crafts.caption: Silver and Leather
libya/crafts.description: Tuareg silver crosses, tooled leather from Ghadames, and Berber weaving in the Nafusa.
libya/crafts.alt: a Tuareg silver cross pendant on tooled leather, Libya

libya/culture.caption: Arab, Berber, Tuareg, Tebu
libya/culture.description: Four peoples and three languages, and a coast that has been Phoenician, Greek, Roman, Ottoman and Italian.
libya/culture.alt: a busy market street in the medina of Tripoli, Libya

libya/eco-tourism.caption: What the Desert Keeps
libya/eco-tourism.description: Sand buried Leptis Magna for a thousand years, which is why there is so much of it left.
libya/eco-tourism.alt: sand drifted against the standing columns of a Roman street, Libya

libya/family-community.caption: Roman Cities Are Good for This
libya/family-community.description: Leptis is enormous, empty and safe to run around in, which not every ruin is.
libya/family-community.alt: children running along a Roman street at Leptis Magna, Libya

libya/festivals.caption: Ghat and the Desert Festivals
libya/festivals.description: The Ghat festival brings Tuareg from three countries for racing, music and poetry.
libya/festivals.alt: Tuareg riders racing camels at the Ghat festival, Libya

libya/food.caption: Bazin and Bsisa
libya/food.description: Bazin with lamb and paprika, couscous on Fridays, and shorba on the table all Ramadan.
libya/food.alt: a shared plate of Libyan bazin with lamb and sauce

libya/forests.caption: The Green Mountain
libya/forests.description: Juniper and cypress on the Jebel Akhdar, the only real forest in the country.
libya/forests.alt: juniper forest on the slopes of the Jebel Akhdar, Libya

libya/heritage.caption: Five Sites, All of Them Major
libya/heritage.description: Leptis, Sabratha, Cyrene, Ghadames and the Acacus rock art — every one on the World Heritage list.
libya/heritage.alt: prehistoric rock engravings of giraffe in the Acacus, Libya

libya/hero.caption: Leptis Magna
libya/hero.description: A Roman city of a hundred thousand people, buried by sand and dug out almost complete.
libya/hero.alt: the colonnaded forum and basilica of Leptis Magna, Libya

libya/hidden-gems.caption: Waw an Namus
libya/hidden-gems.description: A black volcanic caldera in the middle of the Sahara with green lakes at the bottom.
libya/hidden-gems.alt: the black volcanic crater and green lakes of Waw an Namus, Libya

libya/historic-sites.caption: Cyrene and Sabratha
libya/historic-sites.description: A Greek city on an escarpment above the sea, and a Roman theatre facing the water at Sabratha.
libya/historic-sites.alt: the three-storey Roman theatre at Sabratha facing the sea, Libya

libya/lakes-rivers.caption: The Ubari Lakes
libya/lakes-rivers.description: Salt lakes between dunes, the last of them dense enough to float in.
libya/lakes-rivers.alt: Gaberoun lake between high dunes in the Ubari sand sea, Libya

libya/local-life.caption: Tea, Three Times
libya/local-life.description: Poured from a height, three glasses, and no conversation is finished before the third.
libya/local-life.alt: hands pouring Libyan tea from a height into small glasses

libya/luxury.caption: Thin on the Ground
libya/luxury.description: There is very little at the top end here, and what exists is in Tripoli.
libya/luxury.alt: a restored merchant's courtyard house in Tripoli medina, Libya

libya/mountains.caption: The Acacus
libya/mountains.description: Volcanic rock arches and towers on the Algerian border, with rock art under them.
libya/mountains.alt: a natural rock arch in the Acacus mountains at sunset, Libya

libya/nature.caption: The Sand Sea and the Jebel
libya/nature.description: The Ubari sand sea in the southwest, and the green Jebel Akhdar behind Benghazi.
libya/nature.alt: dunes of the Ubari sand sea with a palm-fringed lake below, Libya

libya/outdoor.caption: The Jebel Akhdar
libya/outdoor.description: Walking on the green mountain between Greek tombs cut into the rock.
libya/outdoor.alt: a walking path past rock-cut Greek tombs on the Jebel Akhdar, Libya

libya/photography.caption: Stone and Sea
libya/photography.description: Sabratha's theatre with the Mediterranean through its arches, in the last hour of light.
libya/photography.alt: the arches of Sabratha's theatre with the sea beyond at sunset, Libya

libya/safari.caption: Tracking, Not Driving
libya/safari.description: The wildlife is thin and shy. What you go out to see is the country it survives in.
libya/safari.alt: a desert track crossing gravel plain in the Libyan Sahara

libya/traditional-people.caption: The Tuareg and the Tebu
libya/traditional-people.description: The Tuareg in the southwest around Ghat, the Tebu in the Tibesti foothills in the southeast.
libya/traditional-people.alt: a Tebu man beside a camel in southern Libya

libya/waterfalls.caption: Wadi Country
libya/waterfalls.description: No permanent rivers. The water is in wadis that run once a decade and in springs at the oases.
libya/waterfalls.alt: a spring-fed pool among palms in a Libyan desert oasis

libya/why-visit.caption: Why Libya
libya/why-visit.description: Because Leptis Magna is the best Roman city left anywhere, and hardly anyone has stood in it.
libya/why-visit.alt: a single visitor in the vast forum of Leptis Magna, Libya

libya/wildlife.caption: Desert Survivors
libya/wildlife.description: Barbary sheep in the Acacus, dorcas gazelle on the gravel plains, and very little else.
libya/wildlife.alt: a Barbary sheep on rock in the Acacus mountains, Libya

madagascar/adventure.caption: The RN7 and the Tsingy
madagascar/adventure.description: The road south through the highlands, and the limestone tsingy you cross on via ferrata.
madagascar/adventure.alt: a walker crossing the tsingy on a rope bridge, Madagascar

madagascar/architecture.caption: Highland Brick
madagascar/architecture.description: Two-storey red brick with a wooden balcony, and nothing else in Africa looks like it.
madagascar/architecture.alt: red brick highland houses with wooden balconies, Madagascar

madagascar/beaches.caption: Nosy Be and the East Coast
madagascar/beaches.description: Reef, whale sharks and humpbacks off Nosy Be, and long empty sand on the east coast.
madagascar/beaches.alt: a white sand beach and turquoise water at Nosy Be, Madagascar

madagascar/cities.caption: Antananarivo
madagascar/cities.description: A capital built up twelve hills, with stairs instead of streets in half of it.
madagascar/cities.alt: the stepped hillside houses of Antananarivo, Madagascar

madagascar/crafts.caption: Silk, Raffia and Zafimaniry
madagascar/crafts.description: Wild silk lambas, raffia work, and the Zafimaniry woodcarving of the south-east.
madagascar/crafts.alt: a woman weaving a silk lamba on a wooden loom, Madagascar

madagascar/culture.caption: Malagasy, and Eighteen Peoples
madagascar/culture.description: One language across the island, of Austronesian origin, and eighteen distinct peoples speaking it.
madagascar/culture.alt: a highland Malagasy village of red brick houses, Madagascar

madagascar/eco-tourism.caption: The Reason to Come Carefully
madagascar/eco-tourism.description: Deforestation is the country's crisis, and the parks that work are the ones the villages run.
madagascar/eco-tourism.alt: a reforestation nursery beside a Madagascar rainforest park

madagascar/family-community.caption: Slow, and Worth It
madagascar/family-community.description: Roads are slow and distances are long — but the children will hold a chameleon.
madagascar/family-community.alt: children on a village path in rural Madagascar

madagascar/festivals.caption: Hira Gasy and Donia
madagascar/festivals.description: Hira gasy troupes in the highlands, and the Donia festival on Nosy Be in June.
madagascar/festivals.alt: a hira gasy troupe performing in the highlands, Madagascar

madagascar/food.caption: Romazava and Rice
madagascar/food.description: Rice three times a day, and romazava — beef and greens — with it.
madagascar/food.alt: romazava and rice served at a Malagasy table, Madagascar

madagascar/forests.caption: Rainforest and Spiny Forest
madagascar/forests.description: Andasibe and Ranomafana in the east, and the spiny forest of the south which is like nowhere.
madagascar/forests.alt: the spiny forest of octopus trees in southern Madagascar

madagascar/heritage.caption: Pirates and Kingdoms
madagascar/heritage.description: Île Sainte-Marie's pirate cemetery, and the Merina kingdom that unified the island.
madagascar/heritage.alt: the pirate cemetery on Île Sainte-Marie, Madagascar

madagascar/hero.caption: An Island That Evolved Alone
madagascar/hero.description: Ninety per cent of what lives here lives nowhere else, because it has been on its own since the dinosaurs.
madagascar/hero.alt: the avenue of baobabs at Morondava at sunset, Madagascar

madagascar/hidden-gems.caption: Masoala
madagascar/hidden-gems.description: The largest protected rainforest in the country, reached by boat, with whales in the bay.
madagascar/hidden-gems.alt: the rainforest of Masoala coming down to the sea, Madagascar

madagascar/historic-sites.caption: The Rova and the Royal Hills
madagascar/historic-sites.description: Ambohimanga, the royal hill of the Merina kings above Antananarivo.
madagascar/historic-sites.alt: the wooden royal compound at Ambohimanga, Madagascar

madagascar/lakes-rivers.caption: The Tsiribihina
madagascar/lakes-rivers.description: Three days downriver by pirogue through country with no road in it.
madagascar/lakes-rivers.alt: a pirogue on the Tsiribihina river at dawn, Madagascar

madagascar/local-life.caption: The Zebu Market
madagascar/local-life.description: Zebu cattle are wealth here, and the markets that trade them are the real calendar.
madagascar/local-life.alt: a zebu cattle market in the Madagascar highlands

madagascar/luxury.caption: Small Lodges
madagascar/luxury.description: Owner-run lodges at the park gates, and beach places on Nosy Be with a dozen rooms.
madagascar/luxury.alt: a small lodge among trees at a Madagascar park gate

madagascar/mountains.caption: The Highlands and Maromokotro
madagascar/mountains.description: The central highlands run to two thousand metres; Maromokotro reaches 2,876 in the Tsaratanana.
madagascar/mountains.alt: terraced rice paddies in the Madagascar highlands

madagascar/nature.caption: Six Ecosystems on One Island
madagascar/nature.description: Rainforest east, highlands centre, spiny forest south, dry deciduous west, and reef all round.
madagascar/nature.alt: the tsingy limestone pinnacles of Bemaraha, Madagascar

madagascar/outdoor.caption: Trek, Paddle, Dive
madagascar/outdoor.description: Rainforest trekking, the Tsiribihina by pirogue, and reef diving off Nosy Be.
madagascar/outdoor.alt: kayaks on the water off a Madagascar reef island

madagascar/photography.caption: Baobabs at Six
madagascar/photography.description: The avenue at Morondava for twenty minutes at either end of the day, and nothing else like it.
madagascar/photography.alt: baobabs silhouetted against the sky at Morondava, Madagascar

madagascar/safari.caption: Not a Safari Island
madagascar/safari.description: No lions and no elephant — the wildlife here is small, nocturnal, and worth the torchlight.
madagascar/safari.alt: a chameleon on a branch in Ranomafana rainforest, Madagascar

madagascar/traditional-people.caption: Famadihana and the Ancestors
madagascar/traditional-people.description: The ancestors are present here in a way that shapes the calendar and the architecture.
madagascar/traditional-people.alt: a family tomb standing in highland Madagascar farmland

madagascar/waterfalls.caption: The Eastern Escarpment
madagascar/waterfalls.description: Short, steep rivers off the escarpment, and waterfalls through the rainforest at Andasibe.
madagascar/waterfalls.alt: a waterfall in rainforest on the eastern escarpment, Madagascar

madagascar/why-visit.caption: Nowhere Else
madagascar/why-visit.description: Lemurs, baobabs, tsingy, spiny forest — none of it exists anywhere else on earth.
madagascar/why-visit.alt: a ring-tailed lemur troop in southern Madagascar

madagascar/wildlife.caption: A Hundred Kinds of Lemur
madagascar/wildlife.description: A hundred and seven species and subspecies of lemur, every one of them endemic.
madagascar/wildlife.alt: an indri lemur in the rainforest canopy at Andasibe, Madagascar

malawi/adventure.caption: Diving, Kayak and the Massif
malawi/adventure.description: Freshwater diving on the cichlid reefs, kayaking the lake shore, and Mulanje for a week.
malawi/adventure.alt: kayakers paddling along the rocky shore of Lake Malawi

malawi/architecture.caption: Mission Stone and Lakeshore Brick
malawi/architecture.description: Scottish mission churches in stone, and fired brick along the lake.
malawi/architecture.alt: the stone facade of the Blantyre mission church, Malawi

malawi/beaches.caption: Freshwater Beaches
malawi/beaches.description: Landlocked, and it does not matter: Cape Maclear, Nkhata Bay and Likoma have sand and clear water.
malawi/beaches.alt: a beach and clear water at Nkhata Bay on Lake Malawi

malawi/cities.caption: Lilongwe and Blantyre
malawi/cities.description: A quiet capital, and an older commercial city with the country's first church in it.
malawi/cities.alt: the market and streets of Blantyre, Malawi

malawi/crafts.caption: Carving and Chitenje
malawi/crafts.description: Blackwood carving, basketry, and the printed chitenje cloth worn everywhere.
malawi/crafts.alt: printed chitenje cloth stacked at a market stall, Malawi

malawi/culture.caption: The Warm Heart
malawi/culture.description: The reputation for friendliness is real, and it is the first thing every visitor mentions.
malawi/culture.alt: people talking at a lakeside village market in Malawi

malawi/eco-tourism.caption: Majete's Recovery
malawi/eco-tourism.description: African Parks took on an empty park in 2003 and it has the big five and no poaching now.
malawi/eco-tourism.alt: a ranger and vehicle at a waterhole in Majete, Malawi

malawi/family-community.caption: Easy, and Warm
malawi/family-community.description: Short distances, no malaria-free claim but a very manageable country with children.
malawi/family-community.alt: children swimming from a beach on Lake Malawi

malawi/festivals.caption: The Lake of Stars
malawi/festivals.description: A music festival on the shore, and Gule Wamkulu in the villages all year.
malawi/festivals.alt: a crowd at a music festival on the shore of Lake Malawi

malawi/food.caption: Nsima and Chambo
malawi/food.description: Nsima with relish, and chambo — a lake cichlid — grilled whole on the shore.
malawi/food.alt: a grilled chambo fish served with nsima, Malawi

malawi/forests.caption: Nyika and Zomba
malawi/forests.description: Montane grassland on Nyika at two thousand metres, and cedar forest on the Zomba plateau.
malawi/forests.alt: rolling montane grassland and pines on the Nyika plateau, Malawi

malawi/heritage.caption: Lake Malawi National Park
malawi/heritage.description: The first freshwater national park in the world, listed for its cichlids.
malawi/heritage.alt: granite boulders and clear shallow water in Lake Malawi National Park

malawi/hero.caption: The Lake
malawi/hero.description: Five hundred kilometres of it, and more fish species than any other lake in the world.
malawi/hero.alt: the clear water and rocky shore of Lake Malawi at Cape Maclear

malawi/hidden-gems.caption: Likoma Island
malawi/hidden-gems.description: A Malawian island inside Mozambican water, with a cathedral the size of Winchester's.
malawi/hidden-gems.alt: the large Anglican cathedral standing over Likoma island, Malawi

malawi/historic-sites.caption: Livingstonia
malawi/historic-sites.description: A mission on the escarpment built in 1894, with the manse, the church and the view intact.
malawi/historic-sites.alt: the stone church and manse of Livingstonia on the escarpment, Malawi

malawi/lakes-rivers.caption: The Shire
malawi/lakes-rivers.description: The lake's only outlet, running south through Liwonde to the Zambezi.
malawi/lakes-rivers.alt: the Shire river with hippos and reedbeds in Liwonde, Malawi

malawi/local-life.caption: The Beach at Cape Maclear
malawi/local-life.description: Fishermen, boats, children and visitors on the same strip of sand all day.
malawi/local-life.alt: fishing boats and children on the beach at Cape Maclear, Malawi

malawi/luxury.caption: Small and Well Run
malawi/luxury.description: Lakeshore lodges, Mkulumadzi at Majete, and Kaya Mawa on Likoma island.
malawi/luxury.alt: a lakeside lodge deck over clear water at dusk, Malawi

malawi/mountains.caption: Mulanje
malawi/mountains.description: 3,002 metres at Sapitwa, a granite massif with huts, paths and a week of walking on it.
malawi/mountains.alt: the granite peaks and plateaux of the Mulanje massif, Malawi

malawi/nature.caption: The Rift and the Massif
malawi/nature.description: The Rift Valley floor with the lake in it, and Mulanje standing three thousand metres above the tea.
malawi/nature.alt: the Mulanje massif rising abruptly above tea estates, Malawi

malawi/outdoor.caption: Mulanje for a Week
malawi/outdoor.description: Hut to hut across the massif, with porters, and paths that have been there a century.
malawi/outdoor.alt: walkers crossing a plateau on the Mulanje massif, Malawi

malawi/photography.caption: Clear Water and Granite
malawi/photography.description: The lake in September, when the water is at its clearest and the boulders go down twenty metres.
malawi/photography.alt: clear blue water over granite boulders in Lake Malawi

malawi/safari.caption: Liwonde and Majete
malawi/safari.description: Both restocked from near-empty — Majete had nothing in 2003 and has the big five now.
malawi/safari.alt: elephants on the Shire river bank in Liwonde, Malawi

malawi/traditional-people.caption: Chewa, Yao, Tumbuka, Lomwe
malawi/traditional-people.description: The Chewa Gule Wamkulu masquerade is on the UNESCO list and is danced still.
malawi/traditional-people.alt: Gule Wamkulu masked dancers performing in a village, Malawi

malawi/waterfalls.caption: Manchewe
malawi/waterfalls.description: Off the Nyika escarpment near Livingstonia, with a cave behind the water.
malawi/waterfalls.alt: the Manchewe falls dropping off the escarpment near Livingstonia, Malawi

malawi/why-visit.caption: Why Malawi
malawi/why-visit.description: A lake with more fish species than any other on earth, and parks brought back from nothing.
malawi/why-visit.alt: a dhow under sail on Lake Malawi at sunset

malawi/wildlife.caption: Cichlids, and the Big Five
malawi/wildlife.description: Hundreds of endemic cichlids in the lake, and the big five back in the parks on shore.
malawi/wildlife.alt: brightly coloured mbuna cichlids over rocks in Lake Malawi

mali/adventure.caption: Walking the Dogon Country
mali/adventure.description: Village to village along the escarpment, sleeping on roofs, four days or fourteen.
mali/adventure.alt: walkers on a path below the Bandiagara cliff at first light, Mali

mali/architecture.caption: Sudano-Sahelian
mali/architecture.description: Mud walls, projecting palm beams, and buttressed towers — a style that belongs to this river.
mali/architecture.alt: the buttressed mud facade and wooden beams of a Sahelian mosque, Mali

mali/beaches.caption: River Sand, Not Sea
mali/beaches.description: Landlocked — the beaches here are sandbars on the Niger, and people swim off them.
mali/beaches.alt: a sandbar and shallow water on the Niger river at low season, Mali

mali/cities.caption: Bamako and Mopti
mali/cities.description: A capital sprawling both sides of the Niger, and a port town built on three islands.
mali/cities.alt: the Niger riverfront and pirogues at Mopti, Mali

mali/crafts.caption: Bogolan and Bamana Sculpture
mali/crafts.description: Mud-dyed bogolanfini cloth, Bamana chiwara antelope crests, and Dogon carved doors.
mali/crafts.alt: a length of mud-dyed bogolan cloth in black and ochre, Mali

mali/culture.caption: Where the Blues Came From
mali/culture.description: Ali Farka Toure, Toumani Diabate, Salif Keita and Tinariwen are all from here.
mali/culture.alt: a kora player performing at an evening gathering in Bamako, Mali

mali/eco-tourism.caption: Re-Plastering Djenne
mali/eco-tourism.description: Every year the town rebuilds the mosque's surface by hand in a single day.
mali/eco-tourism.alt: the whole town plastering the Great Mosque of Djenne by hand, Mali

mali/family-community.caption: Hard Country for It
mali/family-community.description: The security situation makes most of Mali unvisitable at present, and that is the honest answer.
mali/family-community.alt: children playing in a village square in southern Mali

mali/festivals.caption: The Sigui and the Dama
mali/festivals.description: Dogon masked ceremonies, the Sigui every sixty years and the Dama for the dead.
mali/festivals.alt: Dogon dancers in tall kanaga masks in a village square, Mali

mali/food.caption: Tigadege Na and Capitaine
mali/food.description: Groundnut stew, and Nile perch grilled whole on the riverbank at Mopti.
mali/food.alt: grilled capitaine fish with rice and onion sauce on a plate, Mali

mali/forests.caption: The Gallery Forest
mali/forests.description: Ribbons of woodland along the river, and the baobabs standing alone on the plain behind.
mali/forests.alt: a large baobab standing alone on Sahelian grassland, Mali

mali/heritage.caption: Four Sites, All at Risk
mali/heritage.description: Djenne, Timbuktu, Bandiagara and the Tomb of Askia — every one of them on the danger list.
mali/heritage.alt: the stepped pyramid tomb of Askia at Gao, Mali

mali/hero.caption: The Great Mosque of Djenne
mali/hero.description: The largest mud-brick building in the world, re-plastered by the whole town every spring.
mali/hero.alt: the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne with its wooden toron beams, Mali

mali/hidden-gems.caption: The Tomb of Askia
mali/hidden-gems.description: A pyramid of mud at Gao, built in 1495 for the emperor of Songhai.
mali/hidden-gems.alt: the mud pyramid tomb of Askia at Gao with wooden beams, Mali

mali/historic-sites.caption: Timbuktu
mali/historic-sites.description: Three mud mosques, and a library tradition that ran to hundreds of thousands of manuscripts.
mali/historic-sites.alt: the mud-brick Sankore mosque in Timbuktu, Mali

mali/lakes-rivers.caption: The Niger and Lake Debo
mali/lakes-rivers.description: Pinasses working the river between Mopti and Timbuktu, and the inland delta spreading behind them.
mali/lakes-rivers.alt: a loaded pinasse under sail on the Niger near Mopti, Mali

mali/local-life.caption: Monday Market at Djenne
mali/local-life.description: The whole delta comes to the square in front of the mosque, once a week.
mali/local-life.alt: the Monday market crowd in front of the Great Mosque of Djenne, Mali

mali/luxury.caption: Almost None
mali/luxury.description: A handful of hotels in Bamako. The rest of the country is guesthouses and roofs.
mali/luxury.alt: a courtyard hotel with mud walls in Bamako, Mali

mali/mountains.caption: The Bandiagara Escarpment
mali/mountains.description: A hundred and fifty kilometres of sandstone cliff, with villages built into the face of it.
mali/mountains.alt: Dogon villages built into the cliff face of the Bandiagara escarpment, Mali

mali/nature.caption: The Niger Bend
mali/nature.description: The river runs north into the Sahara, thinks better of it, and turns southeast.
mali/nature.alt: the Niger river curving broad and brown through Sahelian scrub, Mali

mali/outdoor.caption: The Escarpment on Foot
mali/outdoor.description: The Dogon country is walking country, and always has been.
mali/outdoor.alt: a narrow path climbing between rocks on the Bandiagara escarpment, Mali

mali/photography.caption: Mud and Long Shadows
mali/photography.description: Djenne an hour before sunset, when the toron beams throw stripes down the wall.
mali/photography.alt: low sun on the mud wall and projecting beams of Djenne's mosque, Mali

mali/safari.caption: Not the Business Here
mali/safari.description: There is no lodge circuit. The Gourma elephants are a conservation story, not a game drive.
mali/safari.alt: acacia and dry grassland in the Gourma with a waterhole, Mali

mali/traditional-people.caption: Dogon, Bambara, Tuareg, Fulani
mali/traditional-people.description: Dogon on the escarpment, Bambara on the river, Tuareg and Fulani on the plains north of it.
mali/traditional-people.alt: a Dogon elder outside a granary with a carved door, Mali

mali/waterfalls.caption: Falls at Woroni
mali/waterfalls.description: Small falls on the sandstone plateau above Bandiagara, running only after the rains.
mali/waterfalls.alt: a seasonal waterfall over sandstone on the Dogon plateau, Mali

mali/why-visit.caption: Why Mali
mali/why-visit.description: Because Djenne, Timbuktu and the Dogon country are three of the great sights of Africa.
mali/why-visit.alt: a lone figure in front of the Great Mosque of Djenne, Mali

mali/wildlife.caption: Elephants in the Gourma
mali/wildlife.description: The Gourma herd makes the longest elephant migration in Africa, on a loop into Burkina Faso.
mali/wildlife.alt: desert-adapted elephants crossing dry Sahelian scrub in the Gourma, Mali

mauritania/adventure.caption: Riding the Ore Train
mauritania/adventure.description: Twenty hours in the open on top of iron ore, in the cold, and people do it on purpose.
mauritania/adventure.alt: passengers sitting on top of iron ore wagons in the desert, Mauritania

mauritania/architecture.caption: Dry Stone and Sand
mauritania/architecture.description: Ksour built of flat stone without mortar, and streets that the dunes are taking back.
mauritania/architecture.alt: a dry-stone street and doorway in Ouadane, Mauritania

mauritania/beaches.caption: Seven Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
mauritania/beaches.description: Cold current, big surf, and the Imraguen fishing villages working with dolphins.
mauritania/beaches.alt: Imraguen fishermen hauling nets on the Mauritanian Atlantic shore

mauritania/cities.caption: Nouakchott and Nouadhibou
mauritania/cities.description: A capital built from nothing in 1958, and a port with the world's biggest ship graveyard.
mauritania/cities.alt: the fish market and painted pirogues on the beach at Nouakchott, Mauritania

mauritania/crafts.caption: Silver, Leather and Chests
mauritania/crafts.description: Moorish silver, tooled leather cushions, and the painted wooden chests of the Adrar.
mauritania/crafts.alt: a painted Mauritanian wooden chest with metalwork corners

mauritania/culture.caption: Moor and Fulani
mauritania/culture.description: Bidhan and Haratin Moors across the north, Fulani, Soninke and Wolof along the river.
mauritania/culture.alt: men in blue boubous drinking tea on a mat in the desert, Mauritania

mauritania/eco-tourism.caption: Two Million Birds
mauritania/eco-tourism.description: The Banc d'Arguin is a Ramsar site and one of the most important wintering grounds on earth.
mauritania/eco-tourism.alt: dense flocks of waders on the mudflats of the Banc d'Arguin, Mauritania

mauritania/family-community.caption: Big Country for Small Children
mauritania/family-community.description: Distances are long and facilities are few. Better for teenagers than for toddlers.
mauritania/family-community.alt: children playing among date palms in an Adrar oasis, Mauritania

mauritania/festivals.caption: The Chinguetti Festival
mauritania/festivals.description: Poetry, camel racing and manuscript readings in the old caravan town.
mauritania/festivals.alt: camel racing at a festival outside Chinguetti, Mauritania

mauritania/food.caption: Thieboudienne and Three Teas
mauritania/food.description: Fish and rice from the river south, and the three-glass tea ceremony everywhere.
mauritania/food.alt: three small glasses of Mauritanian tea poured from a height

mauritania/forests.caption: The Palmeraies
mauritania/forests.description: Date palm groves in the Adrar canyons — the only shade for hundreds of kilometres.
mauritania/forests.alt: a dense date palm grove in a canyon at Terjit, Mauritania

mauritania/heritage.caption: The Manuscript Libraries
mauritania/heritage.description: Family libraries in Chinguetti holding astronomy, law and poetry from the middle ages.
mauritania/heritage.alt: an open medieval manuscript in a family library at Chinguetti, Mauritania

mauritania/hero.caption: The Iron Ore Train
mauritania/hero.description: Two and a half kilometres long, twenty hours across the desert, and you can ride the ore.
mauritania/hero.alt: the iron ore train crossing the Sahara at sunset in Mauritania

mauritania/hidden-gems.caption: Terjit
mauritania/hidden-gems.description: A hot spring under palms in a narrow gorge, and the best shade in the country.
mauritania/hidden-gems.alt: a spring pool under dense palms in the Terjit gorge, Mauritania

mauritania/historic-sites.caption: Chinguetti and Ouadane
mauritania/historic-sites.description: Twelfth-century caravan towns in dry stone, half-buried by the dunes now.
mauritania/historic-sites.alt: the dry-stone houses and minaret of Chinguetti under encroaching sand, Mauritania

mauritania/lakes-rivers.caption: The Senegal River
mauritania/lakes-rivers.description: The southern border, and the only permanent river in the country.
mauritania/lakes-rivers.alt: the Senegal river with farmland on its bank at Rosso, Mauritania

mauritania/local-life.caption: The Fish Market at Sunset
mauritania/local-life.description: The pirogues come in at Nouakchott beach and the whole catch is sold on the sand.
mauritania/local-life.alt: crowds buying fish from pirogues on the beach at Nouakchott, Mauritania

mauritania/luxury.caption: Small and Serious
mauritania/luxury.description: Auberges in Atar and Chinguetti run by people who know the desert, and little else.
mauritania/luxury.alt: a courtyard auberge with mats and cushions in Chinguetti, Mauritania

mauritania/mountains.caption: The Kediet ej Jill
mauritania/mountains.description: 915 metres of magnetite near Zouerat, so iron-rich it deflects a compass.
mauritania/mountains.alt: the dark iron mountain of Kediet ej Jill above desert, Mauritania

mauritania/nature.caption: The Adrar
mauritania/nature.description: A sandstone plateau cut by palm-filled canyons, with the old caravan towns in them.
mauritania/nature.alt: a palm-filled canyon below sandstone cliffs in the Adrar, Mauritania

mauritania/outdoor.caption: Trekking the Adrar
mauritania/outdoor.description: Camel treks between the ksour, days at a time, sleeping out on the sand.
mauritania/outdoor.alt: a camel trek crossing dunes in the Adrar at dusk, Mauritania

mauritania/photography.caption: Sand Against Stone
mauritania/photography.description: Chinguetti in the last hour, when the dunes in the streets are lit from the side.
mauritania/photography.alt: low sun on sand drifted against the dry-stone walls of Chinguetti, Mauritania

mauritania/safari.caption: Desert, Not Savanna
mauritania/safari.description: The wildlife is birds and desert-adapted mammals, and the coast is where it concentrates.
mauritania/safari.alt: a dorcas gazelle on gravel plain in the Mauritanian desert

mauritania/traditional-people.caption: The Imraguen
mauritania/traditional-people.description: A coastal people who fish with lanchas and, by tradition, with the help of dolphins.
mauritania/traditional-people.alt: an Imraguen lancha under sail off the Banc d'Arguin, Mauritania

mauritania/waterfalls.caption: Guelta de Matmata
mauritania/waterfalls.description: Permanent pools in the rock south of Atar, with crocodiles that have been there since the Sahara was wet.
mauritania/waterfalls.alt: a permanent rock pool with palms in the Mauritanian desert

mauritania/why-visit.caption: Why Mauritania
mauritania/why-visit.description: A medieval library in a sand-buried town, and a train you ride on the ore.
mauritania/why-visit.alt: a lone figure walking a sand-filled street in Ouadane, Mauritania

mauritania/wildlife.caption: The Banc d'Arguin
mauritania/wildlife.description: Two million wading birds winter here, on the largest tidal flats in West Africa.
mauritania/wildlife.alt: flamingos and waders on the tidal flats of the Banc d'Arguin, Mauritania

mauritius/adventure.caption: Kite, Dive, Hike
mauritius/adventure.description: Kitesurfing at Le Morne, diving the outer reef, and hiking the gorges and the mountains.
mauritius/adventure.alt: kitesurfers on the lagoon below Le Morne, Mauritius

mauritius/architecture.caption: Colonial and Estate
mauritius/architecture.description: The plantation houses of the interior, and the colonial buildings of Port Louis.
mauritius/architecture.alt: a colonial plantation house with a wide veranda, Mauritius

mauritius/beaches.caption: The Lagoon
mauritius/beaches.description: Inside the reef the water is flat and warm the whole way round the island.
mauritius/beaches.alt: turquoise lagoon and reef break off a Mauritian beach, Mauritius

mauritius/cities.caption: Port Louis
mauritius/cities.description: A working port and capital, with a market, a waterfront and the Champ de Mars.
mauritius/cities.alt: the Port Louis waterfront and market, Mauritius

mauritius/crafts.caption: Model Ships and Textiles
mauritius/crafts.description: Model shipbuilding, and a textile industry that grew out of the sugar estates.
mauritius/crafts.alt: a model ship being built in a Mauritian workshop, Mauritius

mauritius/culture.caption: Four Continents
mauritius/culture.description: Indian, African, French and Chinese, in one Creole language and one calendar.
mauritius/culture.alt: a Hindu temple and a church on the same Mauritian street, Mauritius

mauritius/eco-tourism.caption: Bringing Back the Birds
mauritius/eco-tourism.description: The kestrel, the pink pigeon and the echo parakeet were each brought back from near zero.
mauritius/eco-tourism.alt: a pink pigeon in Mauritian native forest, Mauritius

mauritius/family-community.caption: Made for Families
mauritius/family-community.description: Flat warm lagoon, no dangerous surf inside the reef, and short drives from anywhere.
mauritius/family-community.alt: children playing in a calm Mauritian lagoon, Mauritius

mauritius/festivals.caption: Maha Shivaratri and Cavadee
mauritius/festivals.description: Half a million walking to Grand Bassin in February, and Thaipoosam Cavadee in January.
mauritius/festivals.alt: pilgrims walking to Grand Bassin at Maha Shivaratri, Mauritius

mauritius/food.caption: Dholl Puri and Rougaille
mauritius/food.description: Dholl puri off a street cart, rougaille at home, and a fish vindaye that is entirely local.
mauritius/food.alt: dholl puri being made at a street cart, Mauritius

mauritius/forests.caption: Black River Gorges
mauritius/forests.description: The last of the native forest, on the plateau, with trails and endemic birds in it.
mauritius/forests.alt: native forest in the Black River Gorges, Mauritius

mauritius/heritage.caption: Le Morne
mauritius/heritage.description: The mountain where escaped slaves lived at the top, and a world heritage site for that reason.
mauritius/heritage.alt: Le Morne Brabant seen from the lagoon, Mauritius

mauritius/hero.caption: Reef, Sugar and the Volcanic Interior
mauritius/hero.description: A ring of reef, a green interior of sugar and mountain, and four cultures on one island.
mauritius/hero.alt: the mountain of Le Morne rising above the lagoon, Mauritius

mauritius/hidden-gems.caption: Rodrigues
mauritius/hidden-gems.description: Six hundred kilometres east, a tenth the size, and the island Mauritius used to be.
mauritius/hidden-gems.alt: the hills and lagoon of Rodrigues island, Mauritius

mauritius/historic-sites.caption: Aapravasi Ghat
mauritius/historic-sites.description: The immigration depot where half a million indentured labourers first landed.
mauritius/historic-sites.alt: the stone steps of the Aapravasi Ghat, Mauritius

mauritius/lakes-rivers.caption: Grand Bassin
mauritius/lakes-rivers.description: A crater lake and Hindu pilgrimage site, with half a million people walking to it at Maha Shivaratri.
mauritius/lakes-rivers.alt: the temple and statues at Grand Bassin crater lake, Mauritius

mauritius/local-life.caption: The Central Market
mauritius/local-life.description: Port Louis market in the morning, for vegetables, tea and alouda.
mauritius/local-life.alt: the vegetable stalls of Port Louis central market, Mauritius

mauritius/luxury.caption: The Resort Standard
mauritius/luxury.description: The island effectively invented the Indian Ocean resort, and it still does it best.
mauritius/luxury.alt: a resort beach and lagoon in the late afternoon, Mauritius

mauritius/mountains.caption: Le Morne and Pieter Both
mauritius/mountains.description: Le Morne Brabant stands 556 metres out of the lagoon, and is walked in a morning.
mauritius/mountains.alt: the summit ridge of Le Morne Brabant above the sea, Mauritius

mauritius/nature.caption: Lagoon and Gorge
mauritius/nature.description: Lagoon all the way round, sugar cane across the plain, and gorges cut into the plateau.
mauritius/nature.alt: the Black River gorges in morning cloud, Mauritius

mauritius/outdoor.caption: Kite, Hike, Dive
mauritius/outdoor.description: Le Morne's kite lagoon, the Black River trails, and dive sites outside the reef.
mauritius/outdoor.alt: hikers on the trail up Le Morne, Mauritius

mauritius/photography.caption: Lagoon Colour
mauritius/photography.description: The lagoon changes colour every hundred metres, and the aerial work here is the proof.
mauritius/photography.alt: aerial view of a Mauritian lagoon and reef, Mauritius

mauritius/safari.caption: Reef, Not Savanna
mauritius/safari.description: No big game — the wildlife here is the reef, the endemic birds, and the flying foxes at dusk.
mauritius/safari.alt: fruit bats leaving a roost at dusk, Mauritius

mauritius/traditional-people.caption: Creole and Bhojpuri
mauritius/traditional-people.description: Creole spoken by everyone, Bhojpuri in the villages, and French and English in print.
mauritius/traditional-people.alt: a village street in the Mauritian sugar country, Mauritius

mauritius/waterfalls.caption: Chamarel
mauritius/waterfalls.description: A hundred metres in a single drop, near the seven-coloured earths.
mauritius/waterfalls.alt: the Chamarel waterfall dropping into forest, Mauritius

mauritius/why-visit.caption: Four Cultures, One Lagoon
mauritius/why-visit.description: A Hindu festival, a Creole kitchen, a French road name and a Chinese shop, in one street.
mauritius/why-visit.alt: a busy multicultural street scene in Port Louis, Mauritius

mauritius/wildlife.caption: What the Dodo Left
mauritius/wildlife.description: The dodo is gone, but the pink pigeon and the kestrel were both brought back from single figures.
mauritius/wildlife.alt: a Mauritius kestrel perched in native forest

morocco/adventure.caption: Dunes, Gorges and Surf
morocco/adventure.description: Trekking in the Atlas, surfing the Atlantic points, and a night out on the erg at Chegaga.
morocco/adventure.alt: a trekking trail high on a ridge in the High Atlas, Morocco

morocco/architecture.caption: Riad and Medina
morocco/architecture.description: Rooms built inward around a courtyard, because the street was never meant to see in.
morocco/architecture.alt: the tiled courtyard of a traditional Moroccan riad, Morocco

morocco/beaches.caption: The Atlantic Coast
morocco/beaches.description: Essaouira's wind, Taghazout's point breaks, and the long empty beaches between them.
morocco/beaches.alt: the walled seafront of Essaouira with fishing boats, Morocco

morocco/cities.caption: Marrakesh and Casablanca
morocco/cities.description: Jemaa el-Fnaa at dusk, and the Atlantic modernism of Casablanca an hour up the road.
morocco/cities.alt: Jemaa el-Fnaa square in Marrakesh filling at dusk, Morocco

morocco/crafts.caption: Zellige, Leather and Wool
morocco/crafts.description: Tile cut by hand in Fez, tanned leather, and carpets woven to patterns held in memory.
morocco/crafts.alt: a craftsman cutting zellige tile by hand in Fez, Morocco

morocco/culture.caption: Amazigh and Arab
morocco/culture.description: Three Amazigh languages, Arabic, French and Spanish, and a culture that predates all of them.
morocco/culture.alt: an Amazigh village of earth houses built into a hillside, Morocco

morocco/eco-tourism.caption: Oasis Agriculture
morocco/eco-tourism.description: The khettara irrigation channels still working, and the argan cooperatives run by women.
morocco/eco-tourism.alt: a palm oasis irrigated by traditional channels, Morocco

morocco/family-community.caption: Easy Travelling
morocco/family-community.description: Short drives, good roads, and a train line down the coast that children enjoy.
morocco/family-community.alt: a family walking a quiet lane in a Moroccan hill village, Morocco

morocco/festivals.caption: Moussem and Gnaoua
morocco/festivals.description: The Gnaoua festival in Essaouira in June, and the moussems that mark the harvest.
morocco/festivals.alt: musicians playing at the Gnaoua festival in Essaouira, Morocco

morocco/food.caption: Tagine, Bread and Mint
morocco/food.description: Slow-cooked tagine, bread baked in the neighbourhood oven, and tea poured from height.
morocco/food.alt: a tagine cooking over charcoal at a roadside stall, Morocco

morocco/forests.caption: The Cedar Forest
morocco/forests.description: The Middle Atlas cedar, some of it a thousand years old, above Ifrane and Azrou.
morocco/forests.alt: ancient Atlas cedar trees in the Middle Atlas forest, Morocco

morocco/heritage.caption: The Imperial Cities
morocco/heritage.description: Fez, Marrakesh, Meknes and Rabat — four capitals, each of a different dynasty.
morocco/heritage.alt: the tanneries and rooftops of the Fez medina, Morocco

morocco/hero.caption: Where the Atlas Meets the Sahara
morocco/hero.description: Snow on the High Atlas in the morning and the first dunes of the Sahara by evening.
morocco/hero.alt: the High Atlas mountains rising behind a Moroccan kasbah, Morocco

morocco/hidden-gems.caption: Chefchaouen and the Rif
morocco/hidden-gems.description: The blue town in the Rif, and a mountain range most itineraries drive straight past.
morocco/hidden-gems.alt: the blue-painted lanes of Chefchaouen in the Rif, Morocco

morocco/historic-sites.caption: Volubilis and the Kasbahs
morocco/historic-sites.description: A Roman city on the plain at Volubilis, and Ait Benhaddou standing above the Ounila.
morocco/historic-sites.alt: the earth kasbah of Ait Benhaddou above the river, Morocco

morocco/lakes-rivers.caption: The Draa River
morocco/lakes-rivers.description: The longest river in Morocco, mostly dry, and green the whole way where it is not.
morocco/lakes-rivers.alt: palm groves along the Draa valley in southern Morocco

morocco/local-life.caption: The Souk in the Morning
morocco/local-life.description: Before the tour groups, the medina is simply where people buy their vegetables.
morocco/local-life.alt: a produce market in a Moroccan medina early in the morning, Morocco

morocco/luxury.caption: Desert Camps and Riads
morocco/luxury.description: Erg Chigaga camps well beyond the day-trip dunes, and riads restored room by room.
morocco/luxury.alt: a desert camp of tents on the dunes at Erg Chigaga, Morocco

morocco/mountains.caption: The High Atlas
morocco/mountains.description: Toubkal is 4,167 metres and the highest point in North Africa, walkable in two days from Imlil.
morocco/mountains.alt: Mount Toubkal under snow above the village of Imlil, Morocco

morocco/nature.caption: The Draa and the Dades
morocco/nature.description: Palm oases strung along the Draa, and gorges cut red through the Dades and the Todra.
morocco/nature.alt: the Todra gorge with red rock walls and a river below, Morocco

morocco/outdoor.caption: Trek, Surf, Ride
morocco/outdoor.description: Multi-day Atlas treks, Atlantic surf schools, and horses on the Essaouira sand.
morocco/outdoor.alt: surfers walking the beach at Taghazout at sunset, Morocco

morocco/photography.caption: Light on Earth Walls
morocco/photography.description: Pisé takes late light the way nothing else does, which is why every photographer comes here.
morocco/photography.alt: late light on the earth walls of a southern Moroccan kasbah, Morocco

morocco/safari.caption: Desert Country
morocco/safari.description: Not the safari of the east — the wildlife here is desert-adapted, and you look for it at first light.
morocco/safari.alt: a desert track through stony hammada in southern Morocco

morocco/traditional-people.caption: The People of the Atlas
morocco/traditional-people.description: Village life at two thousand metres, where the year is still organised around the snow.
morocco/traditional-people.alt: a shepherd with his flock on a High Atlas terrace, Morocco

morocco/waterfalls.caption: Ouzoud
morocco/waterfalls.description: A hundred metres of water in three stages, with macaques in the olive trees beside it.
morocco/waterfalls.alt: the Ouzoud falls dropping in stages through olive trees, Morocco

morocco/why-visit.caption: Two Days, Four Climates
morocco/why-visit.description: Surf in the morning, cedar forest by lunch, and the Sahara the following evening.
morocco/why-visit.alt: a road climbing a High Atlas pass with the Sahara beyond, Morocco

morocco/wildlife.caption: Barbary Macaques and the Argan Forest
morocco/wildlife.description: Macaques in the cedar forest above Azrou, and goats standing in the argan trees near Essaouira.
morocco/wildlife.alt: Barbary macaques in the cedar forest of the Middle Atlas, Morocco

mozambique/adventure.caption: Dive, Sail, Kayak
mozambique/adventure.description: Manta and whale shark at Tofo, dhow safaris in the Quirimbas, and kayaks in the mangrove.
mozambique/adventure.alt: a diver with a manta ray off Tofo, Mozambique

mozambique/architecture.caption: Coral Stone and Colonial
mozambique/architecture.description: Coral rag on the islands, and Portuguese modernism through Maputo and Beira.
mozambique/architecture.alt: a colonial-era building in Maputo with modernist lines, Mozambique

mozambique/beaches.caption: Bazaruto and the Quirimbas
mozambique/beaches.description: Dune islands in the south, coral islands in the north, and dhows between them.
mozambique/beaches.alt: the sand dunes and turquoise water of Bazaruto, Mozambique

mozambique/cities.caption: Maputo
mozambique/cities.description: Wide avenues, a Mediterranean seafront, and the market Eiffel's company built.
mozambique/cities.alt: the Maputo waterfront and the Indian Ocean, Mozambique

mozambique/crafts.caption: Carving and Basketry
mozambique/crafts.description: Makonde blackwood carving, and the palm basketry of the northern islands.
mozambique/crafts.alt: Makonde blackwood carvings on a workshop bench, Mozambique

mozambique/culture.caption: Portuguese and Swahili
mozambique/culture.description: Five hundred years of Portuguese on a Swahili coast, and a culture made from both.
mozambique/culture.alt: the coral-stone lanes of Ilha de Moçambique, Mozambique

mozambique/eco-tourism.caption: Gorongosa's Restoration
mozambique/eco-tourism.description: Local employment, local science, and a park brought back from nothing — worth understanding.
mozambique/eco-tourism.alt: a park scientist at work in Gorongosa, Mozambique

mozambique/family-community.caption: Warm Water All Year
mozambique/family-community.description: Shallow, warm and calm inside the reef — as easy a sea as the continent offers.
mozambique/family-community.alt: children swimming in shallow water inside a reef, Mozambique

mozambique/festivals.caption: Marrabenta and Timbila
mozambique/festivals.description: Marrabenta on the coast, and the Chopi timbila orchestras of Inhambane.
mozambique/festivals.alt: a Chopi timbila orchestra performing, Mozambique

mozambique/food.caption: Peri-Peri and Matapa
mozambique/food.description: Prawns with peri-peri, and matapa — cassava leaf and coconut — with rice.
mozambique/food.alt: grilled prawns with peri-peri at a beach kitchen, Mozambique

mozambique/forests.caption: Coastal Forest
mozambique/forests.description: The coastal dry forest of the north, and the mangrove that lines most of the delta.
mozambique/forests.alt: mangrove forest along a northern Mozambique estuary

mozambique/heritage.caption: The Swahili Coast
mozambique/heritage.description: Ibo, Angoche and Sofala — Indian Ocean trading towns older than the Portuguese.
mozambique/heritage.alt: the crumbling colonial buildings of Ibo island, Mozambique

mozambique/hero.caption: Two Thousand Kilometres of Coast
