mozambique/hero.description: Reef, dune and island for the whole length of the country, and warm water all year.
mozambique/hero.alt: a dhow sailing off a Mozambican island at sunrise, Mozambique

mozambique/hidden-gems.caption: Ibo Island
mozambique/hidden-gems.description: Silversmiths, a fort, mangrove channels, and about as far from a resort as it gets.
mozambique/hidden-gems.alt: a silversmith working inside the fort on Ibo island, Mozambique

mozambique/historic-sites.caption: Ilha de Moçambique
mozambique/historic-sites.description: The old capital, on a coral island a kilometre long, with a fort at one end.
mozambique/historic-sites.alt: the fortress of São Sebastião on Ilha de Moçambique, Mozambique

mozambique/lakes-rivers.caption: The Zambezi and Cahora Bassa
mozambique/lakes-rivers.description: The Zambezi's last five hundred kilometres, and the Cahora Bassa lake above them.
mozambique/lakes-rivers.alt: the Zambezi river wide in the Mozambican lowlands, Mozambique

mozambique/local-life.caption: The Beach Market
mozambique/local-life.description: Fish landed and sold on the sand, and the dhow that brought it still on the beach.
mozambique/local-life.alt: fish being sold on the sand beside a dhow, Mozambique

mozambique/luxury.caption: Island Lodges
mozambique/luxury.description: A handful of very good island lodges in Bazaruto and the Quirimbas, and little else on them.
mozambique/luxury.alt: an island lodge among palms above a white beach, Mozambique

mozambique/mountains.caption: Mount Namuli and Gorongosa
mozambique/mountains.description: Namuli at 2,419 metres, and Gorongosa's own mountain with rainforest on top of it.
mozambique/mountains.alt: the granite dome of Mount Namuli rising from farmland, Mozambique

mozambique/nature.caption: Reef and Miombo
mozambique/nature.description: Coral reef the whole coast, miombo woodland inland, and the Rift's southern end at Gorongosa.
mozambique/nature.alt: the Gorongosa floodplain in the green season, Mozambique

mozambique/outdoor.caption: Dive and Sail
mozambique/outdoor.description: Whale shark season at Tofo, dhow safaris in the Quirimbas, and reef diving throughout.
mozambique/outdoor.alt: a dhow under sail between coral islands, Mozambique

mozambique/photography.caption: Dhow Light
mozambique/photography.description: Lateen sails at either end of the day, and water that photographs as three colours at once.
mozambique/photography.alt: dhows silhouetted against a Mozambican sunrise, Mozambique

mozambique/safari.caption: Niassa and Gorongosa
mozambique/safari.description: Niassa is one of the largest reserves in Africa, and among the least visited anywhere.
mozambique/safari.alt: a game track through Niassa reserve woodland, Mozambique

mozambique/traditional-people.caption: Makonde and Makua
mozambique/traditional-people.description: Makonde carving in the north, and the Makua women's mussiro face paint.
mozambique/traditional-people.alt: a Makonde carver at work in northern Mozambique

mozambique/waterfalls.caption: Murchison of the South
mozambique/waterfalls.description: Waterfalls off the Zambezi escarpment, and the Lugenda's rapids in the far north.
mozambique/waterfalls.alt: a waterfall off the escarpment in northern Mozambique

mozambique/why-visit.caption: The Coast Nobody Has Ruined Yet
mozambique/why-visit.description: Two thousand kilometres of Indian Ocean, and most of it still without a road to it.
mozambique/why-visit.alt: an empty Indian Ocean beach with palms behind it, Mozambique

mozambique/wildlife.caption: Gorongosa
mozambique/wildlife.description: A park that lost almost everything in the war and has spent twenty years getting it back.
mozambique/wildlife.alt: waterbuck on the Gorongosa floodplain, Mozambique

namibia/adventure.caption: Self-Drive Country
namibia/adventure.description: The best self-drive country in Africa: gravel roads, long distances and nobody on them.
namibia/adventure.alt: a gravel road running straight to the horizon, Namibia

namibia/architecture.caption: Colonial and Desert Vernacular
namibia/architecture.description: German colonial in the towns, and camps built to disappear into the gravel plains.
namibia/architecture.alt: a desert lodge built low into the gravel plain, Namibia

namibia/beaches.caption: The Skeleton Coast
namibia/beaches.description: Fifteen hundred kilometres of Atlantic, fog, shipwrecks and seal colonies.
namibia/beaches.alt: a shipwreck half-buried on the Skeleton Coast, Namibia

namibia/cities.caption: Windhoek and Swakopmund
namibia/cities.description: Windhoek on the highveld, and Swakopmund where German architecture meets Atlantic fog.
namibia/cities.alt: the seafront and pier at Swakopmund in fog, Namibia

namibia/crafts.caption: Basketry and Ostrich Shell
namibia/crafts.description: Kavango wood carving, San ostrich-eggshell beadwork, and Herero doll making.
namibia/crafts.alt: San ostrich eggshell beads being strung, Namibia

namibia/culture.caption: Eleven Peoples
namibia/culture.description: Owambo, Herero, Damara, Nama, San and more, and German still on half the street signs.
namibia/culture.alt: a Herero woman in traditional dress, Namibia

namibia/eco-tourism.caption: Conservancies
namibia/eco-tourism.description: Communal conservancies cover a fifth of the country and are why the black rhino survived.
namibia/eco-tourism.alt: a community game guard on patrol in a conservancy, Namibia

namibia/family-community.caption: Easy and Safe to Drive
namibia/family-community.description: Good roads, no malaria in most of it, and children who will remember the dunes.
namibia/family-community.alt: a family climbing a dune at Sossusvlei, Namibia

namibia/festivals.caption: Windhoek Karnival and Maherero Day
namibia/festivals.description: The Windhoek carnival in April, and Maherero Day at Okahandja in August.
namibia/festivals.alt: a Maherero Day procession at Okahandja, Namibia

namibia/food.caption: Braai and Biltong
namibia/food.description: Game meat over coals, biltong on every counter, and German bread that is actually German.
namibia/food.alt: game meat grilling over coals at a Namibian braai

namibia/forests.caption: The Caprivi Woodland
namibia/forests.description: No rainforest — the green is in the Zambezi region, riverine and full of elephant.
namibia/forests.alt: riverine woodland along the Zambezi in the Caprivi, Namibia

namibia/heritage.caption: Kolmanskop and the Coast
namibia/heritage.description: A diamond town the desert has taken back, and the German colonial coast at Lüderitz.
namibia/heritage.alt: sand filling a room in the ghost town of Kolmanskop, Namibia

namibia/hero.caption: Where the Desert Meets the Wild
namibia/hero.description: The oldest desert on earth running straight into the Atlantic, and almost nobody on it.
namibia/hero.alt: red dunes at Sossusvlei with long morning shadows, Namibia

namibia/hidden-gems.caption: The Kunene
namibia/hidden-gems.description: The far north-west: Epupa, the Himba, and roads that need two vehicles.
namibia/hidden-gems.alt: a track through the mountains of the Kunene region, Namibia

namibia/historic-sites.caption: Twyfelfontein
namibia/historic-sites.description: Two thousand rock engravings on one hillside, cut into sandstone six thousand years ago.
namibia/historic-sites.alt: rock engravings on sandstone at Twyfelfontein, Namibia

namibia/lakes-rivers.caption: The Kunene and the Zambezi
namibia/lakes-rivers.description: Two permanent rivers, one on each border, and dry riverbeds for everything in between.
namibia/lakes-rivers.alt: a dry riverbed cutting through Damaraland, Namibia

namibia/local-life.caption: The Long Road
namibia/local-life.description: Fuel, biltong and a farm stall every two hundred kilometres, and that is the day.
namibia/local-life.alt: a roadside farm stall on a Namibian highway

namibia/luxury.caption: Desert Camps
namibia/luxury.description: Small camps in private concessions the size of counties, and almost no light pollution.
namibia/luxury.alt: a desert camp lit under a full sky of stars, Namibia

namibia/mountains.caption: The Brandberg and the Escarpment
namibia/mountains.description: The Brandberg is 2,573 metres and holds the White Lady, one of Africa's known rock paintings.
namibia/mountains.alt: the granite mass of the Brandberg above the plain, Namibia

namibia/nature.caption: The Namib
namibia/nature.description: Fifty-five million years old, and dunes at Sossusvlei three hundred metres high.
namibia/nature.alt: the dune field of the Namib at first light, Namibia

namibia/outdoor.caption: Dune, Quad, Balloon
namibia/outdoor.description: Climbing Big Daddy, quad biking at Swakopmund, and balloons over the Namib at dawn.
namibia/outdoor.alt: a balloon over the Namib at sunrise, Namibia

namibia/photography.caption: The Cleanest Light in Africa
namibia/photography.description: Dry air, no haze, and one of the darkest night skies measured anywhere.
namibia/photography.alt: the Milky Way over a Namibian desert landscape

namibia/safari.caption: Etosha
namibia/safari.description: Game that comes to you: in the dry season everything in the park is at one of the waterholes.
namibia/safari.alt: elephants and zebra at an Etosha waterhole, Namibia

namibia/traditional-people.caption: The Himba
namibia/traditional-people.description: The Himba of the Kunene, whose way of life is genuinely intact and should be visited carefully.
namibia/traditional-people.alt: a Himba homestead in the Kunene region, Namibia

namibia/waterfalls.caption: Epupa
namibia/waterfalls.description: The Kunene drops through a gorge on the Angolan border, with baobabs on the rim.

namibia/why-visit.caption: Space, and the Silence in It
namibia/why-visit.description: Two and a half million people in a country twice the size of Germany.
namibia/why-visit.alt: an empty gravel plain stretching to distant mountains, Namibia

namibia/wildlife.caption: Desert-Adapted Wildlife
namibia/wildlife.description: Elephant and rhino that walk sixty kilometres between water, and lion that hunt seals.
namibia/wildlife.alt: a desert-adapted elephant in a dry riverbed, Namibia

niger/adventure.caption: Crossing the Tenere
niger/adventure.description: The Tree of Tenere marked the crossing until a truck hit it in 1973. The route is still run.
niger/adventure.alt: a four-wheel-drive convoy crossing the empty Tenere sand, Niger

niger/architecture.caption: Mud and Beams
niger/architecture.description: Sahelian mud with projecting timber, and the Agadez minaret as its tallest expression.
niger/architecture.alt: the beamed mud tower of the Agadez minaret against the sky, Niger

niger/beaches.caption: Sandbars on the River
niger/beaches.description: Landlocked, and the swimming is off the sandbanks at Niamey when the river is low.
niger/beaches.alt: a wide sandbar in the Niger river with people on it

niger/cities.caption: Niamey and Agadez
niger/cities.description: A river capital with the best museum in the Sahel, and a caravan city at the desert edge.
niger/cities.alt: the mud-brick old quarter of Agadez at street level, Niger

niger/crafts.caption: Tuareg Silver and Leather
niger/crafts.description: The Agadez cross in silver, and camel saddles and boxes in tooled leather.
niger/crafts.alt: silver Agadez crosses laid out on tooled leather, Niger

niger/culture.caption: Tuareg, Hausa, Zarma, Fulani
niger/culture.description: Tuareg and Toubou in the north, Hausa and Zarma in the south, Wodaabe in between.
niger/culture.alt: a Tuareg man in indigo leading a camel in the Air, Niger

niger/eco-tourism.caption: Giraffes Beside Farms
niger/eco-tourism.description: Kouré's giraffes live among fields, and the community is paid to keep it that way.
niger/eco-tourism.alt: giraffe walking past millet fields and a farmer at Kouré, Niger

niger/family-community.caption: Giraffes an Hour Away
niger/family-community.description: Kouré is a morning trip from Niamey, on foot, and children can do it.
niger/family-community.alt: a family on foot watching giraffe browse at Kouré, Niger

niger/festivals.caption: The Cure Salee
niger/festivals.description: Tuareg and Wodaabe gather at In-Gall in September when the salt pastures come up.
niger/festivals.alt: camels and tents gathered at the Cure Salee festival at In-Gall, Niger

niger/food.caption: Millet, Djerma Rice and Kilishi
niger/food.description: Millet paste with sauce, and kilishi — beef dried thin and spiced, the best in the region.
niger/food.alt: strips of spiced kilishi dried beef on a rack, Niger

niger/forests.caption: The Doum Palm Valleys
niger/forests.description: Palm-filled wadis in the Air, green lines through absolutely bare rock.
niger/forests.alt: doum palms filling a wadi between bare granite in the Air, Niger

niger/heritage.caption: Three Sites
niger/heritage.description: Agadez, the Air and Tenere reserves, and W National Park — desert, mountain and river.
niger/heritage.alt: prehistoric rock engravings of cattle in the Air mountains, Niger

niger/hero.caption: The Tenere
niger/hero.description: Four hundred thousand square kilometres of sand with nothing in it at all.
niger/hero.alt: the empty dune field of the Tenere desert under a low sun, Niger

niger/hidden-gems.caption: The Bilma Salt Caravans
niger/hidden-gems.description: The azalai still runs from Agadez to Bilma and back, a thousand kilometres by camel.
niger/hidden-gems.alt: a salt caravan of camels crossing dunes near Bilma, Niger

niger/historic-sites.caption: Agadez
niger/historic-sites.description: A mud minaret twenty-seven metres high, and the Sultanate that has stood behind it since 1449.
niger/historic-sites.alt: the tall mud minaret of the Agadez mosque with its wooden beams, Niger

niger/lakes-rivers.caption: The Niger at Niamey
niger/lakes-rivers.description: The river runs 550 kilometres across the southwest and the whole country leans on it.
niger/lakes-rivers.alt: pirogues on the Niger river at Niamey at sunset

niger/local-life.caption: The Niamey Grand Marche
niger/local-life.description: Everything from millet to motorcycle parts, and the noise that goes with it.
niger/local-life.alt: the crowded aisles of the Grand Marche in Niamey, Niger

niger/luxury.caption: Very Little
niger/luxury.description: A few hotels in Niamey. Everything north is camps and hospitality.
niger/luxury.alt: a courtyard hotel terrace in Niamey at dusk, Niger

niger/mountains.caption: Mont Idoukal-n-Taghes
niger/mountains.description: 2,022 metres in the Air, and the high point of a range full of rock art.
niger/mountains.alt: a granite peak in the Air massif with a palm-filled valley below, Niger

niger/nature.caption: The Air Massif
niger/nature.description: Granite mountains standing two thousand metres out of the sand, with guelta pools in them.
niger/nature.alt: the granite peaks of the Air massif rising from desert sand, Niger

niger/outdoor.caption: The Air on Foot and Camel
niger/outdoor.description: Weeks of walking or riding between guelta and village, with Tuareg guides.
niger/outdoor.alt: a camel caravan crossing sand below the Air mountains, Niger

niger/photography.caption: Dunes and Nothing
niger/photography.description: The Tenere at either end of the day, where the only vertical thing is your own shadow.
niger/photography.alt: long shadows across a bare dune field in the Tenere, Niger

niger/safari.caption: W National Park
niger/safari.description: Shared with Benin and Burkina Faso — lion, elephant and buffalo on the Niger river.
niger/safari.alt: elephants in tall grass in W National Park, Niger

niger/traditional-people.caption: The Wodaabe
niger/traditional-people.description: The Gerewol, where the men dress and dance and the women choose.
niger/traditional-people.alt: Wodaabe men in face paint dancing at the Gerewol, Niger

niger/waterfalls.caption: Guelta Pools
niger/waterfalls.description: Permanent rock pools in the Air, the only standing water for hundreds of kilometres.
niger/waterfalls.alt: a permanent rock pool with palms in the Air mountains, Niger

niger/why-visit.caption: Why Niger
niger/why-visit.description: The emptiest desert on earth, and a giraffe population saved by the people farming next to it.
niger/why-visit.alt: a giraffe standing against open Sahelian sky at Kouré, Niger

niger/wildlife.caption: The Last West African Giraffe
niger/wildlife.description: About six hundred of them at Kouré, the only wild population left in the whole of West Africa.
niger/wildlife.alt: West African giraffe browsing among bush near Kouré, Niger

nigeria/adventure.caption: Plateau and Delta
nigeria/adventure.description: Hiking the Jos plateau, the Obudu cable car, and creek trips through the delta.
nigeria/adventure.alt: the rock formations of the Jos plateau, Nigeria

nigeria/architecture.caption: Mud Mosques and Modernism
nigeria/architecture.description: Hausa mud architecture in the north, and the 1970s modernism of Lagos and Abuja.
nigeria/architecture.alt: the Hausa mud architecture of a northern emir's palace, Nigeria

nigeria/beaches.caption: Lagos and the Atlantic
nigeria/beaches.description: Tarkwa Bay, Elegushi and the long Atlantic beaches east towards Lekki.
nigeria/beaches.alt: boats and beach umbrellas at Tarkwa Bay, Lagos, Nigeria

nigeria/cities.caption: Lagos, Abuja, Kano
nigeria/cities.description: Lagos on the lagoon, purpose-built Abuja in the middle, and Kano's thousand-year-old walls.
nigeria/cities.alt: the old city and dye pits of Kano, Nigeria

nigeria/crafts.caption: Bronze, Adire and Aso Oke
nigeria/crafts.description: Benin bronze casting still practised in Igun street, and adire resist-dyed cloth in Abeokuta.
nigeria/crafts.alt: a bronze caster at work in Igun street, Benin City, Nigeria

nigeria/culture.caption: Five Hundred Languages
nigeria/culture.description: Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa and around five hundred more, in one country.
nigeria/culture.alt: a Yoruba drumming group performing at a festival, Nigeria

nigeria/eco-tourism.caption: Community Forest
nigeria/eco-tourism.description: Afi Mountain's drill ranch and the Cross River community forests, both village-run.
nigeria/eco-tourism.alt: drills at the Afi Mountain sanctuary in Cross River, Nigeria

nigeria/family-community.caption: Loud, and Welcoming
nigeria/family-community.description: Not a quiet holiday — but there is nowhere friendlier once you are through the door.
nigeria/family-community.alt: children playing football on a Lagos beach, Nigeria

nigeria/festivals.caption: Osun-Osogbo and Calabar
nigeria/festivals.description: The Osun-Osogbo grove festival in August, and the Calabar carnival through December.
nigeria/festivals.alt: dancers in costume at the Calabar carnival, Nigeria

nigeria/food.caption: Jollof, Suya and Egusi
nigeria/food.description: Suya off the grill at night, egusi with pounded yam, and the jollof question again.
nigeria/food.alt: suya being grilled at a roadside stand at night, Nigeria

nigeria/forests.caption: Cross River
nigeria/forests.description: The Cross River forest holds the last of Nigeria's gorillas and some of West Africa's tallest trees.
nigeria/forests.alt: dense rainforest canopy in Cross River state, Nigeria

nigeria/heritage.caption: The Bronzes
nigeria/heritage.description: The Benin bronzes are the reason half the museums of Europe have a Nigeria problem.
nigeria/heritage.alt: a display of Benin bronze plaques, Nigeria

nigeria/hero.caption: The Loudest Country on the Continent
nigeria/hero.description: Two hundred and twenty million people, and the music and film the rest of the continent watches.
nigeria/hero.alt: the Lagos skyline across the lagoon at dusk, Nigeria

nigeria/hidden-gems.caption: Idanre
nigeria/hidden-gems.description: The Idanre hills, with an old town six hundred steps up and nobody else climbing them.
nigeria/hidden-gems.alt: the granite Idanre hills rising above forest, Nigeria

nigeria/historic-sites.caption: Benin City and Sungbo's Eredo
nigeria/historic-sites.description: The walls of Benin, and Sungbo's Eredo — a hundred and sixty kilometres of earthworks.
nigeria/historic-sites.alt: the earth walls and moat of the Benin kingdom, Nigeria

nigeria/lakes-rivers.caption: The Niger and the Benue
nigeria/lakes-rivers.description: Two great rivers meeting at Lokoja, and the delta they build a thousand kilometres downstream.
nigeria/lakes-rivers.alt: the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers at Lokoja, Nigeria

nigeria/local-life.caption: Danfo and Buka
nigeria/local-life.description: The yellow buses, the roadside buka, and a city that does not stop at any hour.
nigeria/local-life.alt: a yellow danfo bus in Lagos traffic, Nigeria

nigeria/luxury.caption: Lagos Island Hotels
nigeria/luxury.description: Victoria Island and Ikoyi at one end, and Obudu's mountain resort at the other.
nigeria/luxury.alt: a hotel terrace overlooking Lagos lagoon at night, Nigeria

nigeria/mountains.caption: The Obudu Plateau
nigeria/mountains.description: Sixteen hundred metres of grassland on the Cameroon border, with cattle ranches and cloud.
nigeria/mountains.alt: the green Obudu plateau under low cloud, Nigeria

nigeria/nature.caption: Mangrove to Sahel
nigeria/nature.description: Niger delta mangrove in the south, rainforest, savanna, and the Sahel at the Niger border.
nigeria/nature.alt: mangrove creeks in the Niger delta, Nigeria

nigeria/outdoor.caption: Hike, Paddle, Ride
nigeria/outdoor.description: The Jos plateau, the Obudu ranch trails, and creek boats through the delta.
nigeria/outdoor.alt: hikers on a trail across the Obudu plateau, Nigeria

nigeria/photography.caption: Colour and Crowd
nigeria/photography.description: Markets, festivals and cloth — the hardest thing here is choosing what to leave out.
nigeria/photography.alt: a crowded cloth market in southern Nigeria

nigeria/safari.caption: Yankari
nigeria/safari.description: The country's best game reserve, with a warm spring you can swim in at the centre of it.
nigeria/safari.alt: a game track through Yankari savanna at first light, Nigeria

nigeria/traditional-people.caption: Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, Fulani
nigeria/traditional-people.description: Four large cultures and hundreds of smaller ones, each with its own courts and calendars.
nigeria/traditional-people.alt: a Fulani herder with cattle in northern Nigeria

nigeria/waterfalls.caption: Erin-Ijesha and Gurara
nigeria/waterfalls.description: Erin-Ijesha's seven stages in Osun, and the Gurara falls on the road to Abuja.
nigeria/waterfalls.alt: the stepped Erin-Ijesha waterfall in forest, Nigeria

nigeria/why-visit.caption: The Culture Everyone Else Is Watching
nigeria/why-visit.description: Afrobeats and Nollywood came from here, and it is worth seeing where.
nigeria/why-visit.alt: a live Afrobeats performance in Lagos, Nigeria

nigeria/wildlife.caption: Yankari and Gashaka
nigeria/wildlife.description: Yankari's elephant herds, and Gashaka-Gumti's forest chimpanzees on the Cameroon border.
nigeria/wildlife.alt: elephants at the Wikki warm spring in Yankari, Nigeria

rwanda/adventure.caption: The Congo Nile Trail
rwanda/adventure.description: 227 kilometres along Lake Kivu on foot or by bike, through coffee terraces and fishing villages.

rwanda/adventure.query: Rwanda Congo Nile Trail Lake Kivu

rwanda/architecture.caption: The Convention Centre Dome
rwanda/architecture.description: The Kigali Convention Centre dome, lit at night in the national colours, above a city of red-roofed ridges.
rwanda/architecture.alt: the illuminated dome of the Kigali Convention Centre at night, Rwanda

rwanda/beaches.caption: Rubavu Lakeshore
rwanda/beaches.description: Sand, palms and calm freshwater at Gisenyi, an hour from the gorilla trailheads.
rwanda/beaches.alt: the lakeshore beach and palms at Rubavu on Lake Kivu, Rwanda

rwanda/cities.caption: Kigali, Across the Ridges
rwanda/cities.description: Built along ridge lines, swept every morning, and with a monthly Umuganda when the whole city cleans it together.
rwanda/cities.alt: the ridges and rooftops of Kigali at dusk, Rwanda

rwanda/crafts.caption: Imigongo and Agaseke

rwanda/crafts.alt: geometric imigongo art panels made in eastern Rwanda

rwanda/culture.caption: Intore, the Dance of Heroes

rwanda/culture.alt: Intore dancers in grass headdresses performing in Rwanda

rwanda/eco-tourism.caption: Ten Percent, Back to the Hills
rwanda/eco-tourism.description: A share of every permit goes to the communities bordering the parks, and gorilla numbers have climbed since it started.

rwanda/family-community.caption: Umuganda

rwanda/food.alt: grilled brochettes and plantain at a Kigali restaurant, Rwanda

rwanda/forests.caption: The Nyungwe Canopy Walk
rwanda/forests.description: A suspension walkway sixty metres above one of Africa's oldest montane rainforests, with thirteen primate species below it.
rwanda/forests.alt: the canopy walkway suspended above Nyungwe rainforest, Rwanda

rwanda/heritage.caption: Memory and Reconstruction
rwanda/heritage.description: The Kigali Genocide Memorial is where any honest visit to Rwanda starts, and it explains everything that came after.
rwanda/heritage.alt: the gardens of the Kigali Genocide Memorial, Rwanda

rwanda/hero.caption: Land of a Thousand Hills
rwanda/hero.description: Terraced hills to every horizon, five volcanoes along the northern border, and gorillas on the slopes of them.
rwanda/hero.alt: terraced green hills at sunrise in the Rwandan highlands

rwanda/hidden-gems.caption: Gishwati-Mukura
rwanda/hidden-gems.description: Rwanda's newest national park, a recovering forest between Nyungwe and the volcanoes that almost nobody visits.
rwanda/hidden-gems.alt: the recovering montane forest of Gishwati-Mukura National Park, Rwanda

rwanda/historic-sites.caption: Nyanza, the King's Palace
rwanda/historic-sites.description: The reconstructed royal residence at Nyanza, thatched and enormous, with the long-horned Inyambo cattle still kept.
rwanda/historic-sites.alt: the thatched royal palace and Inyambo cattle at Nyanza, Rwanda

rwanda/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Kivu
rwanda/lakes-rivers.description: One of Africa's great lakes, with no bilharzia, no crocodiles, and the Congo Nile Trail along its shore.
rwanda/lakes-rivers.alt: fishing boats on Lake Kivu at dawn, Rwanda

rwanda/local-life.caption: Kimironko Market
rwanda/local-life.description: Fabric, fruit and everything else under one roof, and the tailors who will make it up by tomorrow.
rwanda/local-life.alt: fabric and produce stalls inside Kimironko market in Kigali, Rwanda

rwanda/luxury.caption: Lodges Below the Volcanoes
rwanda/luxury.description: A handful of very good lodges within sight of the park boundary, built so the trek starts after breakfast.
rwanda/luxury.alt: a luxury lodge terrace facing the Virunga volcanoes, Rwanda

rwanda/mountains.caption: The Virunga Volcanoes
rwanda/mountains.description: Five cones along the border — Karisimbi, Bisoke, Muhabura — with a crater lake at the top of Bisoke.
rwanda/mountains.alt: the Virunga volcano chain rising above the farmland, Rwanda

rwanda/nature.caption: Terraces to the Horizon
rwanda/nature.description: Almost every hillside in Rwanda is farmed in contour terraces — the landscape is entirely made by hand.
rwanda/nature.alt: contour-terraced farmland covering the Rwandan hillsides

rwanda/outdoor.caption: Bisoke Crater Lake
rwanda/outdoor.description: Three hours up through nettles and bamboo to a crater lake at 3,711 m, and three hours back down through mud.
rwanda/outdoor.alt: the crater lake at the summit of Mount Bisoke, Rwanda

rwanda/photography.caption: Mist on the Volcanoes
rwanda/photography.description: The Virunga chain clears for about an hour after dawn, and the terraces below hold the light for longer.
rwanda/photography.alt: mist clearing from the Virunga volcanoes at dawn, Rwanda

rwanda/safari.caption: Akagera, Big Five Again
rwanda/safari.description: Lion returned in 2015, rhino in 2017; the eastern savanna park now has all five, twenty years after losing them.
rwanda/safari.alt: elephants and lakes in Akagera National Park, Rwanda

rwanda/traditional-people.caption: Living Memory
rwanda/traditional-people.description: Cultural villages near Musanze where former poachers now guide, and the beekeepers and potters of the Virunga foothills.
rwanda/traditional-people.alt: a traditional potter at work in a Rwandan cultural village

rwanda/waterfalls.caption: Isumo, Under Nyungwe
rwanda/waterfalls.description: A steep tea-and-forest walk down to the Isumo falls on the western edge of the Nyungwe canopy.
rwanda/waterfalls.alt: the Isumo waterfall in the Nyungwe forest, Rwanda

rwanda/why-visit.caption: Small Country, Nothing Missing
rwanda/why-visit.description: Gorillas, canopy forest, Big Five and a lake shore, all within three hours of a capital you can walk at night.
rwanda/why-visit.alt: a silverback gorilla in the bamboo of Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda

rwanda/wildlife.caption: Face to Face with Gorillas
rwanda/wildlife.description: Ten habituated families on the Virunga slopes, one hour with them, eight people at a time.
rwanda/wildlife.alt: a mountain gorilla family on the slopes of Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda

sao-tome-and-principe/adventure.caption: Walking and Diving
sao-tome-and-principe/adventure.description: Cao Grande and the Pico on foot, and volcanic reef straight off the beaches.
sao-tome-and-principe/adventure.alt: walkers on a forest trail below Pico Cao Grande, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/adventure.query: Sao Tome and Principe Pico Cao Grande

sao-tome-and-principe/architecture.caption: Portuguese Colonial and Roca
sao-tome-and-principe/architecture.description: Pastel colonial in town, and the plantation architecture of the rocas in the interior.
sao-tome-and-principe/architecture.alt: the tower and arcades of Roca Agostinho Neto, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/architecture.query: Sao Tome and Principe Roca Agostinho Neto

sao-tome-and-principe/beaches.caption: Praia Jale and Banana Beach
sao-tome-and-principe/beaches.description: Turtle-nesting sand in the south of Sao Tome, and the curved bay on Principe.
sao-tome-and-principe/beaches.alt: the curved palm-backed sand of Banana Beach on Principe, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/beaches.query: Sao Tome and Principe Banana Beach Principe

sao-tome-and-principe/cities.caption: Sao Tome Town
sao-tome-and-principe/cities.description: A small Portuguese colonial capital with a fort, a market and a cathedral.
sao-tome-and-principe/cities.alt: the pastel colonial buildings and fort at Sao Tome town, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/cities.query: Sao Tome and Principe pastel colonial buildings

sao-tome-and-principe/crafts.caption: Cocoa, Coffee and Carving
sao-tome-and-principe/crafts.description: Single-origin chocolate, island coffee, and carving in the plantation villages.
sao-tome-and-principe/crafts.alt: cocoa beans drying on a wooden rack in the sun, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/crafts.query: Sao Tome and Principe cocoa beans drying

sao-tome-and-principe/culture.caption: Creole, and Portuguese
sao-tome-and-principe/culture.description: Forro, Angolar and Principense creoles, and a culture built on the plantations and against them.
sao-tome-and-principe/culture.alt: a street of Portuguese colonial buildings in Sao Tome town, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/culture.query: Sao Tome and Principe Portuguese Sao Tome

sao-tome-and-principe/eco-tourism.caption: Cocoa, Grown and Made
sao-tome-and-principe/eco-tourism.description: Cooperatives grow it, and the chocolate is made on the island rather than shipped raw.
sao-tome-and-principe/eco-tourism.alt: a chocolate maker sorting cocoa beans on a table, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/eco-tourism.query: Sao Tome and Principe chocolate maker sorting

sao-tome-and-principe/family-community.caption: Small and Easy
sao-tome-and-principe/family-community.description: Short distances, calm bays and no dangerous animals — one of the easier African countries with children.
sao-tome-and-principe/family-community.alt: children swimming in a calm bay on Sao Tome, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/family-community.query: Sao Tome and Principe Sao Tome

sao-tome-and-principe/festivals.caption: Auto de Floripes
sao-tome-and-principe/festivals.description: A Principe street play that runs a whole day in August, performed since the sixteenth century.
sao-tome-and-principe/festivals.alt: costumed performers in the Auto de Floripes on Principe, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/festivals.query: Sao Tome and Principe Auto Floripes

sao-tome-and-principe/food.caption: Calulu and Chocolate
sao-tome-and-principe/food.description: Calulu — fish stewed with okra and palm oil — and chocolate made where the beans grow.
sao-tome-and-principe/food.alt: a plate of calulu with breadfruit and rice, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/food.query: Sao Tome and Principe plate calulu breadfruit

sao-tome-and-principe/forests.caption: The Cocoa Forest
sao-tome-and-principe/forests.description: Plantations abandoned in the 1970s and taken back by the forest, with the trees still fruiting.
sao-tome-and-principe/forests.alt: cocoa pods growing among overgrown plantation trees, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/forests.query: Sao Tome and Principe cocoa pods growing

sao-tome-and-principe/heritage.caption: Principe Biosphere
sao-tome-and-principe/heritage.description: The whole of Principe is a UNESCO biosphere reserve, and it is seven thousand people.
sao-tome-and-principe/heritage.alt: forested peaks and coastline on Principe island, Sao Tome and Principe

sao-tome-and-principe/hero.caption: Pico Cao Grande
sao-tome-and-principe/hero.description: A volcanic plug standing three hundred metres straight out of the rainforest.
sao-tome-and-principe/hero.alt: the needle of Pico Cao Grande rising from rainforest, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/hero.query: Sao Tome and Principe Pico Cao Grande

sao-tome-and-principe/hidden-gems.caption: Roca Agostinho Neto
sao-tome-and-principe/hidden-gems.description: The largest plantation on the island, ruined, lived in, and quite unlike anywhere else.
sao-tome-and-principe/hidden-gems.alt: Hidden Gems in Sao Tome and Principe

sao-tome-and-principe/historic-sites.caption: The Rocas
sao-tome-and-principe/historic-sites.description: Plantation estates with hospitals, chapels and rail lines, most of them now half-ruined and lived in.
sao-tome-and-principe/historic-sites.alt: the arcaded courtyard of an abandoned roca plantation house, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/historic-sites.query: Sao Tome and Principe arcaded courtyard abandoned

sao-tome-and-principe/lakes-rivers.caption: Rivers to the Sea
sao-tome-and-principe/lakes-rivers.description: Short, steep rivers off the volcanic interior, and pools in most of them.
sao-tome-and-principe/lakes-rivers.alt: a clear river running over volcanic rock through forest, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/lakes-rivers.query: Sao Tome and Principe clear river running

sao-tome-and-principe/local-life.caption: The Fish Landing
sao-tome-and-principe/local-life.description: Dugouts come in through the surf and the fish is sold on the sand within the hour.
sao-tome-and-principe/local-life.alt: fishermen landing dugout canoes through surf on a black beach, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/local-life.query: Sao Tome and Principe fishermen landing dugout

sao-tome-and-principe/luxury.caption: Good, and Small
sao-tome-and-principe/luxury.description: Restored rocas turned into hotels, and a serious eco-resort on Principe.
sao-tome-and-principe/luxury.alt: a restored plantation house hotel with a verandah, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/luxury.query: Sao Tome and Principe restored plantation house

sao-tome-and-principe/mountains.caption: Pico de Sao Tome
sao-tome-and-principe/mountains.description: 2,024 metres, in cloud most of the year, and a two-day walk to the top.
sao-tome-and-principe/mountains.alt: the cloud-covered summit of Pico de Sao Tome above forest, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/mountains.query: Sao Tome and Principe Pico Sao Tome

sao-tome-and-principe/nature.caption: Obo
sao-tome-and-principe/nature.description: Rainforest covering a third of Sao Tome, from the peaks down to the shore.
sao-tome-and-principe/nature.alt: dense Obo rainforest running down to the sea, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/nature.query: Sao Tome and Principe dense obo rainforest

sao-tome-and-principe/outdoor.caption: Climbing the Pico
sao-tome-and-principe/outdoor.description: Two days through cloud forest, with a night in a shelter and a lot of rain.
sao-tome-and-principe/outdoor.alt: a muddy trail through mossy cloud forest on the Pico, Sao Tome and Principe

sao-tome-and-principe/photography.caption: Volcano and Canopy
sao-tome-and-principe/photography.description: Cao Grande through cloud in the early morning, from the road below it.
sao-tome-and-principe/photography.alt: cloud parting around Pico Cao Grande above forest at dawn, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/photography.query: Sao Tome and Principe Pico Cao Grande

sao-tome-and-principe/safari.caption: Sea, Not Savanna
sao-tome-and-principe/safari.description: There are no large mammals. What there is instead is birds, turtles and whales.
sao-tome-and-principe/safari.alt: a humpback whale off the coast of Principe, Sao Tome and Principe

sao-tome-and-principe/traditional-people.caption: The Angolares
sao-tome-and-principe/traditional-people.description: Descended from a shipwreck or a maroon community, depending on who tells it, and fishermen either way.
sao-tome-and-principe/traditional-people.alt: Angolares fishermen with a dugout canoe on a black beach, Sao Tome and Principe

sao-tome-and-principe/waterfalls.caption: Sao Nicolau
sao-tome-and-principe/waterfalls.description: A waterfall in the forest above Trindade, reached on a short walk from the road.
sao-tome-and-principe/waterfalls.alt: the Sao Nicolau waterfall falling through dense forest, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/waterfalls.query: Sao Tome and Principe sao nicolau waterfall

sao-tome-and-principe/why-visit.caption: Why Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/why-visit.description: Rainforest to the shore, twenty-eight endemic birds, and chocolate made where it grows.
sao-tome-and-principe/why-visit.alt: a volcanic peak above rainforest and an empty beach, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/why-visit.query: Sao Tome and Principe volcanic peak rainforest

sao-tome-and-principe/wildlife.caption: Endemic Birds
sao-tome-and-principe/wildlife.description: Twenty-eight species live on these islands and nowhere else — one of the highest rates on earth.
sao-tome-and-principe/wildlife.alt: a Sao Tome giant weaver on a branch in Obo forest, Sao Tome and Principe
sao-tome-and-principe/wildlife.query: Sao Tome and Principe sao tome giant

senegal/adventure.caption: Surf, Sail, Paddle
senegal/adventure.description: Dakar's surf breaks, pirogues in the delta, and the Paris-Dakar's original finish line.
senegal/adventure.alt: surfers at Ngor island off Dakar, Senegal

senegal/architecture.caption: Colonial and Sudano-Sahelian
senegal/architecture.description: The balconies of Saint-Louis, and the mud-and-timber mosques of the interior.
senegal/architecture.alt: a Sudano-Sahelian mosque in the Senegalese interior

senegal/beaches.caption: The Petite Côte
senegal/beaches.description: Saly, Somone and Cap Skirring — Atlantic sand from the peninsula down to Casamance.
senegal/beaches.alt: the long Atlantic beach at Cap Skirring, Senegal

senegal/cities.caption: Dakar
senegal/cities.description: The most westerly city in Africa, on a peninsula, with the ocean on three sides.
senegal/cities.alt: the Dakar coastline seen from the Corniche, Senegal

senegal/crafts.caption: Glass Painting and Weaving
senegal/crafts.description: Sous-verre glass painting, and the strip-woven cloth of the Manjak weavers.
senegal/crafts.alt: a sous-verre glass painting being finished, Senegal

senegal/culture.caption: Teranga
senegal/culture.description: The word means hospitality, and it is the thing the country most wants you to notice.
senegal/culture.alt: a family gathering for tea in a Senegalese courtyard

senegal/eco-tourism.caption: Community Campements
senegal/eco-tourism.description: The Casamance campements villageois — village-owned, village-run, and thirty years old.
senegal/eco-tourism.alt: a village-run campement in Casamance, Senegal

senegal/family-community.caption: Short Flights, Long Beaches
senegal/family-community.description: Six hours from Europe, and beaches with a shallow warm Atlantic in front of them.
senegal/family-community.alt: children on the beach at Saly on the Petite Côte, Senegal

senegal/festivals.caption: Dak'Art and the Magal
senegal/festivals.description: The Dakar art biennale, and the Grand Magal of Touba, which moves millions of people.
senegal/festivals.alt: crowds gathering at the great mosque of Touba, Senegal

senegal/food.caption: Thieboudienne
senegal/food.description: Rice and fish, cooked in one pot, and the national dish by common consent.
senegal/food.alt: thieboudienne served on a shared platter, Senegal

senegal/forests.caption: Casamance
senegal/forests.description: Palm and rice country south of the Gambia, greener than the rest and quite different.
senegal/forests.alt: rice paddies and palms in Casamance, Senegal

senegal/heritage.caption: Saint-Louis
senegal/heritage.description: The old colonial capital on its island in the river mouth, with the Faidherbe bridge.
senegal/heritage.alt: the colonial waterfront of Saint-Louis at dusk, Senegal

senegal/hero.caption: Where the Sahel Meets the Atlantic
senegal/hero.description: Desert to the north, delta to the south, and Dakar on a peninsula between them.
senegal/hero.alt: the Atlantic breaking below the cliffs at Dakar, Senegal

senegal/hidden-gems.caption: Bassari Country
senegal/hidden-gems.description: The Bassari and Bedik villages of the south-east, up in the hills, and rarely visited.
senegal/hidden-gems.alt: a Bedik village on a hillside in south-east Senegal

senegal/historic-sites.caption: Gorée
senegal/historic-sites.description: The island off Dakar, and the house of slaves that stands on it.
senegal/historic-sites.alt: the pink house of slaves on Gorée island, Senegal

senegal/lakes-rivers.caption: The Senegal and the Saloum
senegal/lakes-rivers.description: The Senegal river along the Mauritanian border, and the Saloum spreading into the sea.
senegal/lakes-rivers.alt: a pirogue on the Saloum delta at sunset, Senegal

senegal/local-life.caption: Ataya and the Market
senegal/local-life.description: Three glasses of tea, poured from height, and each one stronger than the last.
senegal/local-life.alt: tea being poured from height at a Dakar stall, Senegal

senegal/luxury.caption: Delta Lodges
senegal/luxury.description: Small lodges on the Saloum islands, reached only by boat, with birds outside.
senegal/luxury.alt: a lodge deck over the water in the Saloum delta, Senegal

senegal/mountains.caption: Fouta Djallon Foothills
senegal/mountains.description: No high peaks — the ground rises to the Fouta Djallon foothills in the far south-east.
senegal/mountains.alt: rolling hills in the south-east of Senegal

senegal/nature.caption: Delta and Dune
senegal/nature.description: The Sine-Saloum mangrove delta, the Casamance forest, and Sahel sand in the north.
senegal/nature.alt: mangrove channels in the Sine-Saloum delta, Senegal

senegal/outdoor.caption: Surf and Sail
senegal/outdoor.description: Dakar's breaks, kite-surfing on the Petite Côte, and pirogue trips through the mangrove.
senegal/outdoor.alt: kitesurfers off the Petite Côte, Senegal

senegal/photography.caption: Light on Water
senegal/photography.description: Delta light at either end of the day, and pink water at the Lac Rose.
senegal/photography.alt: pink water and salt at the Lac Rose near Dakar, Senegal

senegal/safari.caption: Niokolo-Koba
senegal/safari.description: Lion, hippo and Derby eland in the south-east, in a park that is slowly recovering.
senegal/safari.alt: a game track through Niokolo-Koba woodland, Senegal

senegal/traditional-people.caption: Wolof, Serer and Diola
senegal/traditional-people.description: Wolof across the country, Serer in the delta, and the Diola of Casamance.
senegal/traditional-people.alt: a Serer village in the Sine-Saloum, Senegal

senegal/waterfalls.caption: Dindefelo
senegal/waterfalls.description: A hundred metres of water off the Fouta escarpment, near the Guinea border.
senegal/waterfalls.alt: the Dindefelo waterfall dropping into forest, Senegal

senegal/why-visit.caption: The Easy Door to West Africa
senegal/why-visit.description: Stable, straightforward, six hours from Europe, and the friendliest reputation on the coast.
senegal/why-visit.alt: the Atlantic coast road north of Dakar, Senegal

senegal/wildlife.caption: Djoudj
senegal/wildlife.description: Three million migrating birds winter in the Djoudj — one of the great bird sites on earth.
senegal/wildlife.alt: pelicans massed on the water at Djoudj, Senegal

seychelles/adventure.caption: Dive, Sail, Walk
seychelles/adventure.description: Diving the granite drop-offs, sailing the inner islands, and walking Mahé's ridge trails.
seychelles/adventure.alt: a yacht anchored between granite islands, Seychelles

seychelles/architecture.caption: Creole Houses
seychelles/architecture.description: Steep roofs, wide verandas and louvres — built for heat before anyone had a choice.
seychelles/architecture.alt: a traditional Creole house with louvred shutters, Seychelles

seychelles/beaches.caption: Anse Source d'Argent
seychelles/beaches.description: The most photographed beach in the world, and the granite is the reason why.
seychelles/beaches.alt: granite boulders and shallow water at Anse Source d'Argent, Seychelles

seychelles/cities.caption: Victoria
seychelles/cities.description: One of the smallest capitals in the world, with a clock tower and a market.
seychelles/cities.alt: the market and clock tower in Victoria, Mahé, Seychelles

seychelles/crafts.caption: Boatbuilding and Weaving
seychelles/crafts.description: Pirogue building on La Digue, and coconut palm weaving still done by hand.
seychelles/crafts.alt: a wooden pirogue being built on a beach, Seychelles

seychelles/culture.caption: Creole
seychelles/culture.description: African, French, Indian and Chinese, in one Creole language and one kitchen.
seychelles/culture.alt: a Creole house with a wide veranda on Mahé, Seychelles

seychelles/eco-tourism.caption: Half the Country Is Protected
seychelles/eco-tourism.description: Forty-two per cent of the land is national park, and the marine parks now match it.
seychelles/eco-tourism.alt: a marine park marker buoy over Seychelles reef

seychelles/family-community.caption: Shallow, Warm, Safe
seychelles/family-community.description: Lagoons inside the reef, no dangerous surf on most beaches, and short boat rides.
seychelles/family-community.alt: children in a shallow turquoise lagoon, Seychelles

seychelles/festivals.caption: Festival Kreol
seychelles/festivals.description: Festival Kreol in October, and the sega and moutya danced through it.
seychelles/festivals.alt: dancers at the Festival Kreol on Mahé, Seychelles

seychelles/food.caption: Fish, Coconut and Chilli
seychelles/food.description: Grilled fish, coconut curry, breadfruit, and a chilli sauce that is not a suggestion.
seychelles/food.alt: grilled fish with coconut curry and rice, Seychelles

seychelles/forests.caption: The Vallée de Mai
seychelles/forests.description: Coco de mer palms in a valley on Praslin, and the largest seed of any plant on earth.
seychelles/forests.alt: coco de mer palms in the Vallée de Mai, Seychelles

seychelles/heritage.caption: Aldabra
seychelles/heritage.description: A thousand kilometres out, with a hundred thousand giant tortoises and almost no people.
seychelles/heritage.alt: the raised coral rim of the Aldabra atoll, Seychelles

seychelles/hero.caption: Granite Islands in the Indian Ocean
seychelles/hero.description: Ancient granite, not coral or volcano — these islands are a fragment of a broken continent.
seychelles/hero.alt: granite boulders on a white beach at La Digue, Seychelles

seychelles/hidden-gems.caption: La Digue by Bicycle
seychelles/hidden-gems.description: No real roads and few cars — an island best measured in bicycle hours.
seychelles/hidden-gems.alt: a sandy lane and bicycles under palms on La Digue, Seychelles

seychelles/historic-sites.caption: The Plantations
seychelles/historic-sites.description: L'Union Estate on La Digue, with its vanilla, copra mill and colonial house.
seychelles/historic-sites.alt: the copra mill and plantation house at L'Union Estate, Seychelles

seychelles/lakes-rivers.caption: No Rivers, All Sea
seychelles/lakes-rivers.description: The water here is the Indian Ocean, and the lagoons inside the reef.
seychelles/lakes-rivers.alt: the shallow lagoon inside a Seychelles reef

seychelles/local-life.caption: The Fish Market
seychelles/local-life.description: Victoria's market at eight in the morning is the most useful hour on the island.
seychelles/local-life.alt: the fish market in Victoria early in the morning, Seychelles

seychelles/luxury.caption: The Private Islands
seychelles/luxury.description: North Island, Frégate and Denis — private islands with a dozen villas on each.
seychelles/luxury.alt: a villa above a beach on a private Seychelles island

seychelles/mountains.caption: Morne Seychellois
seychelles/mountains.description: Nine hundred metres of forested granite above Victoria, with trails through the mist forest.
seychelles/mountains.alt: the forested ridge of Morne Seychellois, Seychelles

seychelles/nature.caption: Forty-Three Granite Islands
seychelles/nature.description: Granite in the inner islands, coral atolls in the outer, and a thousand kilometres between.
seychelles/nature.alt: the granite peaks of Mahé above the sea, Seychelles

seychelles/outdoor.caption: Dive, Kayak, Cycle
seychelles/outdoor.description: Granite dive sites, kayaks in the lagoons, and La Digue where the bicycle is the transport.
seychelles/outdoor.alt: bicycles on a sandy track on La Digue, Seychelles

seychelles/photography.caption: Granite and Turquoise
seychelles/photography.description: Grey granite, white sand and three shades of blue — the reason every camera comes here.
seychelles/photography.alt: granite boulders and turquoise water at sunset, Seychelles

reasons: looks like 56% of a slot already filled here

seychelles/safari.caption: Not a Safari, a Reef
