south-sudan/hidden-gems.alt: the Nile running through green hills at Nimule, South Sudan

south-sudan/historic-sites.caption: Lado and the Old Posts
south-sudan/historic-sites.description: The Lado Enclave, Gondokoro and the river stations of the nineteenth-century Nile expeditions.
south-sudan/historic-sites.alt: the ruins of a colonial-era river station on the White Nile, South Sudan

south-sudan/lakes-rivers.caption: The White Nile
south-sudan/lakes-rivers.description: It runs the length of the country and it is the reason for everything here.
south-sudan/lakes-rivers.alt: a fishing canoe on the White Nile at sunset near Juba, South Sudan

south-sudan/local-life.caption: Market Day at Terekeka
south-sudan/local-life.description: Cattle, sorghum, fish and tea, and the whole district in one place.
south-sudan/local-life.alt: a busy open-air market with cattle and traders at Terekeka, South Sudan

south-sudan/luxury.caption: Two Camps
south-sudan/luxury.description: There is a mobile camp on the migration and very little else. That is the honest position.
south-sudan/luxury.alt: a mobile tented camp pitched on open grassland, South Sudan

south-sudan/mountains.caption: The Imatong
south-sudan/mountains.description: Mount Kinyeti at 3,187 metres on the Ugandan border, the highest point in the country.
south-sudan/mountains.alt: the forested slopes of the Imatong mountains rising to Mount Kinyeti, South Sudan

south-sudan/nature.caption: The Sudd
south-sudan/nature.description: One of the largest wetlands on earth, where the Nile spreads out and slows almost to a stop.
south-sudan/nature.alt: papyrus and open water stretching to the horizon in the Sudd, South Sudan

south-sudan/outdoor.caption: Walking the Imatong
south-sudan/outdoor.description: Cool forest, waterfalls and Kinyeti, from Gilo. Guides are essential and available.
south-sudan/outdoor.alt: a forest path climbing through the Imatong mountains, South Sudan

south-sudan/photography.caption: Smoke and Horns
south-sudan/photography.description: A Mundari camp at first light, when the fires are lit and the light comes through them.
south-sudan/photography.alt: sunlight through dung smoke over cattle horns at a Mundari camp, South Sudan

south-sudan/safari.caption: Boma and Badingilo
south-sudan/safari.description: Two parks either side of the migration route, with almost no infrastructure and no crowds.
south-sudan/safari.alt: open grassland and scattered trees in Boma National Park, South Sudan

south-sudan/traditional-people.caption: The Mundari
south-sudan/traditional-people.description: Cattle are wealth, name and argument. A camp of them at dusk is unlike anything else.
south-sudan/traditional-people.alt: a Mundari man resting against the flank of a long-horned bull, South Sudan

south-sudan/waterfalls.caption: Fula Falls
south-sudan/waterfalls.description: The Nile dropping through rock at Fula, on its way north out of Uganda.
south-sudan/waterfalls.alt: white water at the Fula rapids on the White Nile, South Sudan

south-sudan/why-visit.caption: Why South Sudan
south-sudan/why-visit.description: A migration to rival the Serengeti's, seen by a few dozen people a year.
south-sudan/why-visit.alt: a single vehicle beside an immense herd of kob on open plain, South Sudan

south-sudan/wildlife.caption: The Great Kob Migration
south-sudan/wildlife.description: White-eared kob, tiang and Mongalla gazelle — counted at over a million animals.
south-sudan/wildlife.alt: a vast herd of white-eared kob crossing open grassland, South Sudan

sudan/adventure.caption: Diving and Desert Driving
sudan/adventure.description: Liveaboards out of Port Sudan, and four-wheel-drive routes between the pyramid fields.
sudan/adventure.photographer: 沖縄ダイビングスクール ワールドダイビング
sudan/adventure.alt: a dive boat anchored over a reef in the Sudanese Red Sea

sudan/architecture.caption: Mud Brick and Painted Doors
sudan/architecture.description: Nubian vaulted mud-brick houses with painted gates, a technique revived by Hassan Fathy.
sudan/architecture.alt: a vaulted Nubian mud-brick house with a painted gateway, Sudan

sudan/beaches.caption: Reefs Nobody Dives
sudan/beaches.description: Sanganeb atoll and Sha'ab Rumi, where Cousteau sank Conshelf II and the coral grew over it.
sudan/beaches.alt: a coral wall and reef fish at Sanganeb atoll in the Red Sea, Sudan

sudan/cities.caption: Khartoum and Omdurman
sudan/cities.description: Two cities facing each other across the confluence, one colonial grid and one enormous souk.
sudan/cities.alt: the Omdurman souk crowded with people and stalls, Sudan

sudan/crafts.caption: Basketry and Silver
sudan/crafts.description: Coiled palm baskets from the north, Beja swords, and silver from the Omdurman souk.
sudan/crafts.alt: coiled palm-fibre baskets in bright colours at Omdurman souk, Sudan

sudan/culture.caption: Nubian, Arab, Beja
sudan/culture.description: Nubian along the northern Nile, Beja in the Red Sea hills, and nearly six hundred groups altogether.
sudan/culture.alt: a decorated Nubian house with a painted doorway on the Nile, Sudan

sudan/eco-tourism.caption: Gum Arabic and the Acacia Belt
sudan/eco-tourism.description: A gum tapped from wild acacia by hand, in most of the soft drinks in the world.
sudan/eco-tourism.alt: a tapped acacia trunk with gum arabic crystals on the bark, Sudan

sudan/family-community.caption: The Nile at Tuti
sudan/family-community.description: The island in the confluence, farmed, walkable, and reached by ferry from three sides.
sudan/family-community.alt: small farms and palms on Tuti island in the Nile at Khartoum, Sudan

sudan/festivals.caption: Sufi Friday at Omdurman
sudan/festivals.description: The Hamed al-Nil tomb, every Friday at sunset, drumming and whirling for two hours.
sudan/festivals.alt: Sufi dervishes in green and red at the Hamed al-Nil tomb, Omdurman, Sudan

sudan/food.caption: Ful and Kisra
sudan/food.description: Ful medames for breakfast everywhere, kisra sorghum flatbread, and coffee spiced with ginger.
sudan/food.alt: a bowl of ful medames with bread and tea on a table, Sudan

sudan/forests.caption: Acacia and Doum Palm
sudan/forests.description: Gum arabic comes from the acacia belt across the middle of the country. Most of the world's does.
sudan/forests.alt: an acacia woodland tapped for gum arabic in central Sudan

sudan/heritage.caption: Kush
sudan/heritage.description: Gebel Barkal was the holy mountain of two kingdoms, and the temple of Amun is cut into it.
sudan/heritage.alt: the flat-topped Gebel Barkal with the temple ruins at its base, Sudan

sudan/hero.caption: The Pyramids of Meroe
sudan/hero.description: Two hundred of them on a ridge of sand, steeper and smaller than Egypt's, and empty.
sudan/hero.alt: the Nubian pyramids of Meroe standing on desert dunes, Sudan

sudan/hidden-gems.caption: Old Dongola
sudan/hidden-gems.description: A Christian Nubian capital on the Nile, with a throne hall that became a mosque.
sudan/hidden-gems.alt: the ruined columns and throne hall of Old Dongola above the Nile, Sudan

sudan/historic-sites.caption: Meroe, Nuri and El-Kurru
sudan/historic-sites.description: Three royal cemeteries of the Kingdom of Kush, which ruled Egypt for a century.
sudan/historic-sites.alt: the pyramid field at Nuri with the Nile beyond, Sudan

sudan/lakes-rivers.caption: The Blue and the White
sudan/lakes-rivers.description: They meet at Khartoum, one clear and one brown, and you can see the line between them.
sudan/lakes-rivers.alt: the confluence of the Blue and White Nile at Khartoum from the air, Sudan

sudan/local-life.caption: The Camel Market
sudan/local-life.description: Omdurman's camel market on a Saturday, with animals in from Kordofan and Darfur.
sudan/local-life.alt: camels and traders at the Omdurman camel market, Sudan

sudan/luxury.caption: Very Little
sudan/luxury.description: A handful of Red Sea liveaboards, and camps at Meroe. That is the whole of it.
sudan/luxury.alt: a tented camp on sand within sight of the Meroe pyramids, Sudan

sudan/mountains.caption: The Red Sea Hills and Jebel Marra
sudan/mountains.description: Granite hills behind Port Sudan, and a volcanic crater lake on Jebel Marra in Darfur.
sudan/mountains.alt: the volcanic crater lake on Jebel Marra, Sudan

sudan/nature.caption: The Great Bend
sudan/nature.description: The Nile turns southwest for three hundred kilometres here, against every expectation.
sudan/nature.alt: the Nile curving through desert at the great bend in northern Sudan

sudan/outdoor.caption: Walking Between Pyramids
sudan/outdoor.description: There is no fence at Meroe. You walk in off the sand and up the ridge.
sudan/outdoor.alt: footprints in sand leading up to the Meroe pyramids, Sudan

sudan/photography.caption: Pyramids and Dunes
sudan/photography.description: Meroe an hour after dawn, when the sand is still ridged and the shadows are long.
sudan/photography.alt: long shadows across dunes below the Meroe pyramids at dawn, Sudan

sudan/safari.caption: Dinder
sudan/safari.description: One of Africa's oldest national parks, and one of the least visited on the continent.
sudan/safari.alt: acacia woodland and a waterhole in Dinder National Park, Sudan

sudan/traditional-people.caption: The Nubians
sudan/traditional-people.description: The Nubian villages along the northern Nile paint their houses, and have done for a very long time.
sudan/traditional-people.alt: a Nubian woman in a doorway of a brightly painted house, Sudan

sudan/waterfalls.caption: The Cataracts
sudan/waterfalls.description: Six of them on the Nile, rapids where the river crosses granite, and boats have to portage.
sudan/waterfalls.alt: white water over black granite at a Nile cataract, Sudan

sudan/why-visit.caption: Why Sudan
sudan/why-visit.description: More pyramids than Egypt, no queue at any of them, and a welcome people write books about.
sudan/why-visit.alt: a lone figure walking among the pyramids of Meroe, Sudan

sudan/wildlife.caption: Dinder and the Red Sea
sudan/wildlife.description: Dinder on the Ethiopian border holds lion, giraffe and roan; the reefs hold everything else.
sudan/wildlife.alt: a herd of roan antelope in Dinder National Park, Sudan

tanzania/adventure.caption: Uhuru Peak by Machame
tanzania/adventure.description: Six days up the Machame route, one very long night to the summit, and a sunrise you have to earn.
tanzania/adventure.alt: trekkers on the Machame route high on Kilimanjaro, Tanzania

tanzania/architecture.caption: The Doors of Stone Town
tanzania/architecture.description: Brass-studded Indian doors and carved Omani frames, on coral-rag houses in alleys too narrow to drive.
tanzania/architecture.alt: a brass-studded carved door in a Stone Town alley, Zanzibar, Tanzania

tanzania/beaches.caption: Zanzibar, Nungwi to Paje
tanzania/beaches.description: White sand, warm shallow water and dhows still built by hand on the beach at Nungwi.
tanzania/beaches.alt: white sand and traditional dhows on the beach at Nungwi, Zanzibar, Tanzania

tanzania/cities.caption: Dar es Salaam
tanzania/cities.description: Harbour of peace: the ferry terminal, the fish market at Kivukoni, and the dhows still working the channel.
tanzania/cities.alt: the harbour and skyline of Dar es Salaam from the water, Tanzania

tanzania/crafts.caption: Tingatinga and Makonde
tanzania/crafts.description: Enamel-bright Tingatinga painting from Dar es Salaam, and Makonde ebony carving from the southern plateau.
tanzania/crafts.alt: a Makonde carver working ebony wood, Tanzania

tanzania/culture.caption: Maasai, Chagga, Swahili
tanzania/culture.description: Cattle-keepers on the northern plains, coffee farmers on the mountain, and a coast that has always faced east.
tanzania/culture.alt: Maasai men in ceremonial dress on the northern Tanzanian plains

tanzania/eco-tourism.caption: Ngorongoro, Shared Ground
tanzania/eco-tourism.description: The conservation area is the rare model where Maasai pastoralists and wildlife legally use the same land.
tanzania/eco-tourism.alt: Maasai herders and cattle on the Ngorongoro conservation area highlands, Tanzania

tanzania/family-community.caption: Boma and Coffee Farm
tanzania/family-community.description: Maasai boma visits on the crater rim road, and Chagga coffee walks on the lower slopes of Kilimanjaro.
tanzania/family-community.alt: a Chagga family roasting coffee on a farm below Kilimanjaro, Tanzania

tanzania/festivals.caption: Sauti za Busara
tanzania/festivals.description: Four days of live music from across the continent inside the old Arab fort in Stone Town, every February.
tanzania/festivals.alt: musicians performing at the Sauti za Busara festival in Stone Town, Tanzania

tanzania/food.caption: Spice, Ugali, Urojo
tanzania/food.description: Cloves and cardamom from the Zanzibar plantations, grilled seafood at Forodhani, and ugali everywhere else.
tanzania/food.alt: grilled seafood stalls at Forodhani Gardens in Stone Town, Tanzania

tanzania/forests.caption: Udzungwa and Jozani
tanzania/forests.description: The Udzungwa scarp holds species found nowhere else; Jozani holds the red colobus, also found nowhere else.
tanzania/forests.alt: a Zanzibar red colobus monkey in Jozani Forest, Tanzania

tanzania/heritage.caption: Olduvai and the Coast
tanzania/heritage.description: Olduvai Gorge holds the earliest human record; the coast holds a thousand years of Indian Ocean trade.
tanzania/heritage.alt: the layered walls of Olduvai Gorge in the Ngorongoro conservation area, Tanzania

tanzania/hero.caption: Into the Wild
tanzania/hero.description: The Serengeti runs unbroken to the horizon, and the migration has been circling it far longer than anyone has watched.
tanzania/hero.alt: the endless short-grass plains of the Serengeti at sunrise, Tanzania

tanzania/hidden-gems.caption: Ruaha and Katavi
tanzania/hidden-gems.description: The south and west: huge elephant populations, hippo crowded into shrinking pools, and no other vehicles.
tanzania/hidden-gems.alt: elephants beneath baobabs in Ruaha National Park, Tanzania

tanzania/historic-sites.caption: Stone Town and Kilwa
tanzania/historic-sites.description: Stone Town is UNESCO-listed; Kilwa Kisiwani was the richest port on the Swahili coast six centuries ago.
tanzania/historic-sites.alt: the ruins of the great mosque at Kilwa Kisiwani, Tanzania

tanzania/lakes-rivers.caption: Manyara and the Rufiji
tanzania/lakes-rivers.description: Flamingo and tree-climbing lions at Manyara; the Rufiji braiding through Nyerere, the largest park in Africa.
tanzania/lakes-rivers.alt: the Rufiji river braiding through Nyerere National Park, Tanzania

tanzania/local-life.caption: Dala Dalas and Dhows
tanzania/local-life.description: Minibuses inland, dhows on the water, and a fish auction at Kivukoni that starts before it is light.
tanzania/local-life.alt: the early morning fish market at Kivukoni in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania

tanzania/luxury.caption: Camps and Spice Islands
tanzania/luxury.description: Mobile camps that follow the migration, and beach houses on the Zanzibar east coast with nothing either side.
tanzania/luxury.alt: a luxury tented camp on the Serengeti plains at dusk, Tanzania

tanzania/mountains.caption: Kilimanjaro, 5,895 m
tanzania/mountains.description: The highest free-standing mountain on earth: rainforest, moorland, alpine desert and glacier in five days of walking.
tanzania/mountains.alt: the snow-capped summit of Kilimanjaro above the cloud line, Tanzania

tanzania/nature.caption: The Ngorongoro Crater
tanzania/nature.description: A collapsed caldera twenty kilometres across with its own permanent population of thirty thousand animals.
tanzania/nature.alt: the floor of the Ngorongoro Crater seen from the rim, Tanzania

tanzania/outdoor.caption: Snorkelling Mnemba
tanzania/outdoor.description: The atoll off the northeast tip of Zanzibar, plus kite surfing at Paje and diving at Pemba.
tanzania/outdoor.alt: snorkelling over coral reef at Mnemba atoll, Zanzibar, Tanzania

tanzania/photography.caption: Acacia, Kopje, Sunset
tanzania/photography.description: The Serengeti kopjes at the end of the day, and the migration column stretching past the edge of the frame.
tanzania/photography.alt: an acacia silhouetted against the Serengeti sunset, Tanzania

tanzania/safari.caption: Following the Migration
tanzania/safari.description: Calving on the southern plains in February, the Grumeti in June, the Mara river in August — the circuit never stops.
tanzania/safari.alt: wildebeest herds streaming across the Serengeti plains, Tanzania

tanzania/traditional-people.caption: The Hadzabe of Lake Eyasi
tanzania/traditional-people.description: One of the last hunter-gatherer peoples in Africa, speaking a click language unrelated to anything nearby.
tanzania/traditional-people.alt: a Hadzabe hunter with a bow near Lake Eyasi, Tanzania

tanzania/waterfalls.caption: Materuni, Under Kilimanjaro
tanzania/waterfalls.description: Eighty metres of cold water through Chagga coffee farms on the lower slopes, an easy walk from Moshi.
tanzania/waterfalls.alt: the Materuni waterfall in the forest below Kilimanjaro, Tanzania

tanzania/why-visit.caption: Mountain, Plain and Reef
tanzania/why-visit.description: Summit Africa's highest mountain, cross the Serengeti and sleep on the Indian Ocean, in the same fortnight.
tanzania/why-visit.alt: Kilimanjaro rising above the acacia plains at sunrise, Tanzania

tanzania/wildlife.caption: The Big Five, and Then Some
tanzania/wildlife.description: Lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo and rhino, plus the largest elephant herds left in East Africa.
tanzania/wildlife.alt: a lion pride resting on a kopje in the Serengeti, Tanzania

togo/adventure.caption: Walking Around Kpalime
togo/adventure.description: Waterfalls, coffee farms, Mont Agou and the butterfly forest, all within an hour.
togo/adventure.photographer: ธันยกร ไกรสร
togo/adventure.alt: a walking path through cocoa and coffee smallholdings near Kpalime, Togo

togo/architecture.caption: Towers of Mud
togo/architecture.description: Takienta houses with granaries on top, and German colonial stone in Lome and Aneho.
togo/architecture.alt: the sculpted mud tower and granary of a takienta house, Togo

togo/beaches.caption: Fifty Kilometres of Coast
togo/beaches.description: Palm-backed Atlantic sand from Lome east to Aneho, with a heavy swell.
togo/beaches.alt: coconut palms and Atlantic surf on the beach near Aneho, Togo

togo/cities.caption: Lome
togo/cities.description: The only capital on a border, with the biggest market in the region behind the beach.
togo/cities.alt: the beach and palm-lined boulevard at Lome, Togo

togo/crafts.caption: Batik and Pottery
togo/crafts.description: Batik and wood carving around Kpalime, and pottery from the north.
togo/crafts.alt: batik cloth drying on a line at a Kpalime workshop, Togo

togo/culture.caption: Ewe, Kabye, Tem, Batammariba
togo/culture.description: Ewe in the south, Kabye in the centre, Batammariba in the far northwest.
togo/culture.alt: an Ewe drumming group performing in a village, Togo

togo/eco-tourism.caption: Butterflies at Kloto
togo/eco-tourism.description: Over five hundred species recorded in one forest, and a local guiding tradition around them.
togo/eco-tourism.alt: a guide showing butterflies in the Kloto forest, Togo

togo/family-community.caption: Beach and Waterfall in a Day
togo/family-community.description: Togo is narrow enough that the coast and the Kloto hills are the same short trip.
togo/family-community.alt: a family swimming in a pool below a waterfall near Kpalime, Togo

togo/festivals.caption: Evala and the Voodoo Market
togo/festivals.description: Kabye wrestling in July, and the Akodessewa fetish market in Lome all year.
togo/festivals.alt: young men wrestling at the Evala festival in Kabye country, Togo

togo/food.caption: Fufu and Gboma Dessi
togo/food.description: Fufu with groundnut sauce, and gboma dessi — spinach stew with fish.
togo/food.alt: a bowl of gboma dessi spinach stew with fufu, Togo

togo/forests.caption: The Kloto Forest
togo/forests.description: Semi-deciduous forest above Kpalime, and one of the richest butterfly sites in West Africa.
togo/forests.alt: butterflies on a forest path in the Kloto hills, Togo

togo/heritage.caption: Koutammakou, Listed
togo/heritage.description: The Batammariba landscape has been a World Heritage site since 2004, and is still lived in.
togo/heritage.alt: a cluster of takienta tower houses among fields at Koutammakou, Togo

togo/hero.caption: Koutammakou
togo/hero.description: The Batammariba build towered mud houses that are fortress, granary and shrine at once.
togo/hero.alt: a Batammariba takienta tower house at Koutammakou, Togo

togo/hidden-gems.caption: Aneho and Lake Togo
togo/hidden-gems.description: An hour east of Lome: a lagoon, a decayed colonial town, and no visitors.
togo/hidden-gems.alt: a quiet street of faded colonial houses at Aneho, Togo

togo/historic-sites.caption: Aneho and the Old Coast
togo/historic-sites.description: The first colonial capital, with German and Afro-Brazilian buildings going quietly to seed.
togo/historic-sites.alt: a decaying German colonial building in Aneho, Togo

togo/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Togo and the Mono
togo/lakes-rivers.description: A shallow lagoon behind the coast, and the Mono river marking the Benin border.
togo/lakes-rivers.alt: pirogues on the shallow water of Lake Togo

togo/local-life.caption: The Grand Marche and the Nana Benz
togo/local-life.description: The women who built the wax-print trade ran it from this market, and still do.
togo/local-life.alt: wax print cloth stacked at a stall in Lome's Grand Marche, Togo

togo/luxury.caption: A Handful
togo/luxury.description: Beach hotels at Lome and a few good places at Kpalime.
togo/luxury.alt: a beach hotel terrace under palms near Lome, Togo

togo/mountains.caption: Mont Agou
togo/mountains.description: 986 metres, the highest point, walkable in a morning from Kpalime.
togo/mountains.alt: the forested cone of Mont Agou above villages and farms, Togo

togo/nature.caption: The Kloto Hills
togo/nature.description: Coffee and cocoa country in the southwest, forested and cool, around Kpalime.
togo/nature.alt: forested hills and a valley of cocoa near Kpalime, Togo

togo/outdoor.caption: Mont Agou at Dawn
togo/outdoor.description: Up before six, and Ghana visible across the valley by seven.
togo/outdoor.alt: the view from Mont Agou across valleys at first light, Togo

togo/photography.caption: Earth Architecture
togo/photography.description: Koutammakou late in the day, when the mud goes gold and the granaries throw shadows.
togo/photography.alt: late sun on the sculpted walls of takienta houses, Togo

togo/safari.caption: Small and Recovering
togo/safari.description: The parks here are being rebuilt after decades of pressure, and the wildlife with them.
togo/safari.alt: a waterhole and buffalo tracks in a Togolese reserve

togo/traditional-people.caption: The Batammariba
togo/traditional-people.description: Their name means 'those who shape the earth', and the houses are the argument.
togo/traditional-people.alt: a Batammariba woman on the roof terrace of a takienta house, Togo

togo/waterfalls.caption: Kpime and Womé
togo/waterfalls.description: Two falls in the Kloto hills, both of them a short walk off the Kpalime road.
togo/waterfalls.alt: the Womé waterfall falling into a pool in forest near Kpalime, Togo

togo/why-visit.caption: Why Togo
togo/why-visit.description: A whole cross-section of West Africa in a country you can drive in a day.
togo/why-visit.alt: a road running north through changing country in Togo

togo/wildlife.caption: Fazao-Malfakassa
togo/wildlife.description: Elephant, buffalo and a great many butterflies in the largest park in the country.
togo/wildlife.alt: forest and grassland in Fazao-Malfakassa National Park, Togo

tunisia/adventure.caption: Desert, Diving, Dunes
tunisia/adventure.description: Camel treks from Douz, dune camps on the erg, and diving off Tabarka.
tunisia/adventure.alt: camels crossing dunes on the Grand Erg oriental, Tunisia

tunisia/architecture.caption: Whitewash and Blue
tunisia/architecture.description: Sidi Bou Said's blue and white, and the vaulted ksour of the desert south.
tunisia/architecture.alt: the blue doors and white walls of Sidi Bou Said, Tunisia

tunisia/beaches.caption: The Mediterranean
tunisia/beaches.description: Hammamet, Djerba and Cap Bon — twelve hundred kilometres of it, and warm from May.
tunisia/beaches.alt: the whitewashed seafront at Sidi Bou Said, Tunisia

tunisia/cities.caption: Tunis and Sfax
tunisia/cities.description: Tunis at the head of its lake, and Sfax's walled medina working as a medina still.
tunisia/cities.alt: the medina rooftops of Tunis at dusk, Tunisia

tunisia/crafts.caption: Mosaic, Ceramic and Silver
tunisia/crafts.description: Roman mosaic technique still taught, Nabeul ceramic, and Berber silver from the south.
tunisia/crafts.alt: hand-painted Nabeul ceramics on a market stall, Tunisia

tunisia/culture.caption: Punic, Roman, Arab, Berber
tunisia/culture.description: Four layers, all of them still visible, and often in the same town.
tunisia/culture.alt: a Roman mosaic floor in a Tunisian museum

tunisia/eco-tourism.caption: Oasis Water
tunisia/eco-tourism.description: The oasis irrigation of Tozeur and Nefta, managing water in the driest place in the country.
tunisia/eco-tourism.alt: traditional irrigation channels in the Tozeur oasis, Tunisia

tunisia/family-community.caption: Two Hours from Europe
tunisia/family-community.description: Short flights, shallow warm sea, and resorts that have been doing families for decades.
tunisia/family-community.alt: a shallow beach with families on the Tunisian coast

tunisia/festivals.caption: Carthage and the Sahara Festival
tunisia/festivals.description: The Carthage film and music festival in summer, and the Douz Sahara festival in December.
tunisia/festivals.alt: riders at the Sahara festival at Douz, Tunisia

tunisia/food.caption: Couscous, Brik and Harissa
tunisia/food.description: Friday couscous, brik straight out of the pan, and harissa on everything.
tunisia/food.alt: a brik being fried at a Tunisian market stall

tunisia/forests.caption: Cork Oak in the North
tunisia/forests.description: The Kroumirie forest of cork oak in the north-west, which surprises everyone.
tunisia/forests.alt: cork oak forest in the Kroumirie hills, Tunisia

tunisia/heritage.caption: The Medinas
tunisia/heritage.description: Tunis, Sousse and Kairouan — Kairouan's mosque is among the oldest in the Maghreb.
tunisia/heritage.alt: the great mosque of Kairouan from its courtyard, Tunisia

tunisia/hero.caption: Carthage, the Sahel and the Desert
tunisia/hero.description: Mediterranean at the top, olive plains through the middle, and the Sahara at the bottom.
tunisia/hero.alt: the ruins of Carthage above the bay of Tunis, Tunisia

tunisia/hidden-gems.caption: Ksar Ouled Soltane
tunisia/hidden-gems.description: Vaulted grain stores stacked four storeys high, and almost nobody there.
tunisia/hidden-gems.alt: the stacked vaulted ksar at Ksar Ouled Soltane, Tunisia

tunisia/historic-sites.caption: Carthage, Dougga, El Jem
tunisia/historic-sites.description: El Jem's amphitheatre seats thirty-five thousand and is standing almost complete.
tunisia/historic-sites.alt: the Roman amphitheatre at El Jem, Tunisia

tunisia/lakes-rivers.caption: The Medjerda
tunisia/lakes-rivers.description: The only permanent river, running out of Algeria and across the northern plain.
tunisia/lakes-rivers.alt: the Medjerda river crossing the northern plain, Tunisia

tunisia/local-life.caption: The Souk and the Café
tunisia/local-life.description: Mint tea with pine nuts, and a souk that still mostly sells to the people who live there.
tunisia/local-life.alt: mint tea with pine nuts at a Tunisian café

tunisia/luxury.caption: Riad, Dar and Dune Camp
tunisia/luxury.description: Restored dar houses in the medinas, and desert camps beyond the last palm.
tunisia/luxury.alt: the courtyard of a restored dar in the Tunis medina, Tunisia

tunisia/mountains.caption: The Dorsale
tunisia/mountains.description: The Atlas tail crosses the north — Jebel Chambi is 1,544 metres and the highest point.
tunisia/mountains.alt: the ridge of the Tunisian Dorsale in winter light

tunisia/nature.caption: Coast to Chott
tunisia/nature.description: The Cap Bon coast, the olive Sahel, and the salt flats of the Chott el Djerid.
tunisia/nature.alt: the salt crust of the Chott el Djerid, Tunisia

tunisia/outdoor.caption: Desert and Dive
tunisia/outdoor.description: Dune trekking from Douz, quad routes on the chott, and diving at Tabarka.
tunisia/outdoor.alt: a trekking party on the edge of the Grand Erg, Tunisia

tunisia/photography.caption: Light on White
tunisia/photography.description: Whitewash, blue, and desert light — the reason the film crews keep coming back.
tunisia/photography.alt: white and blue architecture in strong Mediterranean light, Tunisia

tunisia/safari.caption: Not a Safari Country
tunisia/safari.description: The wildlife here is birds and desert species, and Ichkeul is the reason to bring binoculars.
tunisia/safari.alt: waders feeding on a Tunisian coastal wetland

tunisia/traditional-people.caption: The Berber South
tunisia/traditional-people.description: The ksour of Tataouine, and the underground houses of Matmata.
tunisia/traditional-people.alt: an underground Berber courtyard house at Matmata, Tunisia

tunisia/waterfalls.caption: The Oasis Cascades
tunisia/waterfalls.description: Chebika, Tamerza and Mides — the mountain oases of the west, with water in a dry country.
tunisia/waterfalls.alt: the palm oasis and waterfall at Chebika, Tunisia

tunisia/why-visit.caption: Rome, and the Sahara, in One Week
tunisia/why-visit.description: An amphitheatre on Monday and a dune camp on Thursday, in a country the size of England.
tunisia/why-visit.alt: a desert road running south towards the Sahara, Tunisia

tunisia/wildlife.caption: Ichkeul and the Desert
tunisia/wildlife.description: Ichkeul's wintering waterfowl, and the desert fox and gazelle of the south.
tunisia/wildlife.alt: flamingos on the lake at Ichkeul, Tunisia

uganda/adventure.caption: Grade Five on the Nile
uganda/adventure.description: White-water rafting below the source at Jinja, plus bungee, kayaking and the long walk up Sipi.
uganda/adventure.alt: white-water rafting on the Nile rapids at Jinja, Uganda

uganda/architecture.caption: Minaret, Dome and Thatch
uganda/architecture.description: The Uganda National Mosque, the Namirembe and Rubaga cathedrals facing each other across two hills.
uganda/architecture.alt: the minaret of the Uganda National Mosque above Kampala

uganda/beaches.caption: The Ssese Islands
uganda/beaches.description: Freshwater beaches and fishing villages on Lake Victoria, an hour and a half by ferry from Entebbe.
uganda/beaches.alt: a sandy freshwater shore and fishing boats on the Ssese Islands, Uganda

uganda/cities.caption: Kampala on Seven Hills
uganda/cities.description: A capital built across hills and traffic, with the Gaddafi Mosque minaret giving the best view of all of it.
uganda/cities.alt: the hills and rooftops of Kampala seen from the Gaddafi Mosque minaret, Uganda

uganda/crafts.caption: Bark Cloth and Basketry
uganda/crafts.description: Bark cloth from the mutuba fig, made in Buganda for six hundred years and now UNESCO-listed.
uganda/crafts.alt: a craftsman beating bark cloth from a mutuba fig tree, Uganda

uganda/culture.caption: The Kingdom of Buganda
uganda/culture.description: Uganda's kingdoms were never abolished for long — Buganda, Bunyoro and Toro still hold court.
uganda/culture.alt: a Buganda kingdom drummer in ceremonial bark cloth

uganda/eco-tourism.caption: The Gorilla Permit
uganda/eco-tourism.description: Permit revenue funds the park and pays a share to the parishes around it — which is why the gorilla numbers are rising.
uganda/eco-tourism.alt: rangers and trackers setting out on a gorilla trek in Bwindi, Uganda

uganda/family-community.caption: Villages at the Forest Edge
uganda/family-community.description: Community walks in Buhoma and Nkuringo, run by the villages that share the forest with the gorillas.
uganda/family-community.alt: a community village walk beside the forest edge at Buhoma, Uganda

uganda/festivals.caption: Imbalu and Nyege Nyege
uganda/festivals.description: The Bagisu Imbalu season in the east, and four days of music on the banks of the Nile at Jinja.
uganda/festivals.alt: drummers and dancers at the Imbalu ceremony in eastern Uganda

uganda/food.caption: Rolex, Matoke, Luwombo
uganda/food.description: Steamed green banana with groundnut sauce, chicken cooked in banana leaf, and an egg rolled in a chapati on every corner.
uganda/food.alt: a street vendor cooking rolex chapati and eggs in Kampala, Uganda

uganda/forests.caption: Kibale and Bwindi
uganda/forests.description: Thirteen primate species in Kibale, and in Bwindi a forest so old and so thick it was never logged.
uganda/forests.alt: dense canopy and buttressed trees in Kibale Forest, Uganda

uganda/heritage.caption: Kingdoms Still Standing
uganda/heritage.description: Royal drums, regalia and clan structures that survived the protectorate, the 1966 crisis and the 1970s.
uganda/heritage.alt: royal regalia and drums inside a Buganda kingdom palace

uganda/hero.caption: The Pearl of Africa
uganda/hero.description: Gorilla forest, the Mountains of the Moon and the Nile leaving Lake Victoria — all inside one small, green country.
uganda/hero.alt: mist over the forested hills of Bwindi Impenetrable National Park at sunrise, Uganda

uganda/hidden-gems.caption: Kidepo Valley
uganda/hidden-gems.description: The furthest park from Kampala and the emptiest: Narus valley, the Morungole range, and cheetah nobody photographs.
uganda/hidden-gems.alt: the Narus valley and mountains of Kidepo Valley National Park, Uganda

uganda/historic-sites.caption: The Kasubi Tombs
uganda/historic-sites.description: The burial ground of four Buganda kings, thatched, enormous and rebuilt by the clans who have always maintained it.
uganda/historic-sites.alt: the great thatched dome of the Kasubi Tombs in Kampala, Uganda

uganda/lakes-rivers.caption: Where the Nile Begins
uganda/lakes-rivers.description: The Nile leaves Lake Victoria at Jinja; Lake Bunyonyi holds twenty-nine islands and no bilharzia.
uganda/lakes-rivers.alt: the islands and terraced shores of Lake Bunyonyi, Uganda

uganda/local-life.caption: Boda Bodas and Owino
uganda/local-life.description: The boda boda is the transport system; Owino market is where the whole city goes to buy everything.
uganda/local-life.alt: boda boda motorcycle taxis waiting at a busy Kampala street stage, Uganda

uganda/luxury.caption: Lodges at the Forest Edge
uganda/luxury.description: Small lodges on the Bwindi ridge and the Kazinga Channel, close enough to walk to the trailhead after breakfast.
uganda/luxury.alt: a lodge terrace overlooking the Bwindi forest ridge at dawn, Uganda

uganda/mountains.caption: The Mountains of the Moon
uganda/mountains.description: The Rwenzori range holds glaciers three degrees from the equator, and Margherita Peak at 5,109 m.
uganda/mountains.alt: the glaciated peaks of the Rwenzori Mountains above the moorland, Uganda

uganda/nature.caption: Green, End to End
uganda/nature.description: Crater lakes around Fort Portal, papyrus swamp on the Nile, and the Rwenzori snowline sitting on the equator.
uganda/nature.alt: the crater lakes and green hills around Fort Portal, Uganda

uganda/outdoor.caption: Sipi, Elgon, Bisoke
uganda/outdoor.description: Three waterfalls and a coffee walk at Sipi, then the long crater rim of Mount Elgon above it.
uganda/outdoor.alt: the Sipi Falls dropping off the Mount Elgon escarpment, Uganda

uganda/photography.caption: Crater Lakes at First Light
uganda/photography.description: The Ndali-Kasenda crater field before the haze lifts, and the Ishasha fig trees in the late afternoon.
uganda/photography.alt: morning mist on the Ndali-Kasenda crater lakes near Fort Portal, Uganda

uganda/safari.caption: Queen Elizabeth and Kidepo
uganda/safari.description: Kob on the Kasenyi plains, elephant on the Kazinga Channel, and Kidepo Valley with almost nobody in it.
uganda/safari.alt: elephants on the Kazinga Channel in Queen Elizabeth National Park, Uganda

uganda/traditional-people.caption: Batwa and Karamojong
uganda/traditional-people.description: The Batwa, forest people of the southwest, and the Karamojong cattle-keepers of the northeast plains.
uganda/traditional-people.alt: a Karamojong herder with cattle on the plains of Karamoja, Uganda

uganda/waterfalls.caption: Murchison, Through the Gap
uganda/waterfalls.description: The entire Victoria Nile forced through a seven-metre gap and dropped forty-three metres into the gorge below.
uganda/waterfalls.alt: the Nile forcing through the narrow gap at Murchison Falls, Uganda

uganda/why-visit.caption: Half the World's Gorillas
uganda/why-visit.description: Nowhere else puts gorillas, chimpanzees, the Big Five, a snowline and the Nile within one week of driving.
uganda/why-visit.alt: a silverback mountain gorilla resting in the Bwindi undergrowth, Uganda

uganda/wildlife.caption: Wildlife Encounters
uganda/wildlife.description: Mountain gorillas in Bwindi, chimpanzees in Kibale, and tree-climbing lions in the Ishasha sector.
uganda/wildlife.alt: a mountain gorilla in the Bwindi Impenetrable Forest, Uganda

zambia/adventure.caption: Devil's Pool and the Gorge
zambia/adventure.description: Swim to the lip of Victoria Falls in low water, then raft the grade five rapids in the Batoka gorge below it.
zambia/adventure.alt: rafting the grade five rapids in the Batoka gorge below Victoria Falls, Zambia

zambia/architecture.caption: Livingstone's Verandas
zambia/architecture.description: Corrugated iron and deep colonial verandas along Mosi-oa-Tunya Road, built for heat and never modernised.
zambia/architecture.alt: a colonial veranda building on Mosi-oa-Tunya Road in Livingstone, Zambia

zambia/beaches.caption: Lake Tanganyika Shore
zambia/beaches.description: Clear freshwater, sand and forested hills at Nsumbu, about as far from anywhere as Zambia gets.
zambia/beaches.alt: the clear freshwater shore of Lake Tanganyika at Nsumbu, Zambia

zambia/cities.caption: Lusaka
zambia/cities.description: The centre of everything: Kabwata market, the Great East Road, and the flights that get you to the parks.
zambia/cities.alt: a busy market street in Lusaka, Zambia

zambia/crafts.caption: Basketry and Copper
zambia/crafts.description: Tight coiled baskets from the Western Province, and copper worked on the belt that built the economy.
zambia/crafts.alt: coiled baskets woven in Zambia's Western Province

zambia/culture.caption: Lozi, Bemba, Tonga
zambia/culture.description: Seventy-three ethnic groups, seven official languages, and a royal barge ceremony older than the country.
zambia/culture.alt: Lozi paddlers and drummers on the Zambezi floodplain, Zambia

zambia/eco-tourism.caption: Kafue and the Carnivores
zambia/eco-tourism.description: Kafue is the size of Wales; the conservation programmes there fund anti-poaching across the whole Greater Kafue system.
zambia/eco-tourism.alt: wild dogs on the Busanga plains in Kafue National Park, Zambia

zambia/family-community.caption: Village Around the Park
zambia/family-community.description: Community campsites and craft cooperatives on the Luangwa boundary, funded by the same beds that fill the lodges.
zambia/family-community.alt: a community craft cooperative near the South Luangwa park boundary, Zambia

zambia/festivals.caption: Kuomboka
zambia/festivals.description: When the floodplain fills, the Litunga is paddled to high ground on the Nalikwanda barge, drummed the whole way.
zambia/festivals.alt: the Nalikwanda royal barge during the Kuomboka ceremony, Zambia

zambia/food.caption: Nshima and Kapenta
zambia/food.description: Maize nshima with relish, dried kapenta from the lakes, and fresh bream out of the Zambezi.
zambia/food.alt: nshima with relish served at a Zambian table

zambia/forests.caption: Miombo and Winterthorn
zambia/forests.description: Miombo woodland turning red at the start of the rains, and the winterthorn groves the elephants feed under.
zambia/forests.alt: elephants under winterthorn trees in the Lower Zambezi, Zambia

zambia/heritage.caption: Mosi-oa-Tunya, UNESCO
zambia/heritage.description: World Heritage since 1989, shared with Zimbabwe, and named by the Kololo long before anyone renamed it.
zambia/heritage.alt: the knife-edge bridge and gorge at Mosi-oa-Tunya, Victoria Falls, Zambia

zambia/hero.caption: The Smoke That Thunders
zambia/hero.description: Mosi-oa-Tunya: a kilometre and a half of the Zambezi falling into a basalt gorge, and spray you can see from thirty kilometres away.
zambia/hero.alt: Victoria Falls in full flood with spray rising from the gorge, Zambia

zambia/hidden-gems.caption: Liuwa Plain
zambia/hidden-gems.description: The second largest wildebeest migration in Africa, on a plain almost nobody has heard of, reachable only in the dry.
zambia/hidden-gems.alt: wildebeest massed on the open grass of Liuwa Plain, Zambia

zambia/historic-sites.caption: Livingstone
zambia/historic-sites.description: The old colonial capital above the falls, its museum, and the tree where the man himself is said to have camped.
zambia/historic-sites.alt: the colonial-era museum building in Livingstone, Zambia

zambia/lakes-rivers.caption: Zambezi, Kafue, Tanganyika
zambia/lakes-rivers.description: Three great river systems and the southern tip of Lake Tanganyika, the second deepest lake on earth.
zambia/lakes-rivers.alt: sunset over the Zambezi river with hippo in the shallows, Zambia

zambia/local-life.caption: Markets and the Great North Road
zambia/local-life.description: Roadside charcoal and tomatoes, long-haul trucks to the copperbelt, and a bus that leaves when it fills.
zambia/local-life.alt: a roadside produce market on the Great North Road in Zambia

zambia/luxury.caption: Bush Camps, Six Beds
zambia/luxury.description: Seasonal bush camps in the Luangwa that take six guests, close at the rains, and are walked between.
zambia/luxury.alt: a small thatched bush camp overlooking the Luangwa river, Zambia

zambia/mountains.caption: The Nyika Plateau
zambia/mountains.description: Two thousand metres of rolling montane grassland on the Malawi border, with roan antelope and no heat.
zambia/mountains.alt: rolling montane grassland on the Nyika plateau, Zambia

zambia/nature.caption: The Zambezi Valley
zambia/nature.description: Escarpment, floodplain and winterthorn forest, with the river braiding through the middle of all of it.
zambia/nature.alt: the Zambezi river and escarpment in the Lower Zambezi valley, Zambia

zambia/outdoor.caption: Canoeing the Lower Zambezi
zambia/outdoor.description: Three days downstream past hippo pods and elephant crossings, camping on islands, no engine at any point.
zambia/outdoor.alt: canoeing past elephants on the Lower Zambezi river, Zambia

zambia/photography.caption: Luangwa at Last Light
zambia/photography.description: The river bends, the hippo surface and the dust goes gold about forty minutes before the drive has to end.
zambia/photography.alt: hippos in the Luangwa river at last light, Zambia

zambia/safari.caption: The Walking Safari
zambia/safari.description: Invented in the Luangwa in the 1950s: no vehicle, an armed scout, and everything at eye level.
zambia/safari.alt: a walking safari group and guide in the South Luangwa bush, Zambia

zambia/traditional-people.caption: The Barotse Floodplain
zambia/traditional-people.description: The Lozi live with the flood — moving cattle, homes and the king himself when the Zambezi rises.
zambia/traditional-people.alt: a Lozi fisherman poling a dugout on the Barotse floodplain, Zambia

zambia/waterfalls.caption: Victoria and Kalambo
zambia/waterfalls.description: Victoria Falls needs no introduction; Kalambo, on the Tanzanian border, drops 235 metres in a single uninterrupted fall.
zambia/waterfalls.alt: the single 235 metre drop of Kalambo Falls, Zambia

zambia/why-visit.caption: Wilderness, Still Unmanaged
zambia/why-visit.description: Zambia kept the walking safari, the small camp and the empty park while its neighbours scaled up.
zambia/why-visit.alt: a lone safari vehicle on an empty track in the South Luangwa, Zambia

zambia/wildlife.caption: Leopard Country
zambia/wildlife.description: The South Luangwa has one of the densest leopard populations in Africa, and the best chance of seeing one hunting.
zambia/wildlife.alt: a leopard in a sausage tree in the South Luangwa valley, Zambia

zimbabwe/adventure.caption: Walking, Canoeing, Rafting
zimbabwe/adventure.description: Canoe the Zambezi past hippo, raft the gorge below the falls, and walk Mana with a guide.
zimbabwe/adventure.alt: canoes on the Zambezi below Mana Pools, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/architecture.caption: Dry Stone
zimbabwe/architecture.description: Great Zimbabwe's coursed granite is the architecture, and nothing since has matched it.
zimbabwe/architecture.alt: coursed dry stone walling at Great Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/beaches.caption: Landlocked
zimbabwe/beaches.description: No coast — the water here is the Zambezi, Kariba, and the pools of the Mana floodplain.
zimbabwe/beaches.alt: the Zambezi river wide and slow above the falls, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/cities.caption: Harare and Bulawayo
zimbabwe/cities.description: Harare on the highveld, and Bulawayo's wide colonial grid built for turning an ox wagon.
zimbabwe/cities.alt: the wide colonial streets of Bulawayo, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/crafts.caption: Stone, Basket and Wire
zimbabwe/crafts.description: Serpentine carving, Binga basketry, and wire sculpture sold on every roadside.
zimbabwe/crafts.alt: woven Binga baskets from the Zambezi valley, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/culture.caption: Shona and Ndebele
zimbabwe/culture.description: Shona across the centre and east, Ndebele in the west, and stone sculpture from both.
zimbabwe/culture.alt: a Shona stone sculptor at work, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/eco-tourism.caption: CAMPFIRE
zimbabwe/eco-tourism.description: The community wildlife programme that much of the region's conservation policy was built on.
zimbabwe/eco-tourism.alt: a community conservation meeting beside a wildlife area, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/family-community.caption: Falls and Elephant
zimbabwe/family-community.description: Victoria Falls, a steam train, and elephant at a waterhole — a good week for children.
zimbabwe/family-community.alt: a family watching elephants from a Hwange hide, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/festivals.caption: HIFA and the Harvest
zimbabwe/festivals.description: The Harare arts festival, and the harvest ceremonies that still open the season.
zimbabwe/festivals.alt: a performance at an arts festival in Harare, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/food.caption: Sadza and Braai
zimbabwe/food.description: Sadza with relish, and meat over coals wherever there is a fire and company.
zimbabwe/food.alt: sadza and relish served at a Zimbabwean table

zimbabwe/forests.caption: Msasa and Miombo
zimbabwe/forests.description: Miombo woodland across the country, and msasa that comes into red leaf in September.
zimbabwe/forests.alt: msasa trees in red new leaf in September, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/heritage.caption: Khami and Matobo
zimbabwe/heritage.description: Khami's terraces, and the Matobo hills where Mzilikazi and Rhodes are both buried.
zimbabwe/heritage.alt: balancing rocks and rock art in the Matobo hills, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/hero.caption: Great Zimbabwe and the Zambezi
zimbabwe/hero.description: A stone city built without mortar, and the largest sheet of falling water on earth.
zimbabwe/hero.alt: the stone walls of Great Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/hidden-gems.caption: Chimanimani
zimbabwe/hidden-gems.description: A mountain range on the Mozambique border that you walk into and camp in.
zimbabwe/hidden-gems.alt: the Chimanimani mountains on the Mozambique border, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/historic-sites.caption: Great Zimbabwe
zimbabwe/historic-sites.description: Eight hundred years old, mortarless, and the largest stone structure south of the Sahara.
zimbabwe/historic-sites.alt: the conical tower inside the Great Enclosure, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/lakes-rivers.caption: The Zambezi and Kariba
zimbabwe/lakes-rivers.description: The Zambezi above the falls, and Kariba's drowned forest downstream of them.
zimbabwe/lakes-rivers.alt: dead trees standing in Lake Kariba at sunset, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/local-life.caption: Kombis and Musika
zimbabwe/local-life.description: The country runs on kombis and market days, both of which are worth an afternoon.
zimbabwe/local-life.alt: a busy produce market in a Zimbabwean town

zimbabwe/luxury.caption: The Old Safari Standard
zimbabwe/luxury.description: Small owner-run camps in Mana and Hwange, run by guides with the country's toughest licence.
zimbabwe/luxury.alt: a tented camp on the Zambezi floodplain at dusk, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/mountains.caption: The Eastern Highlands
zimbabwe/mountains.description: Nyanga, Vumba and Chimanimani along the Mozambique border, up to 2,592 metres.
zimbabwe/mountains.alt: the green Eastern Highlands at Nyanga, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/nature.caption: Highveld and Escarpment
zimbabwe/nature.description: Granite kopjes across the highveld, and the Zambezi escarpment dropping into the valley.
zimbabwe/nature.alt: balancing granite boulders on the Zimbabwean highveld

zimbabwe/outdoor.caption: Raft, Canoe, Walk
zimbabwe/outdoor.description: Grade five rafting below the falls, multi-day canoe trails, and walking safaris in Mana.
zimbabwe/outdoor.alt: rafts in the Batoka gorge below Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/photography.caption: Albida Light
zimbabwe/photography.description: The winterthorn cathedrals of Mana Pools, in dust and low sun, are photographed everywhere.
zimbabwe/photography.alt: dust and low sun through winterthorn trees at Mana Pools, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/safari.caption: Mana Pools on Foot
zimbabwe/safari.description: The park where you may walk unguided, and where the elephant stand on their hind legs.
zimbabwe/safari.alt: an elephant reaching into an albida tree at Mana Pools, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/traditional-people.caption: The Stone Sculptors
zimbabwe/traditional-people.description: Zimbabwean stone sculpture is the country's clearest contemporary export.
zimbabwe/traditional-people.alt: finished stone sculptures in a Zimbabwean workshop

zimbabwe/waterfalls.caption: Victoria Falls
zimbabwe/waterfalls.description: Mosi-oa-Tunya — a mile and a half wide, and a hundred metres down, in full flood.
zimbabwe/waterfalls.alt: Victoria Falls in full flood with spray rising, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/why-visit.caption: Guides, and Great Ruins
zimbabwe/why-visit.description: The hardest guiding exam in Africa, and a stone city most visitors have never heard of.
zimbabwe/why-visit.alt: a professional guide leading walkers through Mana Pools, Zimbabwe

zimbabwe/wildlife.caption: Hwange's Elephant
zimbabwe/wildlife.description: Forty thousand elephant in Hwange, drinking at pumped pans through the dry season.
zimbabwe/wildlife.alt: elephants crowding a pumped waterhole in Hwange, Zimbabwe
